Instruction Rich Text:
1. Sanitize: Pour hot water into a 750 ml mason jar, let sit for 1–2 minutes, then drain and let cool.
  2. Soak (Day 1): Add 20 g (2 tbsp) alfalfa seeds to the jar. Cover with filtered water and close the mesh lid. Soak for 5 hours. Drain, rinse, and prop the jar upside down at an angle to drain fully.
  3. Rinse and Drain (Days 2–4+): Twice daily: fill the jar with filtered water, swirl gently, drain through the mesh lid, and re-prop upside down at an angle. Keep on a countertop away from direct sunlight.
  4. Harvest: By day 4 (up to day 7 depending on temperature), sprouts should fill the jar. Transfer to a container lined with a paper towel and refrigerate. Consume within 5 days.

Prep: Drain the seeds as thoroughly as possible after every rinse, tipping the jar upside down for a few minutes — any pooled water left sitting encourages mold instead of clean, crisp sprouts.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Mold — rinse and drain thoroughly twice daily. Incomplete draining is the main cause. Always prop the jar upside down at an angle so air circulates.

Notes: Always use seeds specifically labeled for sprouting — they are untreated and safe to eat raw. Regular garden or cooking seeds may be treated with fungicides. The same method works for broccoli, radish, clover, and fenugreek seeds — times vary slightly.

Storage: Store in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 5 days. Rinse before eating.

Tips: Keep the jar in a dark or low-light area during sprouting. Move to indirect light for the final 12 hours to green up the leaves and boost chlorophyll.
Why These Ingredients:
Alfalfa sprouting seeds are the only ingredient — they must be specifically labeled for sprouting. Regular seeds sold for planting may be treated with fungicides or other chemicals that are unsafe to consume raw. Sprouting seeds are tested and certified for human consumption without cooking. At just 20 g per batch, they expand to fill a full quart jar.

Filtered water is recommended over tap water where possible. Chlorine in tap water can inhibit germination and slow sprouting. If filtered water isn’t available, leaving tap water in an open container for a few hours allows the chlorine to dissipate.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Make the Dough: Whisk together 113 g (½ cup) melted vegan butter, 150 g (¾ cup) cane sugar, 120 g (½ cup) applesauce, and 4 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract. In a separate bowl, whisk together 210 g (1¾ cups) all-purpose flour, 56 g (½ cup) almond flour, and 6 g (1½ tsp) baking powder. Add dry to wet and mix until just combined. Fold in orange zest (if using) and 105 g (¾ cup) chopped almonds.
  3. First Bake: Shape into two logs about 25 cm (10 inches) long. Bake for 25 minutes until golden and set but still slightly soft.
  4. Cool and Slice: Cool for at least 5 minutes, then slice diagonally into 2 cm (¾ inch) pieces.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Blend: Add 260 g (2 cups) raw almonds to a food processor. Process continuously, stopping to scrape down the sides every 1–2 minutes, for 10–15 minutes total until completely smooth and creamy. The almonds will go from flour to clumps to a thick paste to silky butter.
  2. Season: Add a pinch of salt and 1–2 tbsp neutral oil (optional) for a smoother texture. Blend for 30 more seconds.

Common Mistakes: Don’t stop blending too early — the almonds must go all the way from crumbs to paste to silky butter. Stopping at the clumping stage results in a gritty, thick spread rather than true butter. Any moisture in the almonds will cause the butter to seize — make sure they are completely dry.
Notes: Roasting the almonds first is strongly recommended — it releases the oils, shortens blending time significantly, and deepens the flavor. Roast at 175°C (350°F) for 10–12 minutes, let cool, then blend.
Oil Separation: The oil will separate and float to the top over time — this is completely normal. Stir before use. Refrigerating slows separation.

Neutral oil (optional) speeds up the blending process and produces a silkier, more pourable butter. Almond oil reinforces the flavor; avocado oil is neutral. Never add water — it will cause the butter to seize into a stiff, grainy paste.

Salt (optional) amplifies all the other flavors. Even a tiny pinch added at the end elevates the overall taste significantly. Use fine sea salt rather than coarse for even distribution.

Vanilla extract (optional) adds warmth and a subtle sweetness that makes the butter taste like a premium artisan product.

Maple syrup (optional) adds natural sweetness without refined sugar. Add in small amounts — too much liquid can cause the texture to tighten slightly.

Flax egg is the binder. Mixed with water it forms a gel that holds the pulp together in the absence of eggs. Without it the cookies won’t hold their shape after baking.

Chopped nuts or seeds add crunch and texture that contrasts with the soft, dense almond pulp base. Walnuts and pecans are the richest choices; pumpkin seeds keep it nut-free.

Vegan chocolate chips are the flavor anchor — their richness balances the mild, slightly bland almond pulp. Use a good quality 60%+ dark chocolate chip for the best result.

Cinnamon adds warmth that enhances both the almond and chocolate flavors. It’s a small amount but makes a noticeable difference to the overall flavor profile.

Vanilla extract rounds out the sweetness and adds a familiar cookie aroma that makes these taste like a proper baked treat despite the unconventional base.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Activate the Yeast: In a large mixing bowl, combine 300 ml (1¼ cups) warm water at 40°C (105°F) with 1 tbsp maple syrup. Sprinkle in 7 g (2¼ tsp) active dry yeast and let sit for 5–10 minutes until foamy.
  2. Make the Dough: Add 440 g (3½ cups) bread flour and 1½ tsp salt. Stir to combine, then knead by hand or with a dough hook for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  3. First Rise: Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 60–90 minutes until doubled in size.
  4. Shape: Punch down dough and divide into 8 equal pieces (~90 g each). Roll each into a ball, poke a hole through the center with your thumb, and gently stretch into a ring about 8 cm (3 in) wide.
  5. Second Rise: Place bagels on parchment-lined baking sheets, cover loosely, and rest for 20–30 minutes.
  6. Boil: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Bring 2 liters (8 cups) water to a boil in a large pot; stir in 2 tbsp maple syrup. Boil bagels in batches of 2–3, 1 minute per side, then return to the baking sheet.
  7. Top and Bake: While still moist, sprinkle each bagel with 2 tbsp everything bagel seasoning (total, divided). Bake for 25 minutes until deep golden brown.
  8. Cool: Transfer to a wire cooling rack and cool for at least 10 minutes before slicing.

Notes: Bread flour gives the chewiest bagels — all-purpose works but produces a softer result. The maple syrup in the boil water gives the bagels a subtle shine and slight sweetness.

Prep in Advance: Make the dough the night before and let it rise overnight in the refrigerator (covered). Shape, rest, and boil the next morning.

Maple syrup (dough) — activates the yeast and adds a very subtle sweetness without refined sugar.

Maple syrup (boiling water) — creates a glossy, slightly caramelized crust during boiling — the step that makes a bagel a bagel.

Salt — controls yeast activity and strengthens the gluten structure for a better chew.

Everything bagel seasoning — the iconic blend of sesame seeds, poppy seeds, dried garlic, dried onion, and flaky salt that gives the crust its signature flavor and crunch.

  5. Bake: Pour batter into the prepared pan and spread evenly. Bake for 25–30 minutes until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.

On a large baking sheet, toss 1 small head cauliflower florets and 1 can (425 g / 15 oz) drained chickpeas with 1½ tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 2 tbsp nutritional yeast, and salt and pepper. • 300 g (1 medium) cucumber
  • 240 ml (1 cup) water
  • 240 ml (1 cup) distilled white vinegar
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup
  • 2–3 garlic cloves
  • 5 g (1 tsp) mustard seeds
  • 2 g (1 tsp) black peppercorns
  • 12 g (2 tsp) salt
  • 2–4 fresh dill sprigs
Equipment:
• Small saucepan

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the Cucumber: Wash and slice 1 medium cucumber into rounds or spears. Pack tightly into a clean glass jar.
  2. Make the Brine: In a small saucepan, combine 240 ml (1 cup) water, 240 ml (1 cup) distilled white vinegar, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 2 tsp salt, 2–3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp mustard seeds, and 1 tsp black peppercorns. Bring to a simmer, stirring until salt dissolves, about 2–3 minutes.
  3. Pour and Add Dill: Pour the hot brine over the cucumbers. Tuck in 2–4 fresh dill sprigs.
  4. Cool and Refrigerate: Let cool to room temperature, then seal with a lid and refrigerate.
  5. Wait: Let pickle for at least 24 hours before eating. Best after 48 hours. Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 weeks.

  • non-chlorinated water (enough to fully cover beans)

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Pack the Jar: Trim green beans and pack them tightly into a clean glass jar, standing upright. Add optional flavorings (garlic, chili flakes, dill, peppercorns, mustard seeds).
  2. Make the Brine: Weigh the jar contents. Multiply the total weight by 0.03 for a 3% brine (recommended). Dissolve that amount of salt in water.
  3. Add the Brine: Pour the salt brine over the beans until fully submerged. Leave about 2.5 cm (1 inch) of headspace at the top.
  4. Submerge the Beans: Place a fermentation weight on top to keep the beans below the brine at all times.
  5. Cover and Ferment: Use an airlock lid (best) or a regular lid loosely fitted. Keep at room temperature (18–24°C / 65–75°F). Taste from day 5. Continue fermenting for 5–14 days until tangy and crisp to your liking.
  6. Refrigerate: Once ready, seal the jar tightly and refrigerate.

Name: How to Ferment Anything
Features: 20-minutes-or-less; gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free
Common Ingredients: salt
Ingredients:
• any fresh vegetable or firm fruit, washed
  • non-iodized salt (sea salt, kosher salt, or pickling salt)
  • clean, chlorine-free water (if making a brine)
Equipment:
• Large mixing bowl
  • Digital kitchen scale (grams preferred)
  • Fermentation weight or small clean jar
  • Fermentation jar or crock (1-quart / 1 L)
  • Airlock lid (preferred) or regular lid
  • Clean towel or tray (to catch overflow)
Instruction Rich Text:
What You're Doing

Salt creates a safe brine that prevents bad bacteria and helps good bacteria turn your vegetables sour and delicious.

Salt Strength Guide:

  • 2–2.5% salt = Mild, faster ferment
  • 3–5% salt = Stronger, slower, crunchier (best for warm weather)

1. Prep Your Vegetables

  • Wash thoroughly (no soap)
  • Remove any damaged spots
  • Cut as desired:
    • Shred for sauerkraut
    • Slice for quick ferments
    • Keep whole for pickles

2. Weigh Everything

  • Place empty bowl on scale and zero it out
  • Add all vegetables
  • Add any water you're using
  • Write down the total weight

Example: 900g vegetables + 300g water = 1,200g total

3. Calculate Your Salt

Multiply total weight by your chosen percentage:

  • 2% salt: 1,200 g × 0.02 = 24 g salt
  • 3% salt: 1,200 g × 0.03 = 36 g salt ← recommended
  • 5% salt: 1,200 g × 0.05 = 60 g salt

4. Mix in the Salt

  • Sprinkle measured salt over vegetables
  • Mix thoroughly with clean hands

For shredded vegetables: Massage 2–5 minutes until liquid releases
For whole vegetables: Dissolve salt in the water to make brine

5. Pack Your Jar

  • Transfer everything into jar
  • Press down firmly to remove air bubbles
  • Make sure vegetables are completely covered in liquid
  • Leave 1 inch of space at the top

6. Keep It Submerged

  • Place a weight on top to hold vegetables under brine
  • Cover with airlock lid (best) or regular lid loosened slightly

7. Ferment & Wait

  • Keep at room temperature (65–72°F)
  • Away from direct sunlight

Timeline:

  • Days 1–3: Bubbles appear
  • Days 5–7: Taste it! Should be tangy
  • Weeks 2–4: Gets more sour

Taste after 5–7 days and keep going until you like the flavor.

8. Refrigerate

When it tastes right:

  • Remove weight
  • Seal jar tightly
  • Store in fridge (lasts for months)

Safety Check

✅ Good Signs

  • Vegetables stay under brine
  • Sour, clean smell
  • Cloudy brine is normal
  • White film on top (kahm yeast) is harmless—just skim it off

❌ Bad Signs - Throw It Out

  • Fuzzy or colorful mold
  • Rotten smell
  • Slimy texture

Quick Reference

Simple Formula:

  1. Weigh vegetables + water
  2. Multiply by 0.03 (for 3% salt)
  3. Add that amount of salt
  4. Submerge and ferment 5–14 days
  5. Refrigerate when tasty

First time? Start with shredded cabbage at 2.5% salt for easy sauerkraut!

1. Preheat the Oven: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
  2. Prep the Pumpkin: Wash and dry the pumpkin. Cut in half from stem to base. Scoop out all seeds and stringy fibers with a spoon.
  3. Season: Brush the cut sides with 1 tbsp olive oil or melted butter. Sprinkle with ½ tsp cinnamon, ¼ tsp nutmeg, ¼ tsp ground ginger (optional), a pinch of salt, and 1 tbsp brown sugar or maple syrup (optional for extra sweetness).
  4. Roast: Place cut-side down on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Roast for 45–60 minutes until completely tender when pierced with a fork.
  5. Cool and Use: Allow to cool slightly, then scoop out the flesh. Blend or mash until smooth for use in recipes.

1. Remove the Top: Make a shallow circular incision around the crown of the pomegranate. Lift and pry it off like a lid to expose the seeds.

Notes: Choose a pomegranate that is heavy for its size and deeply colored — a sign of juicy, ripe seeds. The white membrane is completely edible but very bitter — remove as much as possible.

Storage: Store seeded arils in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days, or freeze in a single layer for up to 3 months.

Tips: Wear an apron — pomegranate juice stains permanently. The water method is messier to set up but keeps juice splashes contained, and is best for a large pomegranate. Use arils on oatmeal, salads, grain bowls, yogurt, or as a garnish for dips like muhammara or hummus.

1. Baking: Use ripe bananas in banana bread, muffins, pancakes, waffles, cookies, bars, brownies, or cakes. The riper the banana, the sweeter and more flavorful your baked goods will be.
  2. Frozen treats: Blend 2–3 frozen bananas alone for a 1-ingredient nice cream, or freeze as banana popsicles, smoothie packs, or banana sorbet.
  3. Smoothies: Add to smoothies with plant milk or yogurt — try peanut butter banana, tropical with mango and pineapple, or a classic banana milkshake.
  4. Breakfast: Mash into oatmeal or overnight oats, spread on toast as a natural jam alternative, blend into pancake batter, or use ½ ripe banana as a vegan egg substitute in baking.
  5. Snacks and desserts: Make banana pudding, chocolate-dipped banana bites (freeze for 1–2 hours after dipping), or classic banana splits.
  6. Savory uses: Add to curries to balance spice, use in West African or Caribbean dishes, or blend into sauces for a subtle natural sweetness.
Ingredient Data: [[null, null, "2–3 ripe bananas (about 200–300 g), the riper the better"]]
Prep: Wait until the bananas are heavily spotted with brown, or even mostly black, before using them in any of these ideas — the riper the banana, the sweeter and more flavorful the result, no matter which use you choose.

Notes: The riper the banana (more brown spots), the sweeter and more flavorful it is for baking and blending. Storage: Keep ripe bananas at room temperature and use within 1-3 days. Freeze peeled bananas in a zip-lock bag for up to 3 months — perfect for smoothies and nice cream.

Tips: Speed up ripening by placing bananas (unpeeled) in a 150°C (300°F) oven for 15-20 minutes until the skins are black. The flesh will be perfectly soft and sweet. Frozen bananas make the creamiest smoothies — no ice needed.

Name: How to Wrap a Sandwich
Features: raw; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free; 20-minutes-or-less; gluten-free
Ingredients:
• 1 sandwich
  • 1 sheet parchment or wax paper, large enough to wrap the sandwich
Equipment:

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Position for Wrapping: Place the sandwich in the center of a square sheet of parchment or wax paper. The sheet needs to be large enough to completely cover the sandwich with enough paper left over to fold and tuck underneath.
  2. Fold and Wrap: Pull the paper up and over the top of the sandwich and fold it down snugly against the sandwich, pressing it close so there is no loose paper or air gap.
  3. Secure the Wrap: Take one side of the paper and fold it in toward the center as if wrapping a present, creasing the edge firmly. Repeat on the other side. Tuck both folded edges firmly under the sandwich.

Prep: Use a sheet of paper generously larger than the sandwich itself — a too-small sheet won't fold and tuck securely, and the sandwich will come apart in transit.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Using a sheet of paper that is too small — the paper needs to be large enough to fully wrap and tuck under the sandwich or it will unravel. Not pressing the sandwich down before wrapping — a loose sandwich shifts inside the wrap and makes it harder to fold neatly. Overfilling the sandwich — too many fillings make it impossible to wrap tightly and the paper will tear or open. Folding the sides before the top — always fold the top down first then fold the sides in for a clean and secure wrap.

Notes: Parchment paper holds its shape better than wax paper and is the preferred choice for packed lunches and picnics. If wrapping for travel, fold tightly and secure with tape or a rubber band to keep it closed. This wrapping technique works for any sandwich regardless of fillings.

  5. Ferment: Pour into a sterilized glass jar or yogurt maker. Keep at 40–45°C (104–113°F) for 8–12 hours. The longer it ferments, the tangier it becomes.
  6. Chill: Refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving. The yogurt will thicken as it cools.

  4. Store: Transfer to a clean glass jar. Keeps at room temperature for up to 2 weeks, or refrigerated for up to 2 months.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the Lemons: Scrub 6–8 lemons clean. Trim the stem end of each. Cut each lemon lengthwise into quarters without cutting all the way through, keeping attached at the base like a flower.
  2. Salt Generously: Open each lemon and pack 1–2 tbsp (15–30 g) kosher salt inside the cuts. Press firmly closed.
  3. Pack the Jar: Sprinkle 1 tbsp salt on the bottom of a clean glass jar. Press the salted lemons tightly into the jar, squeezing as you go so they release their juice. Sprinkle extra salt between each layer.
  4. Top Up with Juice: After packing, the lemons should be fully submerged in juice. If there isn’t enough liquid after 24 hours, top up with freshly squeezed lemon juice until covered.
  5. Ferment: Seal tightly and leave at room temperature for 2–3 weeks. Shake gently every few days. Once the rinds are soft, translucent, and deeply fragrant, transfer to the refrigerator.

• 230 g (2 cups) old-fashioned rolled oats
  • 80 g (1 cup) whole almonds
  • 60 g (½ cup) uncooked quinoa
  • 113 g (⅓ cup) vegan honey
  • 56 g (¼ cup) dairy-free unsalted butter

Equipment:
• Baking sheet

  • Medium saucepan

  • Greased spatula

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Toast the Dry Ingredients: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Spread 230 g (2 cups) oats, 80 g (1 cup) chopped almonds, and 60 g (½ cup) quinoa on a baking sheet. Toast for 8–10 minutes, stirring halfway, until lightly golden and nutty. Set aside.
  2. Make the Syrup: In a saucepan, combine 113 g (⅓ cup) vegan honey, 56 g (¼ cup) dairy-free butter, and 50 g (¼ cup) brown sugar. Heat over medium, stirring until butter melts and sugar dissolves, about 3–4 minutes. Bring to a gentle simmer for 1 more minute. Remove from heat and stir in ½ tsp vanilla and ¼ tsp salt.
  3. Combine and Press: Mix toasted ingredients with the warm syrup until evenly coated. Line a 20 cm (8-inch) square pan with parchment. Press the mixture firmly into an even layer.
  4. Chocolate Drizzle: Melt 60 g (⅓ cup) chocolate chips in 20-second microwave intervals until smooth. Drizzle over the top.
  5. Set and Slice: Refrigerate for 3–4 hours or overnight. Lift out with parchment and slice into 12 bars.

1. Sanitize: Pour hot water into a mason jar, let sit for 1–2 minutes, then drain and cool.

  4. Harvest: By day 4 (up to day 6), sprouts should be vibrant and fill the jar. Transfer to a container lined with paper towel and refrigerate. Consume within 5 days.

  3. Mix Dry Ingredients: In a bowl, whisk together 220 g (1¾ cups) all-purpose flour, ½ tsp baking soda, and ¼ tsp salt.

  5. Combine: Add dry ingredients to wet and mix just until combined. Fold in 170 g (¾ cup) chocolate chips. Gently fold in 90 g (¾ cup) frozen raspberries last — do not crush them.
  6. Chill: Cover and refrigerate dough for 30 minutes.

Features: meal-prep-friendly; freezer-friendly; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free

Instruction Rich Text:
Prepare Your Starter (Day Before)

Key to Success: A bubbly, active starter at its peak is essential for the best sourdough!

First Feed — 12 hours before mixing

  • Mix 100 g (4 oz) of starter, discard the rest (see notes below for discard ideas)
  • With 100 g (4 oz) water + 100 g (4 oz) flour
  • Let rise 8–12 hours until doubled and bubbly

Second Feed — 5 hours before mixing

  • Mix 100 g (4 oz) of starter, discard the rest (see notes below for discard ideas)
  • Add 100 g (4 oz) water + 100 g (4 oz) flour
  • Let rise 5 hours until active and at peak
  • Check at 4:45 to confirm it's ready
  • You should have 200 g of bubbly starter ready to use

Ways to Use Sourdough Discard

Instead of throwing away your discard, try these:

  • Scallion Pancakes — Mix discard with chopped scallions, salt, and a little oil, then pan-fry until crispy
  • Start a New Jar — Feed the discard to create a backup starter or share with friends
  • Crackers — Roll thin with olive oil and salt, bake until crispy
  • Pancakes or Waffles — Add to your favorite recipe for extra tang
  • Muffins or Quick Breads — Substitute some flour and liquid in any recipe
  • Pizza Dough — Use discard for flavor in same-day pizza crust
  • Flatbreads or Naan — Quick stovetop breads with great flavor
  • Brownies or Cake — Yes, even chocolate desserts work with discard!

Tip: Keep a jar in the fridge labeled "discard" and add to it each time you feed. Use within a week for best results.

Make the Dough

Mix (30–60 minute rest)

  • Combine 400g water, 200g (4 oz) starter, and 600g flour
  • Mix until just combined
  • Rest 30–60 minutes

Add Salt (4 hour rise)

  • Dissolve 12g salt in a little water
  • Knead into dough for 10 minutes
  • Let rise 4 hours for bulk fermentation

Fold (30 minute rest between folds)

  • First fold: Flip, envelope fold, turn
  • Rest 30 minutes
  • Second fold: One final envelope fold

Shape & Proof (Overnight)

  • Line a large bowl with a floured dish towel
  • Place dough seam side up in the bowl
  • Sprinkle flour on top and cover with towel
  • Refrigerate overnight
  • Next morning: Remove 2 hours before baking to warm up

Bake

  • Preheat Dutch oven to 480°F for 30 minutes
  • Place dough on parchment
  • Score the bread with a sharp knife or lame (make a slash about ½ inch deep)
  • Lower into pot and mist lightly with water
  • Reduce to 430°F
  • Bake 25 minutes with lid on
  • Remove lid, bake 25 minutes more
  • Cool completely before slicing

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Soak the Soybeans: Soak 100 g (½ cup) dried soybeans in cold water overnight or at least 8 hours. Drain and rinse well.
  2. Blend: Add soaked soybeans and 960 ml (4 cups) water to a high-speed blender. Blend on high for 60–90 seconds until smooth.
  3. Cook: Pour into a large saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently to prevent sticking. Skim off any foam. Simmer for 15–20 minutes.
  4. Strain: Pour through a nut milk bag or fine cheesecloth into a large bowl. Squeeze firmly to extract all liquid. Discard the okara (soy pulp).
  5. Flavor (Optional): Add ½ tsp vanilla and 2 pitted dates for a lightly sweetened version. Blend briefly if using dates.
  6. Store: Transfer to a sealed glass bottle or jar. Refrigerate for up to 5 days. Shake well before each use.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prepare the Leaves: Soak grape leaves in warm water and rinse. Trim any thick veins.
  2. Cook the Lentils: Simmer 120 g (½ cup) red lentils with 240 ml (1 cup) water for 8–10 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain excess water.
  3. Sauté the Aromatics: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Sauté 1 medium chopped onion for 3–5 minutes. Add 3 minced garlic cloves and cook 1–2 more minutes.
  4. Make the Filling: In a bowl, combine cooked lentils, 100 g (½ cup) uncooked rice, sautéed onion and garlic, 30 g (½ cup) parsley, 15 g (¼ cup) dill, salt, pepper, and juice of 1 lemon. Mix well.
  5. Roll: Lay each leaf vein-side up. Add 1–2 tsp of filling, fold in sides, and roll tightly.
  6. Layer and Cook: Line the bottom of a pot with spare leaves. Arrange rolls seam-side down in snug layers. Drizzle with 3 tbsp olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, and 240 ml (1 cup) vegetable broth. Place a plate on top to weight them down.
  7. Simmer: Cover and simmer over low heat for 45–60 minutes until rice is fully cooked.
  8. Serve: Cool slightly and serve warm or chilled with lemon wedges.

Name: Sweet Potato Cinnamon Rolls

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Activate the Yeast: Warm 240 ml (1 cup) plant milk to about 40°C (105°F). Add 7 g (2¼ tsp) active dry yeast and 1 tbsp maple syrup. Stir and let sit for 5–10 minutes until foamy.
  2. Make the Dough: In a large bowl, combine 480 g (4 cups) all-purpose flour, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, ½ tsp ground nutmeg, and ¼ tsp ground ginger. Add the yeast mixture, 360 g (1½ cups) mashed sweet potato, and 2 tbsp oil. Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  3. First Rise: Cover and let rise in a warm place for 60–90 minutes until doubled.
  4. Fill and Roll: Mix 2 tbsp cinnamon and 50 g (¼ cup) brown sugar. Roll dough into a rectangle. Spread 2 tbsp melted coconut oil or vegan butter over the surface. Sprinkle with cinnamon sugar. Roll tightly and slice into 12 equal rolls.
  5. Second Rise: Arrange in a greased baking pan. Cover and rise for 30–45 minutes.

Name: How to Make Rose Water
Features: gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free
Common Ingredients: distilled-water-449d8; rose-petals-8df58
Ingredients:
• 60 g (2 cups) fresh fragrant rose petals
  • 480 ml (2 cups) distilled water
  • 480 ml (2 cups) ice
Equipment:
• Saucepan with lid
  • Fine mesh strainer or cheesecloth
  • Sterilized glass jar or bottle with lid
  • Funnel (optional)
Instruction Rich Text:
Method 1 — Simmer method (simple, good for everyday use)

  1. Prepare the rose petals: Use only fragrant, unsprayed rose petals. Rinse 60 g (2 cups) fresh rose petals (or 30 g / 1 cup dried) under cold water and gently pat dry.
  2. Simmer the petals: Place the rose petals in a saucepan and pour 480 ml (2 cups) distilled water over them. Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat. Do not boil. Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 20 minutes until the petals have lost most of their color.
  3. Cool and strain: Remove from heat and allow to cool completely. Pour through a fine-mesh strainer into a sterilized glass jar, pressing the petals gently to extract all the liquid.
  4. Store: Seal tightly and label with the date.

Method 2 — Distillation method (more fragrant, more concentrated — traditional)

  1. Set up the still: Place 60 g (2 cups) fresh rose petals in a large wide pot. Pour 480 ml (2 cups) distilled water over the petals. Place a heatproof bowl in the center of the pot, sitting directly on top of the petals — this bowl will collect the distilled rose water. The rim of the bowl should sit above the water line.
  2. Create the cold lid: Place the pot lid upside down on top of the pot. Fill the inverted lid generously with ice — at least 240 ml (1 cup) to start. The ice is what makes this method work: steam rises from the simmering petals, hits the ice-cold lid, condenses into droplets, and drips down into the collection bowl below.
  3. Simmer gently: Heat the pot over low heat and maintain a very gentle simmer for 20–30 minutes. Do not let it boil hard — a hard boil creates too much steam too quickly and drives off the delicate floral compounds. Keep the heat low and steady.
  4. Replenish the ice: Check the lid every 8–10 minutes. As the ice melts, pour off the water and add fresh ice to keep the lid cold. Cold condensation surface = more rose water collected.
  5. Collect the rose water: After 20–30 minutes the petals will have lost most of their color. Carefully remove the lid and lift the collection bowl out of the pot using tongs or oven mitts — it will be hot. The liquid inside the bowl is your distilled rose water.
  6. Strain and store: Pour through a fine-mesh strainer into a sterilized glass jar if any petal pieces are present. Seal tightly and label with the date.

Prep: Use only fragrant, unsprayed rose petals — pesticide-treated or unscented ornamental roses won't infuse any real rose flavor into the water, no matter how long you simmer them.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Boiling instead of simmering — a hard boil destroys the delicate floral compounds responsible for fragrance and flavor; always keep it at the lowest possible simmer. Forgetting to replenish the ice (distillation method) — once the ice melts the lid warms up, condensation stops, and no more rose water collects; check every 8-10 minutes. Not sterilizing the jar — rose water has no preservatives, and a non-sterilized jar introduces bacteria and will cause spoilage within days. Skipping the collection bowl setup (distillation method) — the bowl must sit above the waterline, or the rose water will be diluted and less fragrant. Using florist roses — these are almost always sprayed with pesticides; only use food-grade, unsprayed roses. Using roses with little fragrance — the scent of the rose directly determines the flavor and aroma, so the more fragrant the petal, the better the rose water.

Notes: Old garden roses, damask roses (Rosa damascena), and centifolia roses produce the most fragrant rose water, though any deeply fragrant variety will work. Collect petals in the morning, since rose fragrance is at its peak before the heat of the day dissipates the essential oils. The distillation method produces more concentrated, purer rose water because only the steam is captured, while the simmer method is simpler but more diluted. A little goes a long way — start with ½ tsp in recipes and adjust to taste, since rose water is potent.

Prep in Advance: Rose petals can be collected and stored in a sealed bag in the refrigerator for up to 2 days before making rose water. For longer storage, dry the petals completely and store in an airtight container. Sterilize your jars in advance by placing clean glass jars in a 160°C (325°F) oven for 10 minutes and letting them cool before filling.

Storage: Refrigerator — store in a sealed sterilized glass jar for up to 2 weeks; discard if the smell or appearance changes. Freezer — freeze in ice cube trays, then transfer to a sealed freezer bag for up to 3 months; each cube is approximately 30 ml (2 tbsp), perfect for portioning into drinks and recipes.

Tips: For a stronger rose water using the simmer method, repeat the process using the strained rose water in place of fresh distilled water with a new batch of petals. For the distillation method, keep a bowl of ice nearby so replenishing the lid is quick and you don't lose condensation time. Use a light-colored pot so you can easily see when the petals lose their color, which is your visual cue that extraction is complete.

Swaps: Dried rose petals — use half the amount (30 g / 1 cup) in place of fresh, rehydrating briefly in the distilled water before starting. Rose hip petals can be used for a slightly earthier, more tart rose water — not traditional but works well in savory applications.

Name: Lemon Bars (Vegan)
Common Ingredients: lemon; all-purpose-flour; vegan-butter; salt; sugar; powdered-sugar; cornstarch-0db33; dairy-free-milk-02620; shortbread-crust-1e18f; turmeric-95970
Ingredients:
• Shortbread Crust
  • 200 g (1⅔ cups) all-purpose flour
  • 60 g (½ cup) powdered sugar
  • 1 g (¼ tsp) salt
  • 115 g (½ cup) vegan butter
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) dairy-free milk
  • Lemon Filling
  • 240 ml (1 cup) fresh lemon juice
  • 2 tbsp lemon zest
  • 300 g (1½ cups) granulated sugar
  • 60 g (½ cup) cornstarch
  • 480 ml (2 cups) dairy-free milk
  • 1 g (¼ tsp) turmeric
  • To Serve
  • Powdered sugar, for dusting
Equipment:
• 9x13 inch baking pan
  • Parchment paper
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Medium saucepan
  • Whisk
  • Spatula
  • Zester or microplane
  • Juicer
  • Sieve
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat and Prep: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a 9x13 inch baking pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides for easy removal.
  2. Make the Crust: Mix together 200 g (1⅔ cups) flour, 60 g (½ cup) powdered sugar, and 1 g (¼ tsp) salt. Add the cold cubed 115 g (½ cup) vegan butter and rub into the flour until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add 15 ml (1 tbsp) dairy-free milk and mix until the dough just comes together. Press evenly into the base of the prepared pan.
  3. Bake the Crust: Bake for 18–20 minutes until lightly golden. Set aside to cool slightly.
  4. Make the Lemon Filling: Whisk together 300 g (1½ cups) sugar, 60 g (½ cup) cornstarch, and a pinch of turmeric. Gradually whisk in 480 ml (2 cups) dairy-free milk, then add 240 ml (1 cup) fresh lemon juice and 2 tbsp lemon zest. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, for 8–10 minutes until the mixture thickens to a pudding-like consistency.
  5. Assemble: Pour the hot lemon filling over the warm crust and spread evenly.
  6. Cool and Set: Allow to cool at room temperature for about 30 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours until fully set.
  7. Serve: Lift the bars out using the parchment overhang. Dust with powdered sugar and slice into 16 squares. Serve chilled.

Name: Hazelnut Butter
Common Ingredients: maple-syrup; hazelnuts; salt; vanilla-extract; neutral-oil
Ingredients:
• 300 g (2 cups) raw hazelnuts
  • 2 g (½ tsp) salt
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) neutral oil
Equipment:
• Parchment paper
  • Baking sheet
  • Clean kitchen towel
  • High-powered food processor or blender
  • Spatula
  • Glass jar with lid for storage
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Toast the Hazelnuts: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Spread the hazelnuts in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 10–12 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until the skins are cracked and the nuts are deep golden brown.
  2. Remove the Skins: Transfer the hot hazelnuts onto a clean kitchen towel. Rub vigorously for about 1 minute to remove as much of the papery skin as possible. Allow the nuts to cool for 5 minutes.
  3. Blend: Transfer the hazelnuts to a high-powered food processor. Process continuously for 8–12 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides every 2 minutes. The hazelnuts will go from coarse crumb to thick paste to smooth creamy butter.
  4. Season: Add 2 g (½ tsp) salt and, if using, 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup and 5 ml (1 tsp) vanilla extract. Blend for a further 30 seconds until fully combined.
  5. Store: Transfer to a clean glass jar. Keeps at room temperature for up to 2 weeks or refrigerated for up to 2 months.

Common Mistakes: Adding liquid too early — never add water or milk to the food processor as it causes the nut butter to seize into a stiff, gritty paste. Add oil only once the butter is already smooth. Not roasting long enough — under-roasted hazelnuts produce a pale, bland butter; the nuts should be deeply golden for the best flavour. Stopping the blending too soon — the mixture will look dry and crumbly for several minutes before it suddenly becomes smooth, so keep blending. Overheating the food processor — if the motor feels very hot, stop and rest for 5 minutes before continuing.

Storage: Store in a sealed glass jar at room temperature for up to 2 weeks. Refrigerate for up to 2 months. The butter will firm up when cold — bring to room temperature before using for easy spreading. Natural oil separation is normal; stir well before each use.

Tips: For a chocolate hazelnut version, blend in 2 tbsp cocoa powder and an extra tbsp of maple syrup once the butter is smooth. Try stirring a spoonful into oatmeal, spreading on toast, or using as a dip for apple slices.

Common Ingredients: avocado; bell-peppers; green-onions; mushrooms; potatoes; red-onion; spinach; tomatoes; tofu; nutritional-yeast; onion; salt; olive-oil; garlic-powder; neutral-oil; chives-c5cdb; dairy-free-milk-02620; turmeric-95970
Ingredients:
• 400 g (14 oz) firm or extra-firm tofu
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil or neutral oil
  • 1.1 g (½ tsp) turmeric
  • 1.5 g (½ tsp) garlic powder
  • 1.2 g (½ tsp) onion powder
  • 10 g (2 tbsp) nutritional yeast
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) dairy-free milk
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • 75 g (½ cup) cherry tomatoes
  • 30 g (1 cup) baby spinach
  • 75 g (½ cup) bell pepper
  • 35 g (½ cup) mushrooms
  • 40 g (¼ cup) red onion
  • Fresh chives or green onions
  • Hot sauce
  • Avocado slices
  • Toast or roasted potatoes
Equipment:
• Tofu press or clean kitchen towel
  • Small bowl
  • Non-stick skillet or cast iron pan
  • Spatula
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Press the Tofu: Drain 400 g firm tofu and press for at least 10 minutes to remove excess moisture. The drier the tofu, the better the texture.
  2. Make the Seasoning Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together ½ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp onion powder, 2 tbsp nutritional yeast, and 2 tbsp dairy-free milk. Set aside.
  3. Cook the Tofu: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Crumble the tofu directly into the pan. Cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes until the bottom starts to brown, then stir and cook for another 3–4 minutes.
  4. Add the Sauce: Pour the seasoning sauce over the tofu and stir to coat evenly. Cook for 1–2 minutes until absorbed and the tofu is golden and slightly crispy.
  5. Add Vegetables: If using add-ins, push the tofu to one side, add the vegetables, and sauté for 2–3 minutes until just tender. Stir everything together and season with salt and pepper.
  6. Serve: Serve immediately, hot and fresh straight from the pan.

Name: Cashew Butter
Common Ingredients: cashews; maple-syrup; salt; cinnamon
Ingredients:
• 411 g (3 cups) raw cashews
  • 1–2 tbsp maple syrup
  • 1.3 g (½ tsp) cinnamon powder
  • 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt
Equipment:
• Parchment paper
  • Baking sheet
  • Food processor or high-speed blender
  • Spatula
  • Glass jar with lid for storage
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Roast the Cashews: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Spread 3 cups raw cashews in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Roast for 8–10 minutes until lightly golden. Watch closely as cashews can burn quickly.
  2. Blend: Let the cashews cool slightly, then transfer to a food processor. Blend for 5–8 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides every 1–2 minutes. The cashews will go through stages — first a coarse crumb, then a thick paste, then a smooth, creamy butter.
  3. Season: Add 1–2 tbsp maple syrup, ½ tsp cinnamon powder, and ¼ tsp salt. Continue blending until fully combined and smooth.
  4. Store: Transfer to a clean glass jar. Store in a cool place for up to 1 month, or refrigerate for longer shelf life.

Name: Chocolate Covered Strawberries
Common Ingredients: chocolate; nuts; strawberries; chocolate-chips; salt; coconut-oil; sprinkles-b4728
Ingredients:
• 450 g (1 lb) fresh strawberries
  • 340 g (12 oz) good-quality chocolate chips or chopped chocolate
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) coconut oil
  • Sprinkles
  • Crushed nuts
  • White chocolate drizzle
  • Flaky sea salt
Equipment:
• Paper towels (for drying)
  • Parchment-lined tray or baking sheet
  • Microwave-safe bowl
  • Spatula or spoon
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the Strawberries: Wash strawberries well and dry completely — pat dry with paper towels, then let air dry for at least 30 minutes. Any water on the strawberries will prevent the chocolate from sticking. Line a tray with parchment paper and set aside.
  2. Melt the Chocolate: Add 340 g (12 oz) chocolate chips and 1 tsp coconut oil (if using) to a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave in 20–30 second bursts, stirring well between each round.
  3. Dip: Hold each strawberry by the green leaves. Dip into the melted chocolate and gently swirl to coat. Lift out and let any excess drip off, then place on the parchment-lined tray.
  4. Set: Let strawberries set at room temperature or refrigerate for 15–20 minutes for a faster set. Best enjoyed within 24 hours.

Prep: Let the washed strawberries air dry for the full 30 minutes after patting them dry — any lingering moisture on the surface is what keeps melted chocolate from sticking properly, causing it to slide right off.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Not drying the strawberries completely — this is the most important step. Even a tiny amount of water will cause the chocolate to seize and not adhere properly. Wash well in advance and allow plenty of drying time. Overheating the chocolate — stop microwaving when 90% melted and stir to finish. Overheated chocolate turns grainy and cannot be fixed. Skipping the parchment paper — chocolate will stick to any other surface.

Notes: Coconut oil is optional but adds shine and makes the chocolate slightly thinner and easier to dip. Room temperature setting gives the glossiest, most professional-looking finish. Refrigerating causes condensation and a duller appearance. Choose ripe, bright red strawberries with firm flesh and intact green tops — the tops are your handle.

Storage: Best enjoyed within 24 hours at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. Can be refrigerated in a single layer in an airtight container for up to 2 days, but the chocolate may develop condensation. Do not freeze.

Swaps: Use white chocolate or milk chocolate instead of dark for a different flavor. Drizzle contrasting chocolate over the set coating for a decorative finish. Add toppings like crushed pistachios, freeze-dried raspberry powder, or flaky sea salt before the chocolate sets.

Tips: Work quickly once the chocolate is melted — it begins to thicken as it cools. If the chocolate thickens too much, microwave for 10 seconds and stir. For the cleanest look, twist the strawberry slightly as you lift it out to cut the drip cleanly.
Why These Ingredients: A few ingredients do most of the work in this recipe. The fresh strawberries adds bright sweetness and a pop of color. The good-quality chocolate chips or chopped chocolate adds rich, deep chocolate flavor. The coconut oil adds richness and a subtle sweetness that supports the other flavors. The white chocolate drizzle adds rich, deep chocolate flavor.

Name: Frozen Banana Bites
Features: 20-minutes-or-less; gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free

Ingredients:
• 2–3 ripe bananas
  • 170 g (1 cup) good-quality chocolate chips
Equipment:
• Glass bowl (for melting chocolate)
  • Fork
  • Parchment-lined baking tray
  • Sealed freezer container

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Slice the Bananas: Peel and cut 2–3 ripe bananas into ½ inch pieces. Set aside on a plate.
  2. Melt the Chocolate: Add 170 g (1 cup) chocolate chips to a glass bowl. Microwave in 30-second increments, stirring well after each round, until completely melted and smooth.
  3. Coat the Bananas: Drop the banana pieces into the melted chocolate a few at a time. Using a fork, flip each piece to coat fully, then lift and shake off any excess chocolate. Place on a parchment-lined tray.
  4. Freeze: Place the tray in the freezer and freeze overnight until completely solid. Once frozen, transfer the bites to a sealed container and store in the freezer.

  6. Sweeten and Serve: Add sweetener to taste if desired. For a London Fog, stir in 60 ml (¼ cup) warm frothed oat milk and a drop of vanilla extract. Serve immediately.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Bake the Potatoes: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Pierce potatoes all over with a fork and bake directly on the oven rack for 50–60 minutes, until completely tender. Baking instead of boiling keeps them dry — the key to light gnocchi. Let cool slightly, then peel while still warm.
  2. Rice the Potatoes: Pass the peeled potatoes through a potato ricer or food mill onto a lightly floured surface. Spread them out and let steam escape for 2–3 minutes — you want them as dry as possible.
  3. Form the Dough: Make a well in the center of the riced potatoes. Add the egg, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Sprinkle 1 cup of flour over the top and gently mix with your hands, adding more flour a little at a time, just until a soft dough forms. Do not overwork — the less you knead, the more tender the gnocchi.
  4. Shape the Gnocchi: Divide the dough into 6 portions. Roll each into a long rope about ¾-inch thick. Cut into 1-inch pieces. If desired, roll each piece along the back of a fork to create ridges.
  5. Cook the Gnocchi: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Working in batches, drop the gnocchi in. They are done when they float to the surface, about 2–3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
  6. Make the Brown Butter Sauce: In a large skillet over medium heat, melt the butter. Add sage leaves and cook, swirling the pan, until the butter turns golden brown and smells nutty, about 3–4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
  7. Finish and Serve: Add the cooked gnocchi to the skillet and toss to coat. Serve immediately with freshly grated Parmesan.

  2. First toast cycle: Place the slices directly in the toaster slots (standing upright) or in a toaster oven. Toast on the highest setting. For a standard toaster, you will need 3–4 cycles total — the slices won't be done after one. For a toaster oven, toast at 220°C / 425°F for 8 minutes, then flip.
  3. Keep toasting until done: Repeat 2–3 more toaster cycles (or another 8–10 minutes in a toaster oven), flipping between rounds. The toast is ready when the outside is golden with lightly crisped edges and a knife slides through the thickest part without resistance. It should feel tender inside but hold its shape.
  4. Brush and top: While still warm, brush lightly with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Add your toppings immediately and serve.

Name: Croissants (Vegan)
Common Ingredients: all-purpose-flour; vegan-butter; oat-milk; salt; sugar; instant-yeast-7f935
Ingredients:
• 300 g (10.6 oz) all-purpose flour
  • 7 g (0.2 oz) instant yeast
  • 30 g (1.1 oz) sugar
  • 6 g (0.2 oz) salt
  • 160 ml (5.3 fl oz) warm oat milk
  • 20 g (0.7 oz) vegan butter
  • 200 g (7.1 oz) vegan butter
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) oat milk
Equipment:
• Stand mixer or large bowl
  • Rolling pin
  • Parchment paper
  • Baking sheet
  • Plastic wrap
  • Sharp knife or pizza cutter
  • Pastry brush
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Make the dough: In a large bowl, combine the flour, instant yeast, sugar, and salt. Add the warm oat milk and softened vegan butter. Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then knead for 5–7 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be slightly tacky but not sticky. Shape into a rectangle, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight.
  2. Prepare the butter block: Place the cold vegan butter between two sheets of parchment paper. Using a rolling pin, pound and shape it into a flat 15×15 cm (6×6 inch) square of even thickness. Refrigerate until firm but still pliable — it should bend without cracking. If it snaps, it’s too cold; let it sit at room temperature for a few minutes.
  3. Laminate — first fold: On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough into a 30×20 cm (12×8 inch) rectangle. Place the butter block in the center. Fold both sides of the dough over the butter like an envelope, pinching the edges to seal completely. Roll out to a long rectangle about 60×20 cm (24×8 inch). Fold into thirds like a letter. Wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
  4. Second and third folds: Repeat the rolling and folding process two more times, refrigerating for 30 minutes between each fold. After the third fold, refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight. Cold, relaxed dough is essential — rushing this step leads to torn layers and butter leaking out.
  5. Shape the croissants: Roll the laminated dough out to a large rectangle about 4–5 mm thick. Cut into long triangles — base roughly 10 cm (4 inches) wide. Make a small 1 cm notch in the center of each base. Gently stretch each triangle lengthwise. Starting from the base, roll tightly toward the tip, keeping tension as you go. Curve the ends slightly inward to form the classic crescent shape. Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet, tip-side down.
  6. Proof: Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let proof at room temperature (ideally 24°C / 75°F) for 2–3 hours, until visibly puffed and jiggling when the tray is gently shaken. Do not over-proof — the layers will collapse. You should be able to see the distinct layers in the dough.
  7. Brush and bake: Preheat the oven to 200°C / 400°F. Brush each croissant gently with oat milk — do not let it drip down the cut sides or it will glue the layers together. Bake for 18–22 minutes until deeply golden brown. Cool on a wire rack for at least 15 minutes before eating.

Prep: Chill the dough for the full hour, or overnight, before laminating — this firms up the butter and gluten so the layers stay distinct instead of merging into a dense, un-flaky dough.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Notes: Use a high-quality European-style vegan butter with at least 80% fat content — Miyoko's, Violife, or Naturli block butter. Low-fat spreads contain too much water and will steam rather than laminate, giving you bread instead of croissants. If at any point the butter starts melting into the dough, stop and refrigerate immediately for 20-30 minutes.

Common Mistakes: Rolling too hard and fast tears the layers. Skipping rest times causes the dough to snap back and the butter to break. Under-proofing gives a dense, bready interior. Do not let the oat milk wash drip down the cut sides — it glues the layers together.

Prep in Advance: The dough can be made through all three folds and refrigerated overnight before shaping. Shaped croissants can also be frozen before proofing — freeze solid on a tray, then transfer to a bag. To bake from frozen, thaw overnight in the refrigerator then proof at room temperature for 3-4 hours.

Storage: Best eaten the day they are baked. Store at room temperature in an open bag for up to 2 days. Reheat in a 180°C / 350°F oven for 5 minutes to restore flakiness. Freeze baked croissants for up to 1 month — reheat from frozen at 180°C for 10-12 minutes.

1. Preheat the oven: Preheat to 425°F (220°C). Position a rack in the center and line a large rimmed baking sheet (or two) with parchment paper.

  3. Season generously: Toss all the vegetables, garlic cloves, thyme, and rosemary in a large bowl with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Make sure every piece is well coated.

  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) soy sauce or tamari
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) apple cider vinegar

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Slice the tempeh: Cut the tempeh block into thin strips, about 3–4 mm thick. Thinner slices will be crispier; thicker ones will be chewier. Aim for even thickness so they cook uniformly.
  2. Make the marinade: In a shallow bowl or dish, whisk together the soy sauce, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper.
  3. Marinate: Add the tempeh strips to the marinade and toss to coat. Let them soak for at least 5 minutes — or up to 30 minutes for deeper flavor. Turn the strips once halfway through.
  4. Cook: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the tempeh strips in a single layer, working in batches if needed. Cook for 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and caramelized. Pour any remaining marinade over the strips in the last minute of cooking and let it reduce and glaze.
  5. Drain and serve: Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate briefly, then serve immediately. Tempeh bacon is best fresh and crispy straight from the pan.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Make the pickled vegetables: Combine the rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl and stir until dissolved (microwave 30 seconds if needed). Add the julienned carrot and daikon, toss to coat, and set aside for at least 15 minutes. The vegetables will soften and turn lightly pink. These can be made up to 3 days ahead and stored in the fridge.
  2. Make the sriracha mayo: In a small bowl, whisk together the vegan mayo, sriracha, and lime juice until smooth. Taste and adjust heat level. Set aside.
  3. Cook the mushrooms: In a small bowl, mix together the soy sauce, hoisin, sesame oil, rice vinegar, sriracha, garlic, and ginger to form the marinade. Heat neutral oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and cook without stirring for 3–4 minutes until golden and caramelized on one side. Flip and cook another 2 minutes. Pour the marinade over the mushrooms and toss to coat. Cook for another 2–3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces and glazes the mushrooms. Remove from heat.
  4. Toast the bread: Slice the baguettes lengthwise, leaving a hinge. Toast cut-side down in a dry pan or under the broiler for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden and crispy on the outside but still soft inside.
  5. Assemble: Spread a generous layer of sriracha mayo on both cut sides of each baguette. Layer the glazed mushrooms along the bottom. Top with pickled vegetables, cucumber slices, fresh cilantro, and jalapeño if using. Squeeze a lime wedge over the top, close the sandwich, and serve immediately.

Ingredients:
• 555 g (3 cups) cooked jasmine or long-grain rice
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) neutral oil
  • 160 g (1 medium) onion
  • 12 g (4) garlic cloves
  • 2 g (1 tsp) fresh ginger
  • 122 g (2 medium) carrots
  • 145 g (1 cup) frozen peas
  • 165 g (1 cup) corn kernels
  • 3 spring onions (scallions), thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) soy sauce or tamari
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) sesame oil
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) rice vinegar
  • ½ tsp white pepper (or black pepper)
  • Sesame seeds, for garnish
  • Extra spring onion greens, for garnish
Equipment:
• Large wok or wide skillet (the bigger the better)
  • Wooden spoon or wok spatula
  • Sharp knife and cutting board
  • Measuring spoons
  • Small bowl (for mixing sauce)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep everything first: Fried rice comes together fast over high heat — have all your ingredients chopped, measured, and ready before you turn on the stove. Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and white pepper together in a small bowl and set aside.
  2. Break up the rice: If using day-old rice, break up any clumps with your hands before cooking. Cold, dry rice fries much better than fresh — it won't steam and clump in the pan.
  3. Cook the aromatics: Heat 1 tbsp of neutral oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add the onion and cook, stirring frequently, for 2–3 minutes until softened and lightly golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onion whites and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
  4. Add the vegetables: Add the carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the peas and corn and cook for another minute, tossing everything together.
  5. Fry the rice: Push the vegetables to the side of the wok. Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the empty space and add the rice. Press it down into the hot pan and let it sit undisturbed for 1–2 minutes to get some crispy bits on the bottom. Then toss everything together, breaking up any remaining clumps.
  6. Season and finish: Pour the sauce mixture over the rice and toss well to coat every grain evenly. Stir-fry for another 1–2 minutes until the sauce is fully absorbed and the rice looks glossy and fragrant. Taste and adjust seasoning.
  7. Serve: Transfer to bowls and garnish with spring onion greens and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

Name: Cucumber Sushi
Common Ingredients: avocado; bell-peppers; carrots; cucumber; rice; sushi-rice; sesame-seeds-2; salt; sugar; extra-soy-sauce-d51d2; nori-3666a; pickled-ginger-40e4a; sesame-oil-c6ff4; soy-sauce-e7086; sriracha-5f319; tamari-de23a; wasabi-61143
Ingredients:
• 185 g (1 cup) sushi rice
  • 300 ml (1¼ cups) water
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) rice vinegar
  • 12.5 g (1 tbsp) sugar
  • 3 g (½ tsp) salt
  • 2 large English cucumbers
  • 4 sheets nori (toasted seaweed)
  • 1 ripe avocado, thinly sliced
  • 61 g (1 medium) carrot
  • ½ red bell pepper, thinly sliced
  • ½ cup (80 g) edamame, shelled and cooked
  • 2 tbsp sesame seeds
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) soy sauce or tamari
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) sesame oil
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) rice vinegar

  • Wasabi
  • Extra soy sauce
Equipment:
• Vegetable peeler or mandoline
  • Sharp knife and cutting board
  • Bamboo sushi mat (optional)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cook the sushi rice: Rinse the sushi rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine with water in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let steam, covered, for 10 more minutes. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
  2. Season the rice: Combine rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl and stir until dissolved. Transfer the hot rice to a wide bowl. Pour the vinegar mixture over the rice and fold gently with a spatula using cutting motions — don't stir or mash. Fan the rice as you fold to cool it quickly and make it glossy. Let cool to room temperature before rolling.
  3. Prep the cucumber: For maki-style rolls: cut cucumber into thin matchsticks to use as a filling. For cucumber-wrapped rolls: use a vegetable peeler or mandoline to shave into long, thin ribbons lengthwise. In either case, pat dry with paper towels — excess moisture makes soggy rolls.
  4. Assemble the rolls: Place a sheet of nori shiny-side down on a bamboo mat or clean kitchen towel. With wet hands, spread a thin, even layer of sushi rice over the nori, leaving a 2 cm border at the top. Arrange fillings in a horizontal line across the center — avocado, carrot, bell pepper, edamame, and cucumber matchsticks. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
  5. Roll tightly: Lift the bottom edge of the mat and roll it over the fillings, pressing firmly and evenly. Pull the mat back as you roll so it doesn't get caught inside. Once fully rolled, press firmly to shape into a tight cylinder. Seal the edge with a small dab of water.
  6. Slice: Using a sharp, wet knife, slice each roll into 8 pieces using a single smooth stroke — don't saw. Wipe and wet the blade between each cut for clean edges.
  7. Make the dipping sauce: Whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and sriracha if using. Serve in a small bowl alongside the rolls.
  8. Serve: Arrange pieces cut-side up on a plate with pickled ginger, wasabi, and dipping sauce. Serve immediately.

Name: Pita Bread
Common Ingredients: all-purpose-flour; bread; salt; olive-oil; sugar; instant-yeast-7f935
Ingredients:
• 500 g (4 cups) bread flour or all-purpose flour
  • 7 g (1 packet / 2¼ tsp) instant yeast
  • 4.2 g (1 tsp) sugar
  • 9 g (1½ tsp) salt
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil
  • 300 ml (1¼ cups) warm water
Equipment:
• Large mixing bowl
  • Stand mixer with dough hook (optional)
  • Cast-iron skillet or heavy griddle
  • Rolling pin
  • Kitchen scale
  • Clean towel (to keep pitas warm)
  • Baking stone or heavy sheet pan (if baking)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Make the dough: In a large bowl, combine flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Add the olive oil and warm water. Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then knead on a lightly floured surface for 8–10 minutes until the dough is smooth, soft, and springs back when poked. Alternatively, knead in a stand mixer with a dough hook for 6 minutes.
  2. First rise: Shape the dough into a ball and place in a lightly oiled bowl. Cover with a damp towel or cling film and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
  3. Divide and rest: Punch down the risen dough and divide into 8 equal pieces (about 100 g each). Shape each into a smooth ball. Cover with a towel and let rest for 10 minutes — this relaxes the gluten and makes rolling easier.
  4. Roll the pitas: On a lightly floured surface, roll each ball into a circle about 20–22 cm (8 inches) in diameter and 3–4 mm thick. Even thickness is key — thick spots won’t puff properly.
  5. Cook: Heat a cast-iron skillet, heavy pan, or griddle over very high heat until smoking hot. Cook each pita for 1–2 minutes on the first side until large bubbles appear. Flip and cook another 1 minute. The pita should puff up dramatically — this is the steam pocket forming inside. Remove and keep warm wrapped in a clean towel.
  6. Alternatively, bake: Preheat oven to 250°C (480°F) with a baking stone or heavy baking sheet inside. Place pitas directly on the hot surface and bake for 4–5 minutes until puffed and just beginning to colour.
  7. Serve: Best eaten warm. Serve with hummus, falafel, dips, or slice open to fill.

Name: Lentil Soup
Common Ingredients: carrots; celery; garlic; cilantro; parsley; lemon; lentils; tomatoes; bread; onion; salt; vegetable-broth; olive-oil; cumin; smoked-paprika; black-pepper; coriander-27a41; turmeric-95970
Ingredients:
• 400 g (2 cups) red lentils
  • 160 g (1 large) onion
  • 12 g (4) garlic cloves
  • 122 g (2 medium) carrots
  • 80 g (2) celery stalks
  • 1 can (400 g) diced tomatoes
  • 1.5 L (6 cups) vegetable broth
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil
  • 4 g (2 tsp) cumin
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) smoked paprika
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) turmeric
  • ½ tsp ground coriander
  • 1 g (½ tsp) black pepper
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt
  • Juice of 1 lemon
  • Fresh parsley or cilantro, to serve
  • Crusty bread or pita, to serve
Equipment:
• Large pot or Dutch oven (at least 4 L)
  • Immersion blender or countertop blender (optional)
  • Sharp knife and cutting board
  • Wooden spoon
  • Ladle
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Sauté the aromatics: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
  2. Add the vegetables and spices: Add the carrots and celery and stir to combine. Add the cumin, smoked paprika, turmeric, coriander, and black pepper. Stir and cook for 1–2 minutes, letting the spices bloom in the oil.
  3. Add lentils, tomatoes, and broth: Add the rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes (with their juices), and vegetable broth. Stir everything together, scraping any browned bits from the bottom.
  4. Simmer: Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are completely soft and beginning to break down. The soup will thicken as it cooks.
  5. Blend (optional): For a creamy texture, use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup — blend half and leave half chunky for texture. Alternatively, transfer a third of the soup to a blender, blend until smooth, and stir back in.

Common Ingredients: all-purpose-flour; maple-syrup; non-dairy-milk; salt; sugar; apple-cider-vinegar; neutral-oil; coconut-oil; baking-powder-3e21e; fine-yellow-cornmeal-a1db5
Ingredients:
• 210 g (1½ cups) fine yellow cornmeal
  • 120 g (1 cup) all-purpose flour
  • 50 g (¼ cup) granulated sugar
  • 14 g (1 tbsp) baking powder
  • 3 g (½ tsp) salt
  • 240 ml (1 cup) unsweetened non-dairy milk
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) apple cider vinegar
  • 30 ml (⅛ cup) neutral oil or melted coconut oil
  • 60 ml (¼ cup) maple syrup
Equipment:
• 20x20 cm (8x8 inch) baking pan or cast-iron skillet
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Whisk
  • Spatula
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat and prep: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Grease a 20×20 cm (8×8 inch) square baking pan or cast-iron skillet with oil. For extra crispy edges, place the oiled pan in the oven while it preheats.
  2. Make vegan buttermilk: In a small bowl, combine the non-dairy milk and apple cider vinegar. Stir and let sit for 3–5 minutes until slightly curdled. This is your vegan buttermilk.
  3. Mix dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
  4. Mix wet ingredients: Add the oil and maple syrup to the vegan buttermilk and stir to combine.
  5. Combine: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined — a few lumps are fine. Do not overmix or the cornbread will be dense and tough.
  6. Bake: Pour the batter into the prepared hot pan. Bake for 20–25 minutes until the top is golden and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
  7. Cool and serve: Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm with vegan butter, maple syrup, or alongside chili, soups, and stews.

  5. Assemble: Arrange the hot fries on a large plate or baking dish. Spoon the warm chili generously over the fries. Drizzle or pour the cheese sauce over the top.
  6. Top and serve: Finish with sliced spring onions, pickled jalapeños, cilantro, and a dollop of vegan sour cream if using. Serve immediately while everything is hot.

Ingredients:
• 1 medium head cauliflower (about 700 g / 1.5 lbs), cut into florets
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) ground flaxseed + 9 tbsp water
  • 15 g (3 tbsp) nutritional yeast

  • 98 g (½) zucchini
  • Handful of cherry tomatoes, halved
  • 40 g (¼) red onion
  • Fresh basil leaves, to finish
  • Chili flakes and olive oil, to finish
Equipment:
• Food processor or box grater
  • Large microwave-safe bowl or steamer
  • Clean kitchen towel or cheesecloth (for squeezing)
  • Large baking sheet or pizza stone
  • Parchment paper
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Spatula
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Make the flax eggs: Mix 3 tbsp ground flaxseed with 9 tbsp water. Stir and let sit 10 minutes until thick and gel-like.
  2. Rice the cauliflower: Pulse cauliflower florets in a food processor until they resemble fine breadcrumbs. Don’t over-process into mush. Alternatively grate on the large holes of a box grater.
  3. Cook the cauliflower: Microwave riced cauliflower in a large bowl for 4–5 minutes until steamed through. Alternatively steam on the stovetop for 5 minutes. Spread onto a clean kitchen towel and cool 5 minutes.
  4. Squeeze out ALL the moisture — this is the most important step: Wrap the cauliflower in the towel and squeeze as hard as you can over the sink. Remove as much water as possible — a soggy crust is almost always from not squeezing enough. Aim to remove at least ½ cup of liquid.
  5. Make the crust mixture: Combine the squeezed cauliflower, flax eggs, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, oregano, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Mix well until it holds together when pressed.
  6. Shape and pre-bake: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Line a baking sheet with oiled parchment. Press the cauliflower mixture into a 25–28 cm circle, about 5–6 mm thick with slightly thicker edges. Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and dry on top with deeply browned edges.
  7. Add sauce and toppings: Mix passata with garlic, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper. Spread over the pre-baked crust leaving a 2 cm border. Add vegan mozzarella, then layer on bell pepper, zucchini, cherry tomatoes, and red onion.
  8. Bake again: Return to oven for 12–15 minutes until cheese is melted and vegetables are tender with charred edges.
  9. Finish and serve: Rest 2–3 minutes. Top with fresh basil, chili flakes, and a drizzle of olive oil. Slice and serve immediately.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat the oven: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Lightly oil a baking dish large enough to hold all 4 peppers upright.
  2. Prep the peppers: Slice the top off each bell pepper and remove the seeds and white membranes. Trim a tiny sliver off the bottom if needed so they stand upright without tipping. Lightly brush or rub the outside of each pepper with olive oil. Place upright in the baking dish.
  3. Make the filling: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, and garlic powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the zucchini and cook for 2–3 minutes. Stir in the drained diced tomatoes and cook for 2 more minutes. Remove from heat and fold in the cooked rice, beans, and corn. Season generously with salt and pepper. Taste — the filling should be well-seasoned as the pepper will absorb some of the flavour.
  4. Fill the peppers: Spoon the filling generously into each pepper, pressing it down lightly and mounding it slightly over the top. If using vegan cheese, sprinkle it over each filled pepper.
  5. Bake covered: Cover the baking dish tightly with foil and bake for 25 minutes. The steam helps cook the peppers through without drying out the filling.
  6. Uncover and finish: Remove the foil and bake for another 10 minutes until the peppers are tender with slightly charred edges and the cheese (if using) is melted and golden.
  7. Serve: Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Top with fresh cilantro or parsley and serve with lime wedges on the side.

Ingredients:
• 277.5 g (1½ cups) sushi rice
  • 360 ml (1½ cups) + 2–3 tbsp water
  • 60 ml (¼ cup) rice vinegar
  • 1 pinch of salt
  • 350 g (12.3 oz) extra firm tofu

  • 10 ml (2 tsp) maple syrup

Equipment:

  • Small bowl of water (to wet hands and knife)
  • Squeeze bottle or piping bag (for sriracha mayo)

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cook the sushi rice: Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs completely clear — this is essential for a non-sticky, glossy result. Add the rinsed rice to a saucepan with 1½ cups + 2–3 tbsp water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then immediately reduce to the lowest heat setting, cover tightly, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let steam, lid on, for 10 minutes. Do not lift the lid while cooking.
  2. Season the rice: While the rice steams, mix together the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt. Transfer the hot rice to a wide, flat bowl — a wooden or ceramic bowl is ideal as metal retains heat. Pour the vinegar mixture over the rice and fold gently with a spatula using wide, slicing motions. Fan the rice as you fold to help it cool quickly to room temperature and develop that signature glossy sheen. Let it cool completely before assembling.
  3. Cook the crispy tofu: Press the tofu firmly with paper towels or a tofu press to remove as much moisture as possible. Cut into thin strips or crumble into chunky pieces. In a small bowl, mix together the sesame oil, maple syrup, soy sauce, and dark soy sauce to make the glaze. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 3–4 minutes without moving, until a golden crust forms on the bottom. Flip and cook another 3 minutes. Pour the glaze over the tofu and toss to coat — the sugars in the maple syrup will caramelise and coat the tofu in a sticky, lacquered finish. Cook for another 1–2 minutes until deeply golden. Set aside to cool slightly.
  4. Make the sriracha mayo: Whisk together the plant-based mayo and sriracha in a small bowl until smooth. Taste and adjust heat — add more sriracha for fire, more mayo to mellow. Transfer to a squeeze bottle or piping bag for easy drizzling.
  5. Prep the fillings: Julienne the carrot into fine matchsticks. Slice the cucumber into thin strips or ribbons. Slice the avocado thinly. Have the micro greens, sesame seeds, and sriracha mayo ready to go before you start rolling.
  6. Assemble the sushi burritos: Lay a sheet of nori on a clean, dry surface or bamboo mat, rough side up. With wet hands, spread a generous, even layer of cooled sushi rice over the entire nori sheet, leaving a 3 cm border along the top edge. The rice layer should be about 5–6 mm thick — substantial enough to hold the fillings when rolled.

    Arrange the fillings horizontally across the centre of the rice: a row of crispy tofu, sliced avocado, carrot, cucumber, and a small handful of micro greens. Drizzle generously with sriracha mayo. Sprinkle with 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds.
  7. Roll like a burrito: Fold the bottom edge of the nori up and over the fillings, tucking it tightly underneath. Fold in both sides like a burrito, then roll forward firmly and evenly, applying pressure as you go to keep it tight and compact. The nori will seal itself with the moisture from the rice. If needed, dab the top edge with a little water to seal. Repeat for the remaining 2 rolls.
  8. Slice and serve: Using a sharp, wet knife, slice each burrito in half at a slight diagonal for the best presentation. Arrange cut-side up on a plate. Drizzle with extra sriracha mayo and garnish with a pinch more sesame seeds and micro greens. Serve immediately.

Name: Maple Glazed Carrots
Common Ingredients: carrots; parsley; maple-syrup; vegan-butter; salt; olive-oil; cinnamon; black-pepper; apple-cider-vinegar; thyme; ginger-b4168
Ingredients:
• 700 g (about 6–8 medium) carrots
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) maple syrup
  • 22.5 ml (1½ tbsp) vegan butter or olive oil
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) apple cider vinegar
  • 1.3 g (½ tsp) ground cinnamon
  • 0.5 g (¼ tsp) ground ginger
  • 3 g (½ tsp) salt
  • 0.5 g (¼ tsp) black pepper
  • 3 g (1 tbsp) fresh thyme leaves
  • Fresh parsley, roughly chopped, to serve
  • Flaky sea salt, to finish (optional)
Equipment:
• Large wide skillet or sauté pan with lid
  • Vegetable peeler
  • Sharp knife and cutting board
  • Wooden spoon or spatula
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the carrots: Peel the carrots and cut them into even pieces — diagonal coins about 1.5 cm thick, or halve lengthwise and cut into batons. Uniform sizing is important so everything cooks at the same rate. Baby carrots can be used whole or halved.
  2. Start cooking: Melt the vegan butter in a large, wide skillet over medium heat. Add the carrots in a single layer and cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes until lightly golden on the first side. Flip and cook another 2–3 minutes. The goal is a little caramelisation before adding the glaze.
  3. Add the glaze: Pour in the maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, cinnamon, ginger, salt, and pepper. Stir to coat every carrot. The mixture will bubble up — that’s the glaze beginning to form. Add 2–3 tbsp of water to help the carrots cook through without burning.
  4. Simmer and glaze: Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the carrots are just tender when pierced with a knife. Remove the lid and increase heat to medium-high. Cook for another 2–3 minutes, stirring frequently, as the liquid reduces into a thick, sticky glaze that coats every piece. Ingredients:
• 2 ripe bananas (the riper the better — lots of brown spots)
  • 135 g (1½ cups) rolled oats
  • 64.5 g (¼ cup) almond butter or peanut butter
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) maple syrup
  • 2 tbsp ground flaxseed
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 2.7 g (1 tsp) ground cinnamon
  • 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt
  • 1.2 g (¼ tsp) baking powder
  • 42.5 g (¼ cup) dark chocolate chips
  • 25 g (¼ cup) dried cranberries or raisins
  • 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds or sunflower seeds
  • 2 tbsp shredded coconut (optional)
Equipment:
• Large baking sheet
  • Parchment paper
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Fork (for mashing)
  • Cookie scoop or spoon
  • Wire cooling rack
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat the oven: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Mash the bananas: In a large bowl, mash the bananas thoroughly with a fork until almost completely smooth — a few small lumps are fine. The riper the bananas, the sweeter and more flavourful the cookies will be.
  3. Add the wet ingredients: Stir in the almond butter, maple syrup, and vanilla extract into the mashed banana. Mix until smooth and combined.
  4. Add the dry ingredients: Add the rolled oats, ground flaxseed, cinnamon, salt, and baking powder. Stir until everything is evenly combined and a thick, sticky dough forms. Let the mixture sit for 3–5 minutes — the oats and flaxseed will absorb the moisture and the dough will firm up slightly.
  5. Fold in the mix-ins: Gently fold in the chocolate chips, dried cranberries, seeds, and coconut if using. Make sure the mix-ins are evenly distributed throughout the dough.
  6. Scoop and shape: Using a spoon or cookie scoop, portion the dough into 12 equal mounds on the prepared baking sheet. Flatten each one gently with the back of a spoon or damp fingers into a round, about 1.5 cm thick — these cookies won’t spread in the oven, so shape them how you want them to look.
  7. Bake: Bake for 12–14 minutes until the edges are set and lightly golden. The centres may still look slightly soft — they will firm up as they cool. Do not overbake or they will dry out.
  8. Cool and serve: Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. They are delicious warm, but firm up to a perfect chewy texture once fully cooled.
