Name: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies (Vegan)
Common Ingredients: flax-egg; oats; all-purpose-flour; vegan-butter; non-dairy-milk; salt; cinnamon; vanilla-extract; nutmeg; brown-sugar; baking-soda; baking-powder-3e21e; raisins-4630d
Ingredients:
• 135 g (1½ cups) rolled oats
  • 120 g (1 cup) all-purpose flour
  • 159.8 g (¾ cup) brown sugar
  • 113.5 g (½ cup) vegan butter
  • 15 g (1) flax egg
  • 8.7 g (2 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 2.7 g (1 tsp) ground cinnamon
  • 0.6 g (¼ tsp) ground nutmeg
  • 2.3 g (½ tsp) baking soda
  • 2.3 g (½ tsp) baking powder
  • 3 g (½ tsp) salt
  • 145 g (1 cup) raisins
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) non-dairy milk
Equipment:
• Large baking sheet(s)
  • Parchment paper
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Electric hand mixer or stand mixer
  • Small bowl (for flax egg and raisin soaking)
  • Spatula
  • Cookie scoop or spoon
  • Wire cooling rack
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Make the flax egg: Mix 1 tbsp ground flaxseed with 3 tbsp water in a small bowl. Stir and set aside for 5 minutes until it becomes thick and gel-like. This acts as the egg binder.
  2. Soak the raisins (optional but recommended): Place the raisins in a small bowl and cover with warm water. Soak for 10 minutes, then drain and pat dry. This plumps them up so they stay juicy and tender inside the baked cookie rather than chewy or hard.
  3. Cream the butter and sugar: In a large bowl, beat the softened vegan butter and brown sugar together with an electric hand mixer or stand mixer for 2–3 minutes until light, fluffy, and slightly pale. This step incorporates air into the dough and is key to a tender, chewy cookie — don’t skip it.
  4. Add wet ingredients: Add the flax egg and vanilla extract to the creamed butter. Beat for another minute until fully combined and smooth.
  5. Add dry ingredients: Add the flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt to the bowl. Mix on low speed (or fold by hand) until just combined — don’t overmix. A few dry streaks are fine at this stage.
  6. Fold in oats and raisins: Add the rolled oats and drained raisins. Fold in gently with a spatula until evenly distributed. If the dough feels very stiff and dry, add the non-dairy milk one tablespoon at a time until it comes together. The dough should be thick, scoopable, and hold its shape.
  7. Chill the dough: Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (or up to 24 hours). Chilling is important — it firms up the fat in the dough so the cookies spread less and bake up thicker and chewier. Don’t skip this step.
  8. Bake: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. Scoop the dough into 16 equal balls (about 2 tbsp each) and place at least 5 cm apart on the sheets. Flatten slightly with your palm — these cookies spread a little but not a lot. Bake for 11–13 minutes until the edges are golden and set but the centres still look slightly underdone. They will continue to cook on the hot tray.
  9. Cool and serve: Leave on the baking sheet for 5–10 minutes — this is crucial, as they will be very soft and fragile straight from the oven. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely. The texture transforms from soft and fragile to perfectly chewy as they cool.

Name: Grilled Asparagus
Common Ingredients: asparagus; garlic; lemon; nutritional-yeast; salt; olive-oil; black-pepper; chili-flakes-f3449
Ingredients:
• 500 g (1 lb) fresh asparagus
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil
  • 9 g (3) garlic cloves
  • 1 tsp lemon zest
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) lemon juice
  • 3 g (½ tsp) salt
  • 0.5 g (¼ tsp) black pepper
  • ¼ tsp chili flakes (optional)
  • 5 g (1 tbsp) nutritional yeast
  • Flaky sea salt, to finish
  • Extra lemon wedges, to serve
Equipment:
• Outdoor grill or grill pan
  • Large bowl or shallow dish (for marinating)
  • Tongs
  • Paper towels
  • Pastry brush (for oiling grill)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the asparagus: Hold each asparagus spear at both ends and bend gently — it will naturally snap at the point where the woody base ends and the tender stalk begins. Discard the woody ends. Alternatively, line the spears up and trim about 4–5 cm off the bottoms with a knife. Pat the spears completely dry with paper towels — moisture causes steaming instead of charring on the grill.
  2. Make the garlic marinade: In a large bowl or shallow dish, combine the olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and chili flakes. Add the asparagus and toss to coat every spear thoroughly. Let marinate for at least 5 minutes — or up to 30 minutes for deeper flavour.
  3. Preheat the grill: Heat an outdoor grill or grill pan over high heat until very hot — you want to see wisps of smoke. Brush the grates lightly with oil to prevent sticking. A screaming hot surface is what creates those beautiful char marks and caramelised edges rather than a soggy steam.
  4. Grill the asparagus: Lay the asparagus spears perpendicular to the grill grates so they don’t fall through. Grill for 3–4 minutes without moving to develop char marks. Flip and grill another 3–4 minutes on the other side. The spears should be bright green with deep char marks, tender when pierced but still with a little bite. Thin spears will cook faster — check after 2 minutes per side.

1. Blend the blueberries: Add the blueberries, lemon juice, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt to a blender. Add 200 ml of the water or coconut water. For best results, refrigerate for 1–2 hours or overnight — the longer it sits, the more the chia seeds bloom and the flavours deepen.
  5. Serve: Stir well before serving as the chia seeds may settle. Pour over a glass full of ice. Garnish with fresh mint, a few whole blueberries, or a slice of lemon. Serve immediately or keep chilled.

  • 240 g (2 cups) self-rising flour
  • 4.7 g (1 tsp) baking powder

  • Parchment paper

  • Bench scraper or knife

Servings 1 bagel bite  Calories 115  Carbohydrates 20 g  Fat 2 g  Fiber 1 g  Protein 4 g

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat the oven: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Make the dough: In a large bowl, combine the self-rising flour, baking powder, and salt. Whisk to combine. Add the thick plant-based yogurt and maple syrup. Mix with a fork or your hands until a shaggy dough forms, then knead in the bowl for 1–2 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky. If the dough sticks heavily to your hands, add flour 1 tbsp at a time. If it feels too dry and crumbly, add yogurt 1 tbsp at a time. The texture should feel like soft, pliable Play-Doh.
  3. Divide and shape: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Divide into 12 equal pieces (about 40 g each) using a bench scraper or knife. Roll each piece into a smooth ball between your palms. Then poke your thumb through the centre of each ball and gently stretch it out to form a ring shape about 5 cm in diameter. The hole will shrink during baking, so make it slightly larger than you want the finished bagel to be.
  4. Apply the wash and toppings: Place the shaped bagel bites on the prepared baking sheet, spaced about 3 cm apart. Mix the non-dairy milk and maple syrup in a small bowl. Brush each bagel bite generously with the vegan wash — this gives them their golden, shiny finish. Sprinkle immediately with your chosen toppings, pressing gently so they adhere.
  5. Bake: Bake for 20–22 minutes until deeply golden on top and the bottoms are set and lightly browned. They should feel firm and hollow-sounding when tapped on the bottom. Don’t underbake — a pale bagel bite will be doughy inside.
  6. Cool briefly and serve: Let cool on the tray for 5 minutes before eating — they are very hot inside straight from the oven. Best eaten warm on the day they’re made, but excellent the next day toasted in a pan or oven for 3–4 minutes.

  • 150 g (1 cup) cherry tomatoes
  • 1 English cucumber, diced
  • 1 red bell pepper, diced
  • 80 g (½) red onion
  • 80 g (½ cup) kalamata olives
  • 1 can (400 g) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
  • Large handful fresh basil or parsley, roughly chopped
  • 80 ml (⅛ cup) extra virgin olive oil

  • 1 g (1 tsp) dried oregano

Equipment:

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cook the pasta: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta 1–2 minutes beyond al dente — slightly softer than you’d serve it hot. Pasta salad firms up as it cools and absorbs the dressing, so a little extra cook time prevents it from becoming tough and chewy once cold. Reserve ¼ cup of pasta water before draining.
  2. Rinse and cool the pasta: Drain the pasta and rinse immediately under cold running water until completely cooled. This stops the cooking, removes excess starch, and prevents the pasta from clumping together. Shake off as much water as possible and transfer to a large bowl.
  3. Make the dressing: In a small bowl or jar, combine the olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, garlic, oregano, maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Whisk vigorously or shake until emulsified and slightly creamy. Taste and adjust — more vinegar for tang, more maple syrup for balance, more salt to bring it all together.
  4. Dress the warm pasta: While the pasta is still slightly warm (not hot), pour about two-thirds of the dressing over it and toss well. Warm pasta absorbs dressing far better than cold pasta — this is the key to a flavourful salad rather than a dry one. Let sit for 5 minutes.
  5. Add the vegetables and chickpeas: Add the cherry tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, red onion, olives, and chickpeas to the dressed pasta. Toss everything together gently until evenly combined. If the red onion tastes sharp and harsh, soak the diced onion in cold water for 10 minutes first and drain before adding — this mellows the bite significantly.
  6. Chill and marinate: Pour the remaining dressing over the salad and toss again. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes — ideally 1–2 hours. This resting time is what transforms a good pasta salad into a great one: the flavours deepen, the vegetables soften slightly, and everything melds together.
  7. Finish and serve: Just before serving, taste and re-season — cold food often needs more salt and acid. Toss in the fresh basil or parsley. If the salad looks a little dry after chilling, drizzle with a splash of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon. Serve cold or at room temperature.

Ingredients:
• 300 g (2½ cups) all-purpose flour
  • 9.3 g (2 tsp) baking powder
  • 2.3 g (½ tsp) baking soda
  • 3 g (½ tsp) salt
  • 25 g (2 tbsp) sugar
  • 80 g (2.8 oz) cold vegan butter
  • 180 ml (¾ cup) cold non-dairy milk
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) apple cider vinegar
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 80 g (½ cup) dried currants or raisins
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) non-dairy milk
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) maple syrup
  • Vegan clotted cream or coconut cream
  • Strawberry jam
Equipment:
• Large mixing bowl
  • Small jug (for buttermilk)
  • Pastry cutter or fingertips (for rubbing butter)
  • Round scone cutter (6–7 cm) or sharp knife
  • Large baking sheet
  • Parchment paper
  • Pastry brush
  • Wire cooling rack
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Make the vegan buttermilk: Combine the cold non-dairy milk and apple cider vinegar in a small jug. Stir and set aside for 5 minutes until it curdles slightly into a buttermilk substitute. Keep it cold — put it back in the fridge if your kitchen is warm.
  2. Mix the dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar.
  3. Cut in the cold butter: Add the cold cubed vegan butter to the flour mixture. Using your fingertips, quickly rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter still visible. Work fast — the butter must stay cold. Those visible butter pieces are what create flaky, layered scones. If the butter starts to feel soft and greasy, refrigerate the bowl for 10 minutes before continuing.
  4. Add the wet ingredients: Add the vanilla extract to the cold buttermilk. Make a well in the centre of the flour mixture and pour in the buttermilk. Add the currants. Using a fork or your hands, mix until the dough just comes together — it should be shaggy, slightly sticky, and have a few dry streaks. Do not overmix. Overworked scone dough develops gluten and produces tough, dense scones.
  5. Shape the scones: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Gently pat and fold it over itself 2–3 times — this creates layers without overworking the gluten. Pat into a circle or rectangle about 3–4 cm thick. Using a sharp 6–7 cm round cutter, press straight down without twisting — twisting seals the edges and prevents the scones from rising properly. Gather the scraps, pat together once more, and cut remaining scones. You should get 8.
  6. Chill before baking: Place the cut scones on a parchment-lined baking sheet, spaced about 3 cm apart. Refrigerate for 15–20 minutes. This firms up the butter again after handling, which is the key to scones that rise tall with flaky layers rather than spreading flat.
  7. Glaze and bake: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Mix the non-dairy milk and maple syrup and brush generously over the tops of the chilled scones — don’t let the glaze drip down the sides as this inhibits rising. Bake for 16–18 minutes until risen, deeply golden on top, and the sides are set. They should look almost overdone on the outside — that’s correct.
  8. Cool and serve: Transfer to a wire rack and cool for at least 10 minutes before serving. Split open and serve warm with vegan clotted cream or coconut cream and strawberry jam.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Press and crumble the tofu: Wrap the tofu block in a clean kitchen towel or several layers of paper towels and press firmly for at least 10 minutes — place a heavy pan or book on top. The drier the tofu, the better it will brown. Once pressed, crumble it into a bowl with your hands into rough, uneven chunks about the size of minced meat. Uneven pieces create better texture than uniform crumbles.
  2. Mix the sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, hoisin sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sriracha, and maple syrup. Taste and adjust — more sriracha for heat, more hoisin for sweetness, more vinegar for brightness. Set aside.
  3. Brown the tofu: Heat the neutral oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the crumbled tofu in a single layer and cook without stirring for 3–4 minutes until deeply golden and caramelised on the bottom. Stir and cook for another 2–3 minutes until golden all over. The patience here pays off — properly browned tofu has a satisfying chew and holds the sauce better than pale, soft crumbles.
  4. Add the aromatics and vegetables: Push the tofu to the sides of the pan. Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onion whites to the centre and cook for 30–60 seconds until fragrant. Add the bell pepper and water chestnuts and stir everything together. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the pepper softens slightly but still has a little crunch.
  5. Add the sauce: Pour the sauce over the filling and toss to coat everything evenly. Cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring frequently, until the sauce reduces and glazes the filling. The mixture should look glossy and saucy but not soupy. Remove from heat.
  6. Prep the lettuce cups: Carefully separate the lettuce leaves, keeping them whole and cup-shaped. Rinse and pat dry. Butter lettuce gives the most elegant, pliable cups; iceberg is crunchier and holds up better if making ahead.
  7. Assemble and serve: Spoon the warm tofu filling generously into each lettuce cup. Top with toasted sesame seeds, spring onion greens, and an extra drizzle of sriracha or chili oil. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side — a squeeze of lime over the top brightens everything.

• 160 g (1 large) onion

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cook the vegetables: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook 4–5 minutes until soft. Add garlic, carrots, and celery and cook for 3–4 minutes. Add the potatoes, thyme, rosemary, soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
  2. Make the gravy: In a separate saucepan, melt the vegan butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1–2 minutes until it turns lightly golden and smells nutty — this is the roux. Gradually pour in the vegetable broth, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Add the oat milk and garlic powder and continue to whisk over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until the sauce thickens to a rich, creamy gravy. Season generously with salt and pepper.
  3. Combine the filling: Pour the gravy over the cooked vegetables. Add the frozen peas, frozen corn, and chickpeas. Stir everything together — the filling should be thick, creamy, and well-seasoned. Taste and adjust. Let cool for 10 minutes before topping with pastry — a very hot filling can make the pastry soggy.
  4. Assemble: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). If using a base crust, line the bottom of a large baking dish or 6 individual ramekins with one sheet of puff pastry, pressing it into the corners. Pour in the filling. Lay the second pastry sheet over the top, pressing and crimping the edges to seal. Score a few slits in the top to allow steam to escape. Brush generously with non-dairy milk for a golden, shiny finish.
  5. Bake: Bake for 35–40 minutes until the pastry is deeply golden, puffed, and flaky. The filling should be bubbling at the edges. If the pastry browns too quickly, tent loosely with foil for the last 10 minutes.
  6. Rest and serve: Let rest for 5–10 minutes before serving — the filling will be extremely hot and needs time to set slightly. Serve with a simple green salad or steamed greens on the side.

Name: Pickled Red Onion

Ingredients:

  • 240 ml (1 cup) apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar

Equipment:
• Sharp knife or mandoline
  • 500 ml glass jar with lid
  • Small saucepan

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Slice the onions: Peel and thinly slice the red onions into rings or half-moons, as uniformly as possible. A mandoline gives the most even slices, but a sharp knife works perfectly. Pack the sliced onions tightly into a clean 500 ml jar.
  2. Make the brine: In a small saucepan, combine the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, peppercorns, and oregano. Heat over medium heat, stirring, until the sugar and salt fully dissolve — about 2–3 minutes. You don’t need to bring it to a full boil.
  3. Pour and press: Carefully pour the hot brine over the onions in the jar. Use a spoon or chopstick to press the onions down so they’re fully submerged. They will initially float — they’ll sink and soften within 20–30 minutes as the jar cools.
  4. Cool and refrigerate: Let the jar cool to room temperature with the lid off (about 30 minutes). Once cool, seal the jar and refrigerate. The onions will be lightly pickled and ready to eat in as little as 30 minutes, but are best after 1–2 hours and even better the next day when they turn a vivid magenta pink.

1. Make the tomato sauce: Heat olive oil in a large, wide oven-safe skillet or pan over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 5–6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the cumin, smoked paprika, sweet paprika, turmeric, and chili flakes and stir for 1 minute until the spices bloom in the oil and become fragrant.
  2. Add tomatoes and chickpeas: Pour in the crushed tomatoes, sugar, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine and simmer over medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes until the sauce thickens and deepens in colour. Add the chickpeas and stir through. Taste and adjust seasoning — the sauce should be bold, spiced, and slightly sweet.
  3. Prepare the tofu “eggs”: While the sauce simmers, drain the silken tofu and cut or scoop into rough oval shapes about the size of a cracked egg — don’t make them too perfect. Place in a bowl and gently toss with nutritional yeast, black salt, turmeric, and garlic powder. Handle gently as silken tofu is very delicate.

  5. Cover and cook: Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan with a lid and cook for 8–10 minutes until the tofu is heated through and has absorbed some of the surrounding sauce. The tofu should look set and lightly glazed.
  6. Finish and serve: Remove the lid. Scatter generously with fresh parsley or cilantro and crumbled vegan feta if using. Bring the pan directly to the table and serve immediately with warm pita or crusty bread for scooping.

Name: Freeze-Dried Strawberry Chia Pudding

Ingredients:
• 1 pack freeze-dried strawberries (such as Crispy Green)
  • 3 tbsp chia seeds
  • ½ cup dairy-free yogurt (plain or vanilla)
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup
  • 240 ml (1 cup) dairy-free milk

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Mix the base: In a bowl or jar, whisk together the dairy-free milk, dairy-free yogurt, and maple syrup until completely smooth. The yogurt adds creaminess and a slight tang that balances the sweetness of the strawberries and maple — don’t skip it.
  2. Add chia seeds and strawberries: Stir in the chia seeds and freeze-dried strawberries. The freeze-dried strawberries will begin to rehydrate in the liquid, releasing an intensely concentrated strawberry flavour and turning the pudding a beautiful deep pink. Give everything a thorough stir to distribute evenly.
  3. Rest and stir again: Let the mixture sit at room temperature for 5 minutes, then stir again vigorously. This second stir is important — chia seeds clump together quickly as they begin to gel, and breaking them up now ensures an even, smooth pudding rather than a clumpy one.

Name: Kale and Avocado Salad
Common Ingredients: avocado; lemon; kale; red-onion; maple-syrup; salt; olive-oil
Ingredients:
• 1 large bunch kale (curly or lacinato/Tuscan), stems removed and leaves torn into bite-sized pieces
  • 2 ripe avocados, diced or sliced
  • 80 g (½) red onion
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) fresh lemon juice
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) maple syrup
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) extra virgin olive oil
  • Salt and pepper to taste
Equipment:
• Large mixing bowl
  • Small bowl (for dressing)
  • Whisk or fork
  • Sharp knife and cutting board
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Massage the kale: Place the torn kale leaves in a large bowl. Drizzle with a small pinch of salt and a tiny splash of the lemon juice. Using both hands, massage the kale firmly for 1–2 minutes, scrunching and squeezing the leaves until they soften, darken, and reduce in volume by about half. This breaks down the tough fibres, removes the bitterness, and transforms raw kale from chewy and harsh into silky and tender — it’s the single most important step in a kale salad.
  2. Make the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper until emulsified. Taste — it should be bright, slightly sweet, and well-seasoned. Adjust with more lemon for tang or more maple syrup for balance.
  3. Assemble and toss: Add the avocado and red onion to the massaged kale. Pour the dressing over the top and toss gently to coat every bite — be careful not to mash the avocado. The avocado will naturally cling to the kale and create an even creamier dressing as you toss.
  4. Serve immediately: Serve right away for the freshest flavour and the best avocado texture. The massaged kale holds up well for hours, but the avocado will begin to brown if it sits too long.

Name: Homemade Potato Chips
Features: refined-sugar-free; gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; nut-free; leftover-friendly

Ingredients:
• 4 large russet potatoes, scrubbed clean
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil or vegetable oil
  • 6 g (1 tsp) fine sea salt
  • 1.5 g (½ tsp) garlic powder
  • 1.2 g (½ tsp) smoked paprika
  • Freshly ground black pepper to taste
Equipment:
• Mandoline slicer (recommended) or sharp knife
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Paper towels
  • 2 large baking sheets
  • Parchment paper
  • Wire cooling rack
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Slice the potatoes: Using a mandoline or sharp knife, slice the potatoes paper-thin (about 1/16 inch). Uniform slices are key for even cooking.
  2. Soak & dry: Place slices in a large bowl of cold water and soak for 30 minutes to remove excess starch. Drain well and pat completely dry with paper towels — this is essential for crispiness.
  3. Season: Toss the dried potato slices with oil, salt, garlic powder, and smoked paprika until evenly coated.
  4. Bake: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Arrange slices in a single layer on parchment-lined baking sheets. Bake for 15–20 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp. Watch closely toward the end — they go from golden to burnt quickly.
  5. Cool & serve: Transfer chips to a wire rack. They will crisp up further as they cool. Season with extra salt if desired and serve immediately.

Tips: The thinner the slice, the crispier the chip. A mandoline is highly recommended. Make sure slices are bone-dry before baking — any moisture = soggy chips.

Name: Chocolate Chip Pancakes

Instruction Rich Text:

  3. Combine: Pour wet ingredients into dry and stir until just combined — lumps are fine. Fold in chocolate chips. Do not overmix.
  4. Cook: Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat and lightly grease with vegan butter or oil. Pour ¼ cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form on the surface and edges look set, about 2–3 minutes. Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more.
  5. Serve: Stack and serve warm with maple syrup, extra chocolate chips, or coconut whipped cream.

Name: Banana Cream Pie
Common Ingredients: plant-milk; banana; vegan-butter; sugar; vanilla-extract; coconut-cream; graham-crackers; powdered-sugar; cornstarch-0db33; turmeric-95970
Ingredients:
• Crust:
  • 150 g (1½ cups) graham cracker crumbs
  • 66.7 g (⅓ cup) granulated sugar
  • 6 tbsp vegan butter, melted
  • Pastry Cream:
  • 480 ml (2 cups) unsweetened plant milk
  • 100 g (½ cup) granulated sugar
  • 40 g (5 tbsp) cornstarch
  • Pinch of turmeric (for color, optional)
  • 2 tbsp vegan butter
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • Assembly:
  • 3 ripe bananas, sliced
  • 360 ml (1½ cups) full-fat coconut cream
  • 37.5 g (3 tbsp) powdered sugar
Equipment:
• 9-inch pie dish
  • Medium saucepan
  • Mixing bowls
  • Whisk
  • Hand or stand mixer
  • Plastic wrap
  • Spatula
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Make the crust: Mix graham cracker crumbs, sugar, and melted vegan butter. Press firmly into a 9-inch pie dish. Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 8 minutes. Cool completely.
  2. Make pastry cream: Whisk sugar, cornstarch, and turmeric (if using) in a saucepan. Gradually whisk in the plant milk until smooth. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened, about 5-6 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the vegan butter and vanilla. Press plastic wrap directly onto the surface and refrigerate until cold, about 2 hours.
  3. Assemble: Spread half the pastry cream in the cooled crust. Layer banana slices on top. Spread remaining pastry cream over bananas.
  4. Whip cream: Beat the chilled coconut cream and powdered sugar until light and fluffy. Spread or pipe over the pie.
  5. Chill: Refrigerate at least 2 hours before slicing. Top with extra banana slices just before serving.

Storage: Cover and refrigerate up to 3 days. Add fresh banana slices and whipped cream just before serving to prevent browning.

Tips: Brush banana slices with a little lemon juice to slow browning. Use very ripe but still firm bananas for best flavor and texture.

Swaps: Use a pre-made pie crust or vanilla wafer crust for a shortcut. Coconut whipped cream is a great dairy-free topping.

Ingredients:
• 1360.8 g (3 lbs) Yukon Gold potatoes
  • 6 tbsp vegan butter, cut into pieces
  • 180 ml (¾ cup) unsweetened plant milk
  • 9 g (1½ tsp) fine salt
  • 1 g (½ tsp) white pepper or black pepper
  • 6 g (2 cloves) garlic
  • Fresh chives or parsley for garnish
Equipment:
• Large pot
  • Colander
  • Potato masher or ricer
  • Wooden spoon or spatula
  • Small saucepan (to warm milk)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Boil potatoes: Place cubed potatoes (and garlic if using) in a large pot. Cover with cold, well-salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until very tender and easily pierced with a fork, about 15–18 minutes.
  2. Drain and dry: Drain thoroughly. Return potatoes to the hot pot and let sit over low heat for 1–2 minutes to evaporate excess moisture.
  3. Mash: Use a potato masher or ricer for best texture. Mash until smooth.
  4. Add butter and milk: Stir in the vegan butter until melted, then add the warm plant milk gradually, mixing until you reach desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
  5. Serve: Transfer to a serving bowl, top with a pat of vegan butter and fresh herbs.

Storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 4 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop with a splash of milk, stirring frequently.

Name: Sweet Potato Tater Tots
Common Ingredients: sweet-potato; all-purpose-flour; onion; salt; olive-oil; garlic-powder; smoked-paprika; black-pepper; cornstarch-0db33
Ingredients:
• 907.2 g (2 lbs) sweet potatoes
  • 24 g (3 tbsp) all-purpose flour
  • 3 g (1 tsp) garlic powder
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) smoked paprika
  • 1.2 g (½ tsp) onion powder
  • 4.5 g (¾ tsp) fine salt
  • 0.5 g (¼ tsp) black pepper
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil or oil for frying
Equipment:
• Large pot
  • Box grater
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Baking sheet
  • Parchment paper
  • Measuring spoons
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Par-cook the sweet potatoes: Peel and halve the sweet potatoes. Boil in salted water for 8–10 minutes until just barely tender — not fully cooked. Drain and let cool completely.
  2. Grate: Using the large holes of a box grater, grate the par-cooked sweet potatoes into a large bowl.
  3. Mix: Add flour, garlic powder, paprika, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until combined.
  4. Shape: Scoop about 1 tablespoon of mixture and roll into a small cylinder (tot shape) between your palms. Repeat with all the mixture.
  5. Bake: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Place tots on an oiled baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil. Bake 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp on the outside.
  6. Serve: Serve hot with dipping sauces like chipotle mayo, ketchup, or ranch.

Swaps: Add a pinch of cinnamon and cayenne for a sweet-heat flavor profile. Can also be made in an air fryer at 400°F for 12–15 minutes.

Storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in the oven or air fryer for best crispiness — avoid the microwave.

  • 165 g (¾ cup) vegan mayonnaise
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) apple cider vinegar
  • 15 g (1 tbsp) yellow mustard
  • 8.3 g (2 tsp) granulated sugar

Instruction Rich Text:

  3. Combine: Add cooled macaroni, celery, red onion, bell pepper, and parsley to the dressing. Fold gently to coat everything evenly.
  4. Chill: Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving to allow flavors to meld. Stir and taste for seasoning before serving.
  5. Serve: Serve cold, garnished with a sprinkle of paprika and extra parsley if desired.

Name: Onion Dip
Features: gluten-free; meal-prep-friendly; grain-free; soy-free; nut-free; leftover-friendly
Common Ingredients: vegan-butter; onion; salt; olive-oil; mayonnaise; cream-cheese; garlic-powder; sugar; black-pepper; vegan-sour-cream; chives-c5cdb; vegan-worcestershire-sauce-2cb32
Ingredients:
• 2 large yellow onions, thinly sliced
  • 2 tbsp vegan butter
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • ½ tsp salt
  • ¼ tsp black pepper
  • ¼ tsp sugar (helps caramelization)
  • 1 cup vegan sour cream
  • ½ cup vegan cream cheese, softened
  • ¼ cup vegan mayonnaise
  • 1 tsp vegan Worcestershire sauce
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • Fresh chives for garnish
Equipment:
• Large skillet
  • Mixing bowl
  • Hand mixer or wooden spoon
  • Knife and cutting board
  • Spatula
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Caramelize the onions: Melt vegan butter with olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add onions, salt, pepper, and sugar. Cook slowly, stirring every 5–10 minutes, for 35–40 minutes until deep golden brown and jammy. Do not rush this step — low and slow is key.
  2. Cool the onions: Remove from heat and let onions cool to room temperature. Chop roughly if desired.
  3. Make the base: Beat together vegan sour cream, vegan cream cheese, vegan mayonnaise, vegan Worcestershire sauce, and garlic powder until smooth and creamy.

1. Prep the base: Pat chickpeas dry with paper towels and spread on a baking sheet. Roast at 400°F (200°C) for 10 minutes to dry them out — this prevents soggy meatballs. Let cool slightly.
  2. Blend: Add chickpeas to a food processor and pulse 8–10 times until roughly chopped (not a paste — you want some texture). Transfer to a large bowl.

Ingredients:
• 680.4 g (1½ lbs) fresh green beans
  • 3 tbsp vegan butter
  • 160 g (1 medium) yellow onion
  • 9 g (3 cloves) garlic
  • 226.8 g (8 oz) cremini mushrooms
  • 24 g (3 tbsp) all-purpose flour
  • 360 ml (1½ cups) vegetable broth
  • 240 ml (1 cup) unsweetened plant milk
  • 120 ml (½ cup) vegan sour cream
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) soy sauce
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt
  • 1 g (½ tsp) black pepper
  • 0.6 g (¼ tsp) nutmeg
  • 240 g (1½ cups) crispy fried onions

Equipment:
• Large pot
  • Large oven-safe skillet or 9x13 baking dish

  • Bowl of ice water

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Blanch the green beans: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans and cook for 4–5 minutes until bright green and just tender. Drain and transfer immediately to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain again and pat dry.
  2. Make the mushroom sauce: Melt vegan butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and mushrooms and cook 6–8 minutes until mushrooms are golden and liquid has evaporated.
  3. Build the sauce: Sprinkle flour over the mushroom mixture and stir to coat. Cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in broth, then plant milk, stirring constantly. Simmer 3–4 minutes until thickened. Remove from heat and stir in vegan sour cream, soy sauce, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
  4. Combine: Fold green beans and ¾ cup fried onions into the sauce. If your skillet is oven-safe, keep it in the pan. Otherwise, transfer to a greased 9x13-inch baking dish.
  5. Bake: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Top with remaining ¾ cup fried onions and vegan cheddar if using. Bake uncovered for 25–30 minutes until bubbly and the top is golden brown.
  6. Rest and serve: Let sit 5 minutes before serving.

Name: Cauliflower Rice

Common Ingredients: cauliflower; garlic; cilantro; parsley; lemon; vegan-butter; salt; olive-oil; black-pepper
Ingredients:
• 1 large head cauliflower (about 2 lbs), cut into florets
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil or vegan butter
  • 9 g (3 cloves) garlic
  • 3 g (½ tsp) fine salt
  • 0.5 g (¼ tsp) black pepper
  • 2 tbsp fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped
  • Juice of ½ lemon (optional)
Equipment:
• Food processor or box grater
  • Clean kitchen towel or paper towels
  • Large skillet
  • Spatula
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Rice the cauliflower: Working in batches, pulse cauliflower florets in a food processor 8–10 times until they resemble rice grains. Do not over-process into mush. Alternatively, grate florets on the large holes of a box grater.
  2. Remove moisture: Transfer riced cauliflower to a clean kitchen towel or paper towels and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. This step is critical for fluffy, non-soggy rice.
  3. Cook: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add cauliflower rice in an even layer and cook undisturbed for 2 minutes to get a little color, then stir and cook another 3–4 minutes until tender and lightly golden.
  4. Season: Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat and stir in fresh herbs and a squeeze of lemon juice if using.
  5. Serve: Use immediately as a base for bowls, stir-fries, curries, or alongside any protein.

Swaps: Use frozen riced cauliflower as a shortcut — thaw and squeeze dry before cooking. Add coconut oil and a pinch of turmeric for a golden rice variation.

  3. Add the beans and lentils: Add black beans and lentils. Use a fork or the back of a spoon to lightly mash about half the mixture — you want a chunky, meaty texture, not a paste.

Name: Onion Rings

Ingredients:
• 320 g (2 large) yellow onions
  • 120 g (1 cup) all-purpose flour
  • 4.7 g (1 tsp) baking powder
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) smoked paprika
  • 3 g (1 tsp) garlic powder
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) onion powder
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt
  • 1 g (½ tsp) black pepper
  • ½ tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
  • 240 ml (1 cup) unsweetened plant milk + 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
  • 3 tbsp aquafaba (liquid from a can of chickpeas)
  • 162 g (1½ cups) panko breadcrumbs
  • Vegetable or canola oil for frying (about 4 cups)
  • Flaky sea salt for finishing
Equipment:
• Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven
  • Deep-fry or candy thermometer
  • 4 shallow bowls (for dredging station)
  • Wire rack over a baking sheet
  • Spider strainer or slotted spoon
  • Paper towels
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the onions: Slice onions into ½-inch rings and separate into individual rings. Pat dry with paper towels. Discard the very small inner rings or save for another use.
  2. Set up the dredging station: In a shallow bowl, combine ½ cup flour with salt and pepper. In a second bowl, whisk the vegan buttermilk and aquafaba together. In a third bowl, combine remaining ½ cup flour, baking powder, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne. In a fourth bowl, add panko breadcrumbs.
  3. Dredge: Working one ring at a time, coat in plain flour (shake off excess), dip in the buttermilk mixture, coat in seasoned flour, dip in the buttermilk mixture again, then press firmly into panko breadcrumbs. This double-dip gives an ultra-crispy crust. Place on a wire rack.
  4. Heat the oil: Pour oil into a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to a depth of 2–3 inches. Heat to 375°F (190°C) over medium-high heat. Use a thermometer for best results.

Name: Banana Nut Muffins
Common Ingredients: flax-egg; all-purpose-flour; banana; vegan-butter; walnuts; yogurt; salt; sugar; cinnamon; vanilla-extract; pecans; nutmeg; brown-sugar; baking-soda; baking-powder-3e21e
Ingredients:
• 3 very ripe bananas, mashed (about 1½ cups)
  • 210 g (1¾ cups) all-purpose flour
  • 150 g (¾ cup) granulated sugar
  • 4.7 g (1 tsp) baking soda
  • 2.3 g (½ tsp) baking powder
  • 3 g (½ tsp) fine salt
  • 2.7 g (1 tsp) ground cinnamon
  • 0.6 g (¼ tsp) ground nutmeg
  • 30 g (2) flax eggs
  • 113.5 g (½ cup) vegan butter
  • ¼ cup unsweetened coconut yogurt
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 100 g (1 cup) walnuts or pecans
  • 26.6 g (2 tbsp) brown sugar
Equipment:
• 12-cup muffin tin
  • Paper liners or non-stick spray
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Fork or potato masher
  • Whisk
  • Spatula
  • Wire cooling rack
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or grease well.
  2. Mash bananas: In a large bowl, mash bananas until mostly smooth. A few small lumps are fine and add texture.
  3. Mix wet ingredients: Whisk flax eggs, melted vegan butter, coconut yogurt, and vanilla into the mashed bananas until well combined.
  4. Add dry ingredients: Add flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg directly to the wet mixture. Fold gently until just combined — do not overmix. A few streaks of flour are okay.
  5. Fold in nuts: Gently fold in ¾ of the chopped walnuts, reserving the rest for topping.
  6. Fill and top: Divide batter evenly among the muffin cups, filling each about ¾ full. Sprinkle remaining walnuts and a pinch of brown sugar over each muffin.
  7. Bake: Bake 20–22 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean and the tops are domed and golden. Do not overbake.
  8. Cool: Let muffins cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.

Name: Salsa
Common Ingredients: garlic; cilantro; lime; tomatoes; jalapeno; onion; salt; cumin; sugar
Ingredients:
• 6 roma tomatoes, quartered (or 1 can 28 oz whole peeled tomatoes, drained)
  • 1 small white onion, roughly chopped
  • 9 g (3 cloves) garlic
  • 1–2 jalapeños, seeds removed for mild or kept for hot
  • ½ cup fresh cilantro, loosely packed
  • Juice of 2 limes
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt
  • 1 g (½ tsp) cumin
  • 1 g (¼ tsp) sugar
Equipment:
• Blender or food processor
  • Dry skillet or broiler pan (optional, for charring)
  • Knife and cutting board
  • Serving bowl
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Char for depth (optional but recommended): Place tomatoes, onion, garlic, and jalapeños on a dry skillet or under the broiler on high for 5–7 minutes, turning once, until lightly blackened in spots. This adds a smoky, roasted depth to the salsa. Skip this step for a fresh, bright salsa.
  2. Blend: Add all ingredients to a blender or food processor. Pulse 8–12 times for a chunky salsa, or blend 20–30 seconds for a smoother restaurant-style salsa.
  3. Taste and adjust: Taste and add more salt, lime juice, or jalapeño as needed. If too acidic, add the pinch of sugar.
  4. Rest: Transfer to a bowl and let sit at room temperature for 15–20 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.
  5. Serve: Serve with tortilla chips, over tacos, eggs, grilled meats, or burrito bowls.

Name: Naan (Vegan)
Common Ingredients: garlic; cilantro; parsley; all-purpose-flour; vegan-butter; yogurt; salt; olive-oil; sugar; coconut-oil; active-dry-yeast-2541b; baking-powder-3e21e
Ingredients:
• 2¼ tsp active dry yeast (1 packet)
  • 4.2 g (1 tsp) sugar
  • 180 ml (¾ cup) warm water
  • 300 g (2½ cups) all-purpose flour
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt
  • 2.3 g (½ tsp) baking powder
  • ½ cup full-fat coconut yogurt (or plain vegan yogurt)
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil or melted coconut oil
  • Garlic Butter Topping:
  • 3 tbsp vegan butter, melted
  • 9 g (3 cloves) garlic
  • 2 tbsp fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped
  • Flaky sea salt for finishing
Equipment:
• Large mixing bowl
  • Small bowl (for yeast)
  • Cast iron skillet or heavy pan
  • Rolling pin
  • Pastry brush
  • Clean kitchen towel or plastic wrap
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Activate the yeast: Combine warm water, sugar, and yeast in a small bowl. Stir and let sit 5–10 minutes until foamy. If it doesn’t foam, your yeast is dead — start over with fresh yeast.
  2. Make the dough: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, salt, and baking powder. Add the yeast mixture, coconut yogurt, and olive oil. Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then turn out onto a floured surface and knead for 5–6 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky. Add flour 1 tbsp at a time if too sticky.
  3. First rise: Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp towel or plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled in size.
  4. Divide and roll: Punch down the dough and divide into 8 equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each piece into an oval about ⅛-inch thick.
  5. Cook: Heat a cast iron skillet or heavy pan over high heat until very hot — no oil needed. Cook naan one at a time for 1–2 minutes per side until large bubbles form and dark char spots appear. The char is what gives naan its signature flavor.
  6. Finish: Mix melted vegan butter with garlic. Brush each naan immediately while hot. Sprinkle with fresh cilantro and flaky salt.
  7. Serve: Serve warm alongside curries, soups, or use as a flatbread base for toppings.

• 150 g (1 cup) hemp seeds
  • 138 g (1 cup) pumpkin seeds
  • 70 g (½ cup) sunflower seeds
  • 84 g (½ cup) chia seeds
  • ¼ cup ground flaxseed
  • 15 g (¼ cup) nutritional yeast

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Toast the seeds (optional but recommended): Spread hemp seeds, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds on a dry skillet over medium heat. Toast 3–4 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly golden. This deepens the flavor significantly. Let cool completely before blending.
  2. Blend: Add all ingredients to a high-speed blender or food processor. Blend on high for 30–60 seconds until you reach a fine, flour-like powder. Do not over-blend or the seeds will release their oils and turn into butter.
  3. Sift (optional): Pass through a fine mesh sieve to remove any larger pieces. Return any chunks to the blender and pulse again.
  4. Taste and adjust: Taste the powder and adjust — add more cacao for a richer chocolate flavor, more vanilla for sweetness, or a pinch more salt to enhance overall flavor.
  5. Store: Transfer to an airtight glass jar or container. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 months, or freeze for up to 6 months. Always use a dry spoon to scoop.

Name: Sour Green Grape Roll-Ups
Common Ingredients: lemon; grapes; sugar; citric-acid-9e362
Ingredients:
• 4 cups green seedless grapes, stems removed
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) lemon juice
  • ¼ tsp citric acid
  • 0.5 g (⅛ tsp) caster sugar
Equipment:
• Blender
  • Parchment-lined baking sheet
  • Offset spatula
  • Oven or dehydrator
  • Scissors or pizza cutter
  • Small bowl (for sour coating)
  • Airtight container
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Blend: Add grapes and lemon juice to a blender. Blend until completely smooth with no chunks remaining.
  2. Spread: Pour the mixture onto a parchment-lined baking sheet and spread evenly to about ⅛-inch thickness. Use an offset spatula to get an even layer — thin and consistent is key for uniform drying.
  3. Dry: Oven method: Bake at 140–170°F (60–75°C) for 4–8 hours. Dehydrator method: Set to 135°F (57°C) for 6–10 hours. The roll-up is ready when it is dry to the touch but still flexible and peels cleanly off the parchment.
  4. Sour candy finish: Mix the caster sugar and citric acid together in a small bowl. Once the roll-up has cooled, lightly dust or press the mixture onto the surface for a sweet-tart, candy-style coating.
  5. Peel and cut: Peel the roll-up off the parchment and cut into strips using scissors or a pizza cutter.
  6. Store: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week. Place parchment between layers to prevent sticking.

Name: Quinoa Cookies (Vegan)
Common Ingredients: quinoa; oats; peanut-butter; chocolate-chips; maple-syrup; pumpkin-seeds-2; sunflower-seeds-2; almond-butter-2; salt; sugar; cinnamon; vanilla-extract; coconut-oil; brown-sugar; baking-soda
Ingredients:
• 170 g (1 cup) cooked quinoa
  • 135 g (1½ cups) rolled oats
  • 192 g (¾ cup) almond butter
  • 120 ml (½ cup) maple syrup
  • 40 g (¼ cup) coconut sugar
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) coconut oil
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 2.7 g (1 tsp) ground cinnamon
  • 2.3 g (½ tsp) baking soda
  • 1.5 g (¼ tsp) fine salt
  • 85 g (½ cup) dark chocolate chips
  • 35 g (¼ cup) pumpkin seeds or sunflower seeds
Equipment:
• 2 baking sheets
  • Parchment paper
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Cookie scoop or tablespoon
  • Wire cooling rack
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. Mix wet ingredients: In a large bowl, stir together almond butter, maple syrup, coconut sugar, melted coconut oil, and vanilla until smooth and well combined.
  3. Add dry ingredients: Stir in the rolled oats, cooked quinoa, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt. Mix until a thick, cohesive dough forms.
  4. Fold in mix-ins: Fold in the chocolate chips and seeds if using. The dough will be thick and slightly sticky — that’s perfect.
  5. Scoop and flatten: Scoop about 1½ tablespoons of dough per cookie, roll into a ball, place on the prepared baking sheet, and press down gently to about ½-inch thickness. These cookies don’t spread much on their own.
  6. Bake: Bake 11–13 minutes until the edges are golden and set. The centers may look slightly underdone — that’s fine; they firm up as they cool.
  7. Cool: Let cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. They need to cool fully to reach their best texture.

Name: Pistachio Milk

Ingredients:
• 1 cup raw unsalted pistachios
  • 960 ml (4 cups) filtered water
  • 2 Medjool dates, pitted (or 1 tbsp maple syrup)
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract

Equipment:

  • Large bowl or pitcher

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Soak the pistachios: Place pistachios in a bowl and cover with cold water. Soak for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge. Soaking softens the nuts for smoother blending and a creamier milk. Drain and rinse well.
  2. Blend: Add the soaked pistachios, 4 cups of fresh filtered water, dates, vanilla, and salt to a high-speed blender. Blend on high for 60–90 seconds until completely smooth and creamy.
  3. Strain: Pour the blended mixture through a nut milk bag, fine mesh sieve, or cheesecloth into a large bowl or pitcher. Squeeze or press to extract as much liquid as possible. For a thicker, creamier milk, skip straining entirely.
  4. Taste and adjust: Taste and adjust sweetness with more dates or maple syrup, or add more vanilla if desired.
  5. Store: Pour into a sealed glass bottle or jar. Refrigerate for up to 4–5 days. Shake or stir well before each use as it will naturally separate.

Name: Heavy Cream (Vegan)
Features: gluten-free; meal-prep-friendly; raw; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; nut-free
Common Ingredients: vanilla-extract; coconut-cream; powdered-sugar
Ingredients:
• 1 can (400ml / 13.5 oz) full-fat coconut cream
  • 25 g (2 tbsp) powdered sugar
  • ½ tsp vanilla extract (optional)
Equipment:
• 1 can full-fat coconut cream (refrigerated overnight)
  • Cold mixing bowl
  • Hand mixer or stand mixer (for whipped cream)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Chill the coconut cream: Refrigerate the can of full-fat coconut cream overnight, or for at least 6–8 hours. Do not shake the can. The cream will solidify and separate from the liquid at the bottom — this separation is what you need.
  2. For pouring cream: Open the can and gently stir. Use the thick coconut cream as a 1:1 substitute for heavy cream in soups, sauces, curries, pasta, or any savory recipe. Use it straight from the can without whipping.
  3. For whipped cream: Open the chilled can and scoop out only the solid white cream into a cold mixing bowl, leaving the liquid behind. Add powdered sugar and vanilla if using. Beat with a hand mixer or stand mixer on high for 2–3 minutes until light, fluffy, and stiff peaks form.
  4. Use or store: Use immediately as whipped cream, or refrigerate the thick cream for up to 5 days. The whipped version is best used the same day but will keep in the fridge for 1–2 days.

Best brands: Look for cans that list coconut cream or coconut extract as the first ingredient with no added stabilizers or gums — these whip the best.

Name: Nacho Salad
Common Ingredients: avocado; black-beans; corn; cilantro; lettuce; lime; red-onion; tortilla; tomatoes; jalapeno; cashews; maple-syrup; chipotle-peppers-in-adobe-sauce; salt; cumin; garlic-powder; smoked-paprika; chili-powder; vegan-sour-cream
Ingredients:
• 4 cups romaine lettuce, roughly chopped
  • 425.2 g (1 (15 oz) can) black beans
  • 165 g (1 cup) corn kernels
  • 200 g (1) avocado
  • 150 g (1 cup) cherry tomatoes
  • ½ red onion, thinly sliced
  • ¼ cup fresh cilantro, roughly chopped
  • 14 g (1) jalapeño
  • 2 big handfuls tortilla chips, lightly crushed
  • Seasoned Beans:
  • 2 g (1 tsp) cumin
  • Chipotle Lime Dressing:
  • ⅓ cup vegan sour cream or cashew cream
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) lime juice
  • 1 chipotle pepper in adobo, minced
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) maple syrup
  • ¼ tsp garlic powder, ¼ tsp salt
  • 1–2 tbsp water to thin
Equipment:
• Small saucepan (for beans)
  • Dry skillet (for corn)
  • Small bowl and whisk (for dressing)
  • Large salad bowl or platter
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Season the beans: Warm black beans in a small saucepan over medium heat with cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, chili powder, and salt. Cook 3–4 minutes, stirring, until the beans are fragrant and coated in the spices. Set aside.
  2. Char the corn: Heat a dry skillet over high heat. Add the corn and cook undisturbed for 2–3 minutes until charred in spots. Season with a pinch of salt. This smoky step adds serious depth to the salad.
  3. Make the dressing: Whisk together the vegan sour cream, lime juice, minced chipotle, maple syrup, garlic powder, and salt. Add water 1 tbsp at a time until you reach a pourable, creamy consistency. Taste and adjust — more lime for brightness, more chipotle for heat.
  4. Assemble: Add the romaine to a large bowl or platter. Top with seasoned beans, charred corn, avocado, cherry tomatoes, red onion, cilantro, and jalapeño.
  5. Add chips and dress: Scatter the crushed tortilla chips over the top. Drizzle with the chipotle lime dressing just before serving so the chips stay crunchy.
  6. Serve immediately: Toss lightly and serve right away. If prepping ahead, keep the chips and dressing separate until the last minute.

Common Ingredients: garlic; cilantro; parsley; quinoa; salt; vegetable-broth; olive-oil; basmati-rice; black-pepper
Ingredients:
• ¾ cup white or brown basmati rice, rinsed
  • ¾ cup white or tri-color quinoa, rinsed
  • 2¼ cups vegetable broth or water
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil
  • 6 g (2 cloves) garlic
  • ½ tsp fine salt (adjust if using salted broth)
  • ¼ tsp black pepper
  • 2 tbsp fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (for serving)
Equipment:
• Medium saucepan with tight-fitting lid
  • Fine mesh sieve (for rinsing)
  • Fork

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Rinse both grains: Rinse the rice and quinoa separately under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes excess starch from the rice and saponins from the quinoa (the natural coating that can make it taste bitter). Drain well.
  2. Toast the grains: Heat olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the rinsed rice and quinoa and toast, stirring frequently, for 2–3 minutes until the grains smell nutty and lightly golden. This step adds a wonderful depth of flavor.
  3. Add liquid and cook: Pour in the vegetable broth, add salt and pepper, and stir to combine. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 18–20 minutes until all the liquid is absorbed and the grains are tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
  4. Rest: Remove from heat and let sit, still covered, for 5 minutes. This allows the steam to finish cooking the grains and prevents the bottom from getting soggy.
  5. Fluff and serve: Uncover and fluff gently with a fork. Stir in fresh herbs and taste for seasoning. Serve as a side dish, base for bowls, or use anywhere you would use plain rice.

Features: refined-sugar-free; gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; meal-prep-friendly; leftover-friendly
Common Ingredients: garlic; lemon; red-pepper; spinach; nutritional-yeast; cashews; onion; salt; olive-oil; artichoke; black-pepper; vegan-parmesan
Ingredients:
• 60 g (2 cups) fresh baby spinach
  • 396.9 g (1 (14 oz) can) artichoke hearts
  • 1½ cups raw cashews, soaked 4 hours or boiled 15 min
  • ¾ cup water
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) lemon juice
  • 9 g (3 cloves) garlic
  • ½ small onion, finely diced
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil
  • 15 g (3 tbsp) nutritional yeast
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) onion powder
  • ½ tsp salt
  • ¼ tsp black pepper
  • ½ tsp red pepper flakes (optional)
  • ¼ cup vegan parmesan or extra nutritional yeast, for topping
Equipment:
• Skillet
  • High-speed blender
  • Small baking dish or cast iron skillet
  • Bowl for soaking cashews
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a small baking dish or cast iron skillet.
  2. Sauté aromatics: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook 4–5 minutes until soft. Add garlic and cook 1 more minute. Remove from heat.
  3. Wilt the spinach: Add spinach to the pan and stir over medium heat 1–2 minutes until just wilted. Set aside.
  4. Blend the base: Drain the soaked cashews. Add to a high-speed blender with water, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, onion powder, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes. Blend 60–90 seconds until completely smooth and creamy.
  5. Combine: Transfer the cashew cream to a large bowl. Stir in the sautéed onion and garlic, wilted spinach, and chopped artichoke hearts. Mix well to combine evenly.
  6. Bake: Spread the mixture into the prepared baking dish. Top with vegan parmesan or extra nutritional yeast. Bake 20–25 minutes until the top is golden and the edges are bubbling.
  7. Serve: Serve hot straight from the oven with tortilla chips, pita, sourdough, or sliced baguette.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cook the edamame: If using frozen edamame, thaw completely and pat dry. If using fresh, cook in salted boiling water for 3–4 minutes, then drain and cool. Reserve a few whole edamame beans for topping.
  2. Blend: Add the edamame, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin, and salt to a food processor or high-speed blender. Blend on high for 60–90 seconds, scraping down the sides as needed.
  3. Adjust consistency: Add cold water 1 tablespoon at a time and blend again until you reach a smooth, creamy hummus consistency. The cold water makes it fluffier and lighter.
  4. Taste and adjust: Taste and add more lemon juice for brightness, salt for depth, or garlic for bite. Blend again briefly.
  5. Serve: Transfer to a serving bowl. Use the back of a spoon to create a well in the center. Drizzle generously with olive oil. Top with reserved edamame, sesame seeds, and everything bagel seasoning if using.

  • 3 g (1 tbsp) dried thyme
  • 1 tbsp dried rosemary, crushed
  • 3 g (1 tsp) garlic powder
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) onion powder

  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) olive oil

  • 1 clean empty spice jar

Instruction Rich Text:
Option 1: Homemade Spice Blend

  1. Clean the jar — Wash your empty spice jar thoroughly with warm soapy water. Remove the old label. Let it dry completely.
  2. Mix your spices — In a small bowl, combine oregano, basil, thyme, rosemary, garlic powder, onion powder, and red pepper flakes. Stir well.
  3. Fill the jar — Using a small funnel or spoon, pour the blend into the jar. Tap gently to settle.
  4. Label it — Add a handwritten or printed label with the blend name and date made.
  5. Store — Keep in a cool, dry place. Use within 6–12 months for best flavor.

Option 2: Salad Dressing Shaker

  1. Prep the jar — Remove the sifter insert and replace with a solid lid or leave as-is for a drizzle effect.
  2. Add ingredients — Pour in olive oil, vinegar, mustard, and honey. Season with salt and pepper.
  3. Shake and serve — Seal tightly and shake vigorously before each use. Drizzle directly over your salad.
  4. Refrigerate — Store in the fridge for up to 1 week. Shake before each use.

Option 3: Mini Herb Terrarium

  1. Prepare the jar — Remove the sifter lid. Clean and dry the jar completely.
  2. Add drainage layer — Place a thin layer of small pebbles at the bottom (about ¼ inch).
  3. Add charcoal — Sprinkle a small pinch of activated charcoal to keep things fresh (optional but recommended).
  4. Add soil — Spoon in potting soil to fill about half the jar.
  5. Plant your cutting — Use tweezers to gently place a small succulent, moss, or herb cutting into the soil.
  6. Water lightly — Add just a few drops of water. These mini terrariums need very little moisture.
  7. Display — Place on a sunny windowsill and enjoy your tiny garden!

Name: Repurposed Jar Ideas
Features: gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free
Common Ingredients: basil; mint; rosemary
Ingredients:
• 1 clean empty glass jar (any size)
  • 1 cup soy wax flakes
  • 1 candle wick with metal tab
  • 15–20 drops essential oil (lavender, vanilla, or citrus)
  • 1 pencil or chopstick (to hold wick)
  • Optional: dried flowers or herbs for decoration
  • 1 large clean glass jar
  • Twine or ribbon
  • Hot glue gun
  • Paint or chalkboard paint (optional)
  • 1 clean glass jar (tall and narrow works best)
  • Fresh herb cuttings (basil, mint, rosemary)
  • Room temperature water
  • Small pebbles (optional, for stability)
Equipment:
• Clean, empty glass jars (mason jars, pasta sauce jars, jam jars)
  • Double boiler or microwave-safe bowl
  • Thermometer (for candle making)
  • Hot glue gun
  • Paintbrush
  • Scissors or pruning snips
  • Labels or chalkboard paint markers
Nutrition:
This is a zero-waste DIY project — no calories here! 🌿

  • Waste diverted: 1–3 glass jars kept out of recycling
  • Cost savings: Homemade candle ~$5 vs $20+ store-bought
  • Carbon footprint: Reduced by reusing instead of purchasing new
  • Shelf life: Candle 40–50 burn hours | Utensil holder indefinite | Herb station ongoing
Instruction Rich Text:
Option 1: Homemade Soy Candle

  1. Clean the jar — Wash thoroughly with warm soapy water and dry completely. Remove labels.
  2. Prep the wick — Dip the metal tab of the wick in a small drop of melted wax and press it firmly to the bottom center of the jar. Let it set for 5 minutes.
  3. Hold the wick upright — Rest the wick across a pencil or chopstick laid over the jar opening. This keeps it centered while pouring.
  4. Melt the wax — Melt soy wax flakes in a double boiler over medium heat, stirring gently until fully liquid (around 170°F / 77°C).
  5. Add scent — Remove from heat and let cool slightly to 140°F (60°C), then stir in essential oils.
  6. Pour — Slowly pour the wax into the jar, leaving about ½ inch of space at the top.
  7. Cure — Allow to cool at room temperature for 24–48 hours. Trim the wick to ¼ inch before lighting.

Option 2: Kitchen Utensil Holder

  1. Clean and dry — Remove all labels and wash the jar well. Let it dry fully.
  2. Paint (optional) — Apply chalkboard paint or a color of your choice. Let each coat dry before adding the next (2–3 coats recommended).
  3. Add twine — Wrap twine around the neck of the jar several times and secure with a knot or hot glue for a rustic look.
  4. Fill and display — Place on your countertop and fill with spatulas, wooden spoons, whisks, or scissors.

Option 3: Herb Propagation Station

  1. Prep the cuttings — Snip 4–6 inch sprigs from fresh herbs just below a leaf node. Remove leaves from the bottom 2 inches.
  2. Fill the jar — Add room temperature water to about half the jar. Optionally add a few pebbles to stabilize the stems.
  3. Place cuttings — Drop the herb stems in, making sure no leaves are submerged.
  4. Find the light — Place on a sunny windowsill. Change the water every 2–3 days.
  5. Wait for roots — Roots typically appear within 1–3 weeks. Once roots are 1–2 inches long, transplant to soil or keep growing in water.

Features: gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free

Ingredients:
• 960 ml (4 cups) fresh apple juice
  • 4 g (2) cinnamon sticks
  • 4 whole cloves
  • 2 g (2) star anise
  • 3 slices fresh ginger
  • 1 orange, sliced into rounds
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup
  • Apple slices and cinnamon sticks for garnish
Equipment:

  • Fine mesh strainer

  • Mugs or heatproof glasses
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Combine — Add apple juice, cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise, ginger, and orange slices to a saucepan over medium heat.
  2. Simmer — Bring to a gentle simmer (do not boil). Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 20–30 minutes to let the spices infuse.
  3. Taste & sweeten — Taste and add maple syrup if a sweeter cider is desired.
  4. Strain — Pour through a fine mesh strainer into mugs, discarding the solids.
  5. Garnish & serve — Garnish with a fresh apple slice and cinnamon stick. Serve warm.

Slow Cooker Method

Combine all ingredients in a slow cooker and cook on LOW for 2–3 hours or HIGH for 1 hour. Strain and serve.

  5. Serve — Pour into mugs and dust with a pinch of cinnamon. Enjoy immediately.

Instruction Rich Text:

  2. Blend — Add soaked cashews, 2 cups fresh water, coconut cream, maple syrup, vanilla, nutmeg, cinnamon, turmeric, and salt to a high-speed blender.
  3. Blend until silky — Blend on high for 60–90 seconds until completely smooth with no cashew chunks.
  4. Strain (optional) — For an ultra-smooth eggnog, strain through a nut milk bag or fine mesh strainer.
  5. Taste & adjust — Add more maple syrup for sweetness or nutmeg for spice. Add rum or bourbon if making an adult version.

Classic Black Iced Tea

  • 4 cups filtered water
  • 4 black tea bags (or 3 tbsp loose-leaf black tea)
  • 2–3 tbsp maple syrup or agave (adjust to taste)
  • 1 lemon, sliced
  • Fresh mint for garnish
  • Lots of ice

For Sweet Tea Version

  • Add an extra 1–2 tbsp maple syrup while the tea is still warm

For Arnold Palmer Version

  • ½ pitcher iced tea + ½ pitcher fresh-squeezed lemonade
Equipment:
• Medium saucepan or kettle
  • Large pitcher (1.5–2 quart)
  • Long spoon for stirring
  • Tall glasses
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Boil water — Bring 4 cups of filtered water to a full boil.
  2. Steep — Remove from heat. Add tea bags and steep for 3–5 minutes. Steeping too long makes it bitter — set a timer!
  3. Remove bags — Gently squeeze each bag once before removing. Do not over-squeeze or it becomes bitter.
  4. Sweeten while warm — Stir in maple syrup while the tea is still hot so it dissolves completely.
  5. Cool & chill — Let cool to room temperature, then pour into a pitcher and refrigerate for 1–2 hours.
  6. Serve — Pour over plenty of ice. Garnish with lemon slices and fresh mint.

Cold Brew Method (No Bitterness)

  1. Add 4 tea bags to 4 cups of cold water in a pitcher.
  2. Refrigerate for 8–12 hours or overnight.
  3. Remove bags, sweeten, and serve over ice.

Ingredients:
• 1 cup daikon radish, julienned
  • 1 cup carrots, julienned
  • ½ cup rice vinegar
  • ½ cup warm water
  • 2 tbsp sugar
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1 block (14 oz) extra-firm tofu, pressed and sliced
  • 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
  • 1 tbsp hoisin sauce
  • 1 tsp sesame oil
  • 1 tsp sriracha
  • 1 tsp maple syrup
  • 1 clove garlic, minced
  • 3 tbsp vegan mayonnaise
  • 1 tsp sriracha (adjust to taste)
  • 1 tsp lime juice
  • 2 Vietnamese baguettes (bánh mì rolls) or 4 small French baguette sections
  • ½ cucumber, thinly sliced lengthwise
  • 1 jalapeño, thinly sliced (optional)
  • Large handful of fresh cilantro sprigs
  • 2 green onions, sliced
  • 2 tbsp soy sauce or Maggi seasoning (for drizzling)
Equipment:
• Sharp knife and cutting board
  • Mixing bowls (for brine and marinade)
  • Non-stick skillet or cast iron pan
  • Tofu press or clean kitchen towel
  • Small whisk
  • Broiler or toaster (for bread)
  • Airtight jar (for pickling vegetables)
Instruction Rich Text:
Step 1: Make the Pickled Vegetables (best done 1–24 hrs ahead)

  1. Make the brine — Whisk together rice vinegar, warm water, sugar, and salt in a bowl until the sugar fully dissolves.
  2. Julienne the vegetables — Cut daikon and carrots into thin matchsticks, about 2 inches long.
  3. Pickle — Submerge vegetables in the brine. Let sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate overnight for deeper flavor. Drain before using.

Step 2: Marinate & Cook the Tofu

  1. Press the tofu — Wrap tofu in a clean towel and press firmly for 15 minutes to remove excess moisture. Slice into thin planks or triangles.
  2. Make the marinade — Mix soy sauce, hoisin, sesame oil, sriracha, maple syrup, and minced garlic in a bowl.
  3. Marinate — Coat tofu slices in the marinade and let sit for at least 15 minutes (or up to 1 hour).
  4. Pan-fry — Heat a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil. Cook tofu 3–4 minutes per side until golden, caramelized, and slightly crispy. Set aside.

Step 3: Make the Sriracha Mayo

  1. Mix vegan mayo, sriracha, and lime juice together in a small bowl. Taste and adjust heat level.

Step 4: Toast the Bread

  1. Toast — Slice baguettes lengthwise and toast cut-side down in a dry skillet or under the broiler for 2–3 minutes until golden and crisp on the inside while staying soft on the outside.

Step 5: Assemble

  1. Spread — Generously spread sriracha mayo on both cut sides of the toasted baguette.
  2. Layer the tofu — Lay caramelized tofu slices along the bottom half.
  3. Add pickled veg — Pile on the drained pickled daikon and carrots.
  4. Add fresh toppings — Layer cucumber slices, jalapeño, cilantro sprigs, and green onions.
  5. Drizzle — Add a tiny drizzle of soy sauce or Maggi seasoning for extra umami.
  6. Close and serve immediately — Bánh mì is best eaten fresh while the bread is still crisp.

1. Prepare the Chili Mixture: In a large heatproof bowl, mix together the gochugaru, red chili flakes, sesame seeds, soy sauce, sugar, and salt. Stir well and set aside. Make sure the bowl is completely dry — any water will cause the hot oil to splatter dangerously.
  2. Infuse the Oil: Pour the neutral oil into a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the sliced garlic, ginger, green onions, cinnamon stick, star anise, bay leaves, and Sichuan peppercorns. Reduce to medium-low and cook for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the garlic is light golden and the oil gently bubbles. Do not let the garlic turn dark brown — dark garlic makes bitter oil.
  3. Pour the Oil: If you prefer a cleaner oil, strain out the solids. For a more textured, flavor-packed result, pour everything directly over the chili mixture. Carefully ladle the hot oil over the chili in 2–3 pours, stirring between each pour. The mixture will sizzle and bloom dramatically — this releases the deep red color and aroma.
  4. Add Sesame Oil: If using, stir in the ¼ cup sesame oil now while everything is still warm. Mix thoroughly until all the chili flakes are coated and glistening.
  5. Cool and Store: Let the chili oil cool to room temperature uncovered for about 30–45 minutes — the flavors deepen significantly as it cools. Spoon into a clean, dry glass jar with a tight-fitting lid. For best flavor, let it rest for at least a few hours before using. Overnight is even better.

Name: Homemade Ketchup
Common Ingredients: celery; garlic; tomatoes; maple-syrup; onion; salt; garlic-powder; smoked-paprika; sugar; cinnamon; allspice; black-pepper; apple-cider-vinegar; tomato-paste; brown-sugar; cayenne-29751
Ingredients:
• 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes or whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
  • 1 small yellow onion, roughly chopped
  • 3 garlic cloves, smashed
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 3 tbsp apple cider vinegar
  • 2 tbsp maple syrup or coconut sugar
  • 1 tbsp brown sugar (adjust to taste)
  • 1 tsp salt
  • ½ tsp onion powder
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • ¼ tsp ground allspice
  • ¼ tsp ground cloves
  • ¼ tsp celery seed
  • ¼ tsp smoked paprika
  • ¼ tsp black pepper
  • Pinch of cayenne (optional)
  • 1 cinnamon stick
Equipment:
• Medium saucepan
  • Immersion blender or countertop blender
  • Fine mesh strainer (optional, for ultra-smooth result)
  • Wooden spoon or silicone spatula
  • Glass jar or squeeze bottle for storing
  • Measuring spoons and cups
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Sauté the Aromatics: Warm 1 tbsp neutral oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and smashed garlic. Cook for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent. Do not brown them.
  2. Build the Sauce: Stir in the crushed tomatoes and tomato paste. Mix well. Add the apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, brown sugar, all the spices, and the cinnamon stick. Stir to combine.
  3. Bring to a Simmer: Raise heat to medium-high until the mixture just starts to bubble, then reduce to a low simmer.
  4. Simmer Low and Slow: Cook uncovered over low heat for 30–45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes. The mixture should reduce by about one-third and thicken noticeably. Remove the cinnamon stick before blending.
  5. Blend Until Smooth: Use an immersion blender directly in the pot, or carefully transfer to a countertop blender. Blend until completely smooth and glossy. For an ultra-smooth result, pass through a fine mesh strainer pressing firmly with a spatula.
  6. Taste and Adjust: Adjust to your preference — too acidic? Add a little more maple syrup. Too sweet? Add a splash more vinegar. Too thick? Stir in 1–2 tbsp water. Too thin? Simmer 10 more minutes.
  7. Cool and Store: Let cool to room temperature — it will thicken further as it cools. Pour into a clean glass jar or squeeze bottle. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving. Flavor improves significantly after 24 hours.

Name: Lemon Pepper Corn

Ingredients:
• 4 ears of fresh corn, husked
  • 2 tbsp vegan butter (or olive oil)
  • 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
  • 1 tsp lemon zest (from about 1 lemon)
  • 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon)
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • ½ tsp salt, or to taste

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Boil or Grill the Corn: Boil: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the husked corn and cook for 8–10 minutes until tender. Remove with tongs.
    Grill: Preheat grill to medium-high heat. Brush corn lightly with oil and grill for 10–12 minutes, turning every 2–3 minutes, until charred in spots.
  2. Make the Lemon Pepper Butter: In a small saucepan over low heat (or in the microwave in 20-second intervals), melt 2 tbsp vegan butter. Stir in lemon zest, lemon juice, black pepper, garlic powder, and salt. Mix well.
  3. Coat the Corn: While the corn is still hot, brush or spoon the lemon pepper butter generously over each ear, turning to coat all sides evenly.
  4. Garnish and Serve: Transfer corn to a serving plate. Sprinkle with fresh parsley if using. Serve immediately while hot.

Ingredients:
• 4 cups green cabbage, thinly shredded (about ½ small head)
  • 1 cup purple cabbage, thinly shredded
  • 2 large carrots, julienned or coarsely grated
  • 2 navel oranges, peeled and segmented
  • 3 green onions, thinly sliced
  • ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves
  • 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
  • 3 tbsp fresh ginger, finely grated (about a 2-inch knob)
  • 3 tbsp rice vinegar
  • 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari

1. Make the Ginger Dressing: In a small bowl or jar, whisk together the grated ginger, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, maple syrup, orange juice, orange zest, garlic, and chili flakes if using. Taste and adjust — add more maple syrup for sweetness, more vinegar for tang, or more ginger for punch. Set aside.
  2. Prep the Vegetables: Shred both cabbages as thinly as possible — a mandoline gives the best results but a sharp knife works well. Julienne or coarsely grate the carrots. Slice the green onions thinly on a diagonal.

  6. Add the Toppings and Serve: Add the orange segments, green onions, and cilantro. Drizzle over the remaining dressing. Toss gently to combine. Top with toasted sesame seeds and serve immediately.

1. Pre-cook the Wheat Berries: Wheat berries take the longest to cook, so start them first. Place the rinsed wheat berries in a small saucepan with 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer, cover, and cook for 45–60 minutes until tender but still slightly chewy. Drain any excess water and set aside. If you have pre-soaked them overnight, reduce the cook time to about 25–30 minutes.
  2. Sauté the Onion: While the wheat berries cook, heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed saucepan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until deeply golden and soft. Take your time here — caramelized onion is the flavor backbone of this porridge. Add the garlic and cook for another 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
  3. Bloom the Spices: Add the turmeric and black pepper directly to the onion and garlic. Stir constantly for 30–60 seconds until the spices are fragrant and coat everything in a warm golden color. This step activates the turmeric and deepens the flavor significantly.
  4. Add the Bulgur and Oats: Pour in the vegetable broth and 1 cup water. Stir in the bulgur and rolled oats. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a low simmer. Cook uncovered for 12–15 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the bulgur is tender and the oats have broken down into a creamy, porridge-like consistency.
  5. Fold in the Wheat Berries: Add the cooked wheat berries to the pot and stir to combine. Simmer together for another 3–5 minutes so everything melds. The porridge should be thick and spoonable but still loose — add an extra splash of broth or water if it gets too thick.
  6. Season and Serve: Taste and adjust with salt to your liking. Ladle into bowls, drizzle with a generous pour of good olive oil, and scatter with fresh parsley or chives. Serve hot.

  • Parchment-lined baking sheet or silicone mat
  • Offset spatula

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat and Prep the Pan: Preheat your oven to 170°F (77°C), or as low as it will go. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
  2. Blend: Add 3 cups (450 g) strawberries, 1 tbsp maple syrup, and 1 tbsp lemon juice to a blender or food processor. Blend until completely smooth with no chunks remaining.
  3. Spread: Pour the strawberry purée onto the prepared baking sheet. Use an offset spatula to spread it evenly to about ⅛-inch thickness. Thin and uniform is key — thick spots stay tacky while thin spots over-dry and crack.
  4. Dry: Oven method: Bake at 170°F (77°C) for 3–4 hours. Dehydrator method: Set to 135°F (57°C) for 6–8 hours. The roll-up is ready when it is dry to the touch but still flexible and peels cleanly off the parchment without tearing.
  5. Cool and Peel: Remove from the oven and let cool completely at room temperature. Carefully peel the fruit leather off the parchment paper in one sheet.
  6. Cut and Roll: Cut into strips using scissors or a pizza cutter. Roll each strip in a piece of parchment paper to prevent sticking.
  7. Store: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week, or refrigerate for up to 3 weeks. Place parchment between layers to prevent sticking.

  • 1 tbsp baking powder
  • 1 tbsp sugar (or maple syrup)
  • ¼ tsp salt
  • 1¼ cups (300 ml) oat milk (or any plant-based milk)

1. Make the Vegan Buttermilk: Combine 1¼ cups (300 ml) oat milk and 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar in a jug or bowl. Stir briefly and set aside for 5 minutes to curdle into a buttermilk substitute. It will look slightly curdled — that’s exactly what you want.
  2. Mix the Dry Ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together 1½ cups (180 g) spelt flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 1 tbsp sugar, and ¼ tsp salt until evenly combined.
  3. Mix the Wet Ingredients: Add 2 tbsp melted coconut oil and 1 tsp vanilla extract to the curdled oat milk mixture and stir to combine.
  4. Combine: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined — a few lumps are completely fine. Do not overmix; overworked spelt batter becomes dense and tough. Let the batter rest for 2 minutes while the pan heats.
  5. Cook: Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat and lightly grease with coconut oil or a neutral oil. Pour ¼ cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form across the surface and the edges look set and matte, about 2–3 minutes. Flip and cook for 1–2 minutes more until golden. Adjust heat as needed — spelt browns faster than all-purpose flour.
  6. Keep Warm and Serve: Transfer cooked pancakes to a baking sheet in a 200°F (93°C) oven to keep warm while you finish the batch. Serve stacked with maple syrup, fresh berries, nut butter, or a dusting of powdered sugar.
