Name: Cinnamon Rolls (Vegan)
Common Ingredients: all-purpose-flour; vegan-butter; oat-milk; salt; cream-cheese; sugar; cinnamon; vanilla-extract; nutmeg; brown-sugar; powdered-sugar; instant-yeast-7f935
Ingredients:
• Dough
  • 2¼ tsp (7 g) instant yeast (1 packet)
  • 240 ml (1 cup) oat milk
  • ¼ cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 360 g (3 cups) all-purpose flour
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt
  • ¼ cup (60 g) vegan butter, softened
  • Filling
  • ⅓ cup (75 g) vegan butter, softened
  • ¾ cup (150 g) brown sugar, packed
  • 16 g (2 tbsp) ground cinnamon
  • ¼ tsp ground nutmeg (optional)
  • Cream Cheese Glaze
  • 115 g (4 oz) vegan cream cheese
  • 120 g (1 cup) powdered sugar
  • 2–3 tbsp oat milk
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • Pinch of salt
Equipment:
• Stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl for hand kneading)
  • Rolling pin
  • 9×13 inch (23×33 cm) baking dish
  • Parchment paper
  • Offset spatula or butter knife
  • Bench scraper or sharp knife (or dental floss)
  • Small mixing bowl (for glaze)
  • Kitchen thermometer (for milk temperature)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Activate the Yeast: In a large bowl or the bowl of a stand mixer, combine the warm oat milk (110°F / 43°C), instant yeast, and granulated sugar. Stir briefly and let sit for 5 minutes until the mixture looks slightly foamy. If it doesn't foam at all, your milk was too hot or the yeast is dead — start over with fresh yeast.
  2. Make the Dough: Add the flour, salt, and softened vegan butter to the yeast mixture. Mix with a dough hook on medium speed for 6–8 minutes, or knead by hand on a lightly floured surface for 8–10 minutes, until the dough is smooth, soft, and just slightly tacky — it should pull away from the sides of the bowl cleanly and spring back slowly when poked.
  3. First Rise: Shape the dough into a ball. Place in a lightly oiled bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap or a damp kitchen towel. Let rise in a warm spot for 1 to 1½ hours until doubled in size. A good warm spot: inside a turned-off oven with just the oven light on.
  4. Make the Filling: In a small bowl, mix together the softened vegan butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg until a thick paste forms. Set aside at room temperature.
  5. Roll and Fill: Turn the risen dough out onto a lightly floured surface and press down gently to release any large air bubbles. Roll into a rectangle approximately 45 × 30 cm (18 × 12 inches), with the longer edge facing you. Spread the cinnamon filling evenly using an offset spatula, going all the way to the edges on three sides and leaving a 1 cm (½ inch) border on the far long edge so the rolls seal cleanly.
  6. Roll and Cut: Starting from the long edge closest to you, roll the dough tightly and evenly into a log. Pinch the seam firmly to seal. Using a sharp knife or unflavored dental floss, cut the log into 12 equal rolls, each about 4 cm (1½ inches) wide.
  7. Second Rise: Line a 9×13 inch (23×33 cm) baking dish with parchment paper. Arrange the rolls cut-side up with a little space between each. Cover loosely and let rise in a warm spot for 30–45 minutes until puffed and touching. Alternatively, refrigerate overnight at this stage and bake straight from the fridge the next morning.
  8. Bake: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Bake for 22–26 minutes until the tops are light golden — they should look just set. Do not overbake; rolls that look slightly underdone in the center are perfectly cooked once rested.
  9. Make the Cream Cheese Glaze: Beat the vegan cream cheese until smooth. Add the powdered sugar, vanilla extract, pinch of salt, and 2 tbsp oat milk. Whisk until silky and smooth, adding the third tablespoon of oat milk if needed for a thick but pourable consistency.
  10. Glaze and Serve: Spread or pour the glaze generously over the rolls while they are still warm — not piping hot, not fully cool. The warmth helps the glaze melt slightly into the rolls. Serve immediately from the pan.

  7. Cool on the Pan: Remove from the oven and let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for at least 10 minutes before moving them — they are fragile straight from the oven and will firm up to the perfect chewy-crisp texture as they rest. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

Name: Artichoke Dip (Vegan)
Common Ingredients: garlic; lemon; spinach; nutritional-yeast; cashews; onion; salt; vegetable-broth; olive-oil; artichoke; smoked-paprika; breadcrumbs-ecfe4
Ingredients:
• 240 g (1 cup) raw cashews
  • 180 ml (¾ cup) vegetable broth
  • 15 g (3 tbsp) nutritional yeast
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) lemon juice
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) onion powder
  • ¼ tsp smoked paprika
  • salt and pepper to taste
  • 800 g (2 cans / 14 oz each) artichoke hearts in water
  • 60 g (2 cups) fresh baby spinach
  • 9 g (3) garlic cloves
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil
  • 30 g (¼ cup) breadcrumbs
  • Smoked paprika, for dusting
Equipment:
• High-speed blender or food processor
  • Skillet or frying pan
  • Oven-safe baking dish (20 cm / 8 inch)
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Colander
  • Knife and cutting board
Nutrition:
Servings ¼ cup  Calories 165  Carbohydrates 14 g  Fat 10 g  Fiber 4 g  Protein 6 g
‍Monounsaturated 4 g  Polyunsaturated 2 g  Saturated 1.8 g  Trans 0 g
‍Vitamin A 95 mcg  Vitamin C 8 mg  Vitamin D 0 mg

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Soak or Boil the Cashews: If you haven’t done so already, soak the raw cashews in cold water for at least 4 hours (or overnight). For a quick method, cover with boiling water and simmer for 15 minutes until tender. Drain and rinse. Soft cashews are essential for a silky, creamy dip.
  2. Preheat the Oven: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F). Lightly grease a small to medium oven-safe baking dish (about 20 cm / 8 inches) with olive oil or cooking spray.
  3. Make the Cashew Cream: Add the drained cashews, vegetable broth, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, onion powder, salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika to a high-speed blender. Blend on high for 1–2 minutes until completely smooth and creamy with no gritty texture. Taste and adjust seasoning.
  4. Cook the Garlic and Spinach: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant and just golden — don’t let it burn. Add the chopped spinach and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until fully wilted and any moisture has evaporated. Remove from heat.
  5. Combine: In a large bowl, combine the chopped artichoke hearts, the cashew cream, and the sautéed garlic and spinach. Stir well until everything is evenly coated and distributed. Taste and adjust salt and lemon juice as needed.
  6. Fill the Baking Dish: Transfer the mixture into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly. If using, scatter the breadcrumbs over the top and dust with a little extra smoked paprika. Drizzle with a thin thread of olive oil.
  7. Bake: Bake uncovered for 22–26 minutes until the dip is bubbling at the edges and the top is lightly golden. If you used breadcrumbs, they should be toasted and golden. For extra color, switch to broil for the last 2–3 minutes — watch closely.
  8. Rest and Serve: Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving — it will be very hot straight from the oven. Serve directly from the baking dish with toasted pita, crusty bread, crackers, or crudités.

Baby spinach adds color, nutrients, and a subtle earthiness. Wilting it fully and pressing out the moisture before adding to the mix is critical — watery spinach makes a loose, watery dip.

Smoked paprika adds a subtle smokiness that gives the dip depth and makes it taste more complex than the ingredient list suggests.

Vegetable broth is used in the cashew cream instead of water — it adds a background savory flavor that water alone doesn’t provide.

Name: Pico de Gallo
Features: 20-minutes-or-less; gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free
Common Ingredients: garlic; cilantro; lime; tomatoes; jalapeno; onion; salt; black-pepper
Ingredients:
• 492 g (4 medium) ripe tomatoes
  • ½ small white onion, finely diced
  • 14 g (1) jalapeño
  • ⅓ cup (15 g) fresh cilantro, leaves and tender stems, finely chopped
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) fresh lime juice
  • ½ tsp salt, or to taste
  • ¼ tsp black pepper
  • 3 g (1) garlic clove
Equipment:
• Sharp chef’s knife and cutting board
  • Fine mesh strainer or colander
  • Medium mixing bowl
  • Citrus juicer or reamer
  • Spoon or spatula for mixing

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Dice the Tomatoes: Cut the tomatoes into a fine, even dice — about ½ cm (¼ inch). For the cleanest pico, use a very sharp knife. After dicing, transfer to a fine mesh strainer or colander and let drain for 5 minutes — this removes excess juice and prevents a watery salsa. Don’t skip this step.
  2. Dice the Onion and Jalapeño: Finely dice the white onion to roughly the same size as the tomato pieces — uniform size means a better bite in every scoop. For the jalapeño, remove the seeds and white membrane for a milder heat, or leave them in for a spicier result. Dice finely.
  3. Chop the Cilantro: Finely chop the cilantro, using both the leaves and the tender upper stems — the stems are full of flavor. Avoid the thick lower stems.
  4. Combine: In a medium bowl, combine the drained tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and garlic (if using). Add the lime juice, salt, and black pepper. Toss gently to combine — don’t over-mix or the tomatoes will break down.
  5. Taste and Rest: Taste and adjust — add more lime juice for brightness, more salt to bring out the tomato flavor, or more jalapeño for heat. Let the pico rest for at least 10 minutes at room temperature before serving — this allows the flavors to meld and the salt to draw out the tomato juices into the dressing. It improves significantly within the first 15–30 minutes.
  6. Serve: Serve with tortilla chips, spooned over tacos, burritos, grilled corn, guacamole, or any Mexican-inspired dish. Serve at room temperature for the best flavor — cold pico de gallo mutes the tomato and lime.

Notes: Pico de gallo is all about the tomatoes — use the ripest, most flavorful ones you can find. In summer, heirloom or vine-ripened tomatoes make an extraordinary pico. In winter, Roma (plum) tomatoes are the most reliable choice. White onion is traditional and gives the sharpest, cleanest bite. Red onion can be used for a milder, slightly sweeter flavor.

Tips: Draining the diced tomatoes is the single step most home cooks skip — don’t. Even 5 minutes in a strainer removes enough liquid to make the difference between a watery salsa and a thick, scoopable one. Use a very sharp knife — a dull blade crushes the tomato and releases far more juice than necessary. Let it rest — pico after 15–30 minutes of resting is remarkable.

Storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The pico will release more liquid over time — drain it briefly before serving. Do not freeze.

Swaps: No jalapeño? Use serrano pepper for more heat, or poblano for a very mild fruity flavor. Swap lime juice for lemon juice if lime isn’t available. Add ½ ripe mango, finely diced, for a sweet mango pico de gallo. Stir in 1 diced avocado for a chunky guacamole-pico hybrid.

The fresh lime juice adds acidity that brightens and balances the dish. The garlic clove builds a savory, aromatic base. The ½ small white onion adds sweetness and depth as it cooks down.

Name: Yogurt Parfait (Vegan)
Common Ingredients: blueberries; chia-seeds; nut-butter; raspberries; oats; maple-syrup; peanuts; yogurt; vanilla-extract; mixed-berries; agave-f3c73; coconut-flakes-0f5a4; granola-22bfd; vanilla-0b300
Ingredients:
• 2 cups (480 g) vegan yogurt, coconut or oat-based, plain or vanilla
  • 1 cup (150 g) mixed fresh berries (strawberries, blueberries, raspberries)
  • ½ cup (50 g) granola (vegan)
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) maple syrup or agave
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 1 tbsp chia seeds (optional)
  • 16 g (1 tbsp) nut butter
  • 1 tbsp toasted coconut flakes (optional, for topping)
Equipment:
• 2 tall glasses, mason jars, or bowls
  • Spoon or spatula for layering
  • Small bowl (for macerating berries if needed)
  • Knife and cutting board (for strawberries)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the Yogurt: If using plain vegan yogurt, stir in the vanilla extract and 1 tbsp maple syrup until smooth and well combined. Taste and adjust sweetness — the yogurt should be pleasantly sweet but not cloying, as the fruit and granola will add more. If using vanilla yogurt, taste first before adding any sweetener.
  2. Prep the Berries: Wash and dry the berries. Hull and slice the strawberries if using. Leave blueberries and raspberries whole. If your berries aren’t very sweet, toss them with a small drizzle of maple syrup and let sit for 2–3 minutes to macerate slightly — this draws out their juices and intensifies the flavor.
  3. Layer the Parfait: Using tall glasses, jars, or bowls, begin building the layers. Start with a generous layer of yogurt at the bottom (⅓ of the total). Add a layer of berries, then a layer of granola. Repeat the layers — yogurt, berries, granola — ending with the final layer of yogurt on top.
  4. Add the Toppings: Finish the top layer with a scatter of fresh berries and a handful of granola for crunch. If using, drizzle with nut butter, sprinkle with chia seeds, and scatter toasted coconut flakes over the top. Add a final drizzle of maple syrup for a glossy finish.
  5. Serve Immediately or Chill: Serve right away if you want the granola to stay crunchy. For a softer, more custardy parfait, cover and refrigerate for 1–2 hours — the granola will absorb the yogurt and the whole thing will set into a thick, pudding-like texture. Both versions are delicious — it’s a matter of preference.

Swaps: Swap fresh berries for mango, banana, kiwi, stone fruit, or any seasonal fruit. Replace granola with toasted oats, muesli, crushed nuts, or puffed rice for a different crunch. Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cook the Edamame: If using frozen edamame, bring a small pot of salted water to a boil and cook the edamame for 3–5 minutes until bright green and just tender. Drain and rinse under cold water immediately to stop the cooking and preserve the vivid green color. Pat dry. If your edamame is already thawed and tender, you can skip boiling and use it straight — though a brief blanch improves the flavor and color significantly.
  2. Blend the Base: Add the tahini, lemon juice, and garlic to a food processor. Process for 1 minute until the mixture is smooth and slightly fluffy — this step emulsifies the tahini and creates a lighter, creamier texture throughout the hummus. Don’t skip it.

  4. Add Ice-Cold Water: With the processor running, drizzle in the ice-cold water, one tablespoon at a time, until the hummus reaches your desired consistency — thick and scoopable or slightly looser and spreadable. The cold water is key to a light, airy texture. Process for another 1–2 minutes after the last addition — longer blending always means smoother hummus.
  5. Taste and Adjust: Taste carefully and adjust — more lemon juice for brightness, more salt to round out the flavors, more tahini for nuttiness, or a tiny extra drizzle of olive oil for richness. The hummus should taste vibrant, nutty, and well-seasoned.
  6. Serve: Transfer to a wide, shallow serving bowl. Use the back of a spoon to create a swirl on the surface. Drizzle generously with olive oil, dust with smoked paprika, and scatter with sesame seeds and fresh herbs if using. Serve with warm pita, crackers, or crudités.

1. Crush the Cucumbers: Place the cucumbers on a cutting board. Using the flat side of a large knife or a rolling pin, bash each cucumber firmly along its length until it cracks and splits open — you want them broken, not pulverized. They don’t need to be uniform. Crushing (rather than slicing) creates jagged, irregular surfaces that absorb the dressing far better than smooth cuts and gives the salad its signature rustic texture. Cut or tear the crushed cucumbers into 3–4 cm (1–1½ inch) bite-sized pieces.
  2. Salt and Drain: Transfer the cucumber pieces to a colander or strainer set over a bowl. Sprinkle with ½ tsp salt and toss to coat. Let sit for 10–15 minutes — the salt draws out excess moisture, concentrating the cucumber flavor and preventing the dressing from being diluted. After resting, pat the cucumbers dry with a paper towel or kitchen cloth. Don’t rinse — the residual salt seasons the salad.

Make the Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together the minced garlic, rice vinegar, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, maple syrup, chili flakes, and grated ginger (if using) with the remaining ¼ tsp salt.   4. Dress and Toss: Transfer the drained cucumbers to a serving bowl. Pour the dressing over and toss well to coat every piece. Let the salad sit for at least 5 minutes before serving so the cucumbers absorb the dressing. The longer it sits (up to 20 minutes), the more intensely flavored it becomes.
  5. Finish and Serve: Scatter the toasted sesame seeds, sliced spring onions, and fresh cilantro over the top. Serve immediately at room temperature or slightly chilled. Serve as a side dish, appetizer, or alongside rice, noodles, or any Asian-inspired meal.

Name: Three Bean Salad (Vegan)

Ingredients:
• 1 can (400 g) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
  • 1 can (400 g) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
  • 1 can (400 g) cannellini or green beans, drained and rinsed
  • ½ small red onion, very finely diced
  • 80 g (2) celery stalks
  • ¼ cup (15 g) fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
  • Dressing
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) red wine vinegar
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup or sugar
  • 3 g (1) garlic clove
  • 5 g (1 tsp) Dijon mustard
  • ½ tsp salt, or to taste
  • ¼ tsp black pepper
  • ¼ tsp dried oregano
Equipment:
• Colander or strainer
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Small bowl or jar (for dressing)
  • Whisk or fork
  • Knife and cutting board
  • Spoon or spatula for tossing
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Drain and Rinse the Beans: Drain all three cans of beans through a colander and rinse thoroughly under cold running water. Shake off excess water and pat dry with a paper towel — wet beans dilute the dressing and make the salad watery. If using fresh or frozen green beans instead of canned, blanch in salted boiling water for 2–3 minutes until just tender but still bright green, then drain and rinse under cold water to stop cooking.
  2. Prep the Vegetables: Very finely dice the red onion — small pieces mean you get onion flavor in every bite without any sharp, dominant chunks. For a milder onion flavor, soak the diced onion in cold water for 5–10 minutes then drain and pat dry — this removes some of the harshness without losing the flavor. Thinly slice the celery and finely chop the parsley.
  3. Make the Dressing: In a small bowl or jar, whisk together the red wine vinegar, olive oil, maple syrup, minced garlic, Dijon mustard, salt, black pepper, and dried oregano until smooth and emulsified. Taste — it should be bright, tangy, slightly sweet, and well-seasoned. Adjust vinegar for more acidity or maple syrup to balance.
  4. Combine: In a large bowl, combine the drained chickpeas, kidney beans, cannellini beans, red onion, celery, and parsley. Pour the dressing over and toss gently but thoroughly to coat everything evenly.

Ingredients:
• 4 ears of fresh corn, husked (or 3 cups frozen corn, thawed)
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil
  • ½ small red onion, finely diced
  • 14 g (1) jalapeño

Equipment:

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Grill the Corn: Heat a grill, grill pan, or cast iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Brush the husked corn lightly with olive oil and place directly on the grill. Cook, turning every 2–3 minutes, for 10–12 minutes total until the kernels are charred in spots and deeply golden all over. The char is the whole point — don’t rush it or turn the heat down. Transfer to a board and let cool for 5 minutes.

    No grill? Broil the corn on a baking sheet under a high broiler for 10–12 minutes, turning halfway, until charred. Or char frozen corn directly in a dry, screaming-hot cast iron pan for 4–5 minutes without stirring until the kernels blacken in spots.
  2. Cut the Kernels: Stand each cob upright on a cutting board. Using a sharp knife, slice downward along the cob to remove the kernels in strips. Rotate and repeat all the way around. Collect any kernels and corn milk that fall — it all goes into the salad. You should have about 3 cups of kernels total.
  3. Prep the Vegetables: Finely dice the red onion and jalapeño and dice the red bell pepper into small, even pieces. Thinly slice the spring onions and roughly chop the cilantro. If using avocado, dice it just before assembling to prevent browning.
  4. Make the Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together the lime juice, olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, black pepper, and chili flakes (if using). Taste — it should be bold, smoky, and citrusy. Adjust lime juice or salt as needed.
  5. Combine and Dress: In a large bowl, combine the grilled corn kernels, red onion, jalapeño, red bell pepper, spring onions, and cilantro. Pour the dressing over and toss well. Add the diced avocado last (if using) and fold in gently to keep the pieces intact.
  6. Taste and Serve: Taste and adjust — a little more lime juice, salt, or chili flakes if needed. Serve immediately at room temperature, or refrigerate for up to 1 hour before serving. Garnish with extra cilantro, a wedge of lime, and a dusting of smoked paprika. Serve as a side dish, taco topping, or spooned over grain bowls.

Make Ahead: Prep all fruit and store undressed in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Make the dressing separately. Combine and dress within 30 minutes of serving for the best texture. Dressed fruit salad is best eaten within 2–3 hours — after that, the softer fruits break down and release too much liquid.

Storage: Store undressed fruit in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Once dressed, best eaten within 3–4 hours. The salad will become increasingly juicy and the softer fruits will soften further — this isn’t unpleasant, just different in texture. Not suitable for freezing.

Swaps: Use any seasonal fruit combination — peaches, nectarines, cherries, watermelon, papaya, dragon fruit, or pomegranate seeds all work beautifully. Swap lime for lemon or orange juice for a different citrus note. Replace maple syrup with date syrup, agave, or a little orange juice concentrate. Add 1 tbsp of fresh ginger, finely grated, to the dressing for a warming spiced version. Swap mint for fresh basil for a more unusual, aromatic finish. For a tropical version, use mango, pineapple, papaya, passionfruit, and coconut flakes with a lime-coconut dressing.

Strawberries are the anchor of the salad — sweet, bright red, and visually striking. They also release the most juice once dressed, contributing to the natural syrup that forms at the bottom of the bowl.

Mango adds tropical sweetness and a buttery, dense texture that contrasts beautifully with the lighter berries. Use a ripe mango — an underripe one will be sour and fibrous.

Kiwi brings a tart, refreshing bite and a pop of bright green color. It also contains actinidin, an enzyme that tenderizes surrounding fruit slightly — another reason not to dress the salad too far ahead.

Pineapple provides juicy, fibrous chunks that hold their shape well and add a tropical note. Fresh pineapple is best; canned in juice (not syrup) works fine.

Blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries add color contrast, antioxidants, and a balance of sweetness and tartness. Add them last and fold gently — they crush easily and will bleed color into the whole salad if overhandled.

Lime juice and zest are the secret to a fruit salad that tastes like more than just a bowl of cut fruit. Acid brightens every flavor and the zest adds a fragrant citrus note that lifts the whole thing.

Maple syrup or agave is optional — if your fruit is very ripe and sweet you may not need any at all. Add it gradually and taste as you go.

Fresh mint added at the very last moment gives a cooling, aromatic finish. It wilts and blackens quickly once dressed, so never add it early.

Name: Tomato Basil Orzo (Vegan)

Ingredients:
• 300 g (10.5 oz) orzo pasta
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) olive oil
  • 12 g (4) garlic cloves
  • ½ tsp chili flakes, or to taste
  • 500 g (about 3 cups) cherry tomatoes
  • 32 g (2 tbsp) tomato paste
  • ½ cup (120 ml) dry white wine or vegetable broth
  • 1½ cups (360 ml) vegetable broth, plus more as needed
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt

  • 1 cup (25 g) fresh basil leaves, roughly torn
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) extra virgin olive oil
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) lemon juice

Equipment:
• Large wide skillet or shallow saucepan (at least 28 cm / 11 inches)
  • Wooden spoon or silicone spatula
  • Ladle or measuring jug (for adding broth gradually)
  • Knife and cutting board
  • Grater or microplane (for lemon zest if adding)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Bloom the Garlic and Chili: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a large, wide skillet or shallow saucepan over medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and chili flakes and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring often, until the garlic is golden and fragrant — watch carefully, it goes from golden to burnt quickly. The garlic should be pale golden, not dark brown.
  2. Cook the Tomatoes: Add the halved cherry tomatoes and tomato paste to the pan. Stir to combine and cook over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down, released their juices, and the mixture looks jammy and concentrated. Add the sugar or maple syrup and stir through — this balances the acidity of the tomatoes without making it sweet.
  3. Deglaze: Pour in the white wine or vegetable broth and stir to lift any caramelized bits from the base of the pan. Let it bubble and reduce for 1–2 minutes until almost fully absorbed.
  4. Add the Orzo: Add the dry orzo directly to the pan and stir to coat in the tomato mixture. Pour in the vegetable broth, stir well, and bring to a simmer. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently — much like risotto — for 10–12 minutes until the orzo is al dente and has absorbed most of the liquid. Add extra splashes of broth if needed to keep the orzo loose and saucy. It should be creamy and saucy, not dry.
  5. Finish: Remove from the heat. Stir in the lemon juice and finishing olive oil. Taste and adjust salt, pepper, and chili. Let rest for 1–2 minutes — the orzo will thicken slightly as it sits.
  6. Add the Basil and Serve: Tear the fresh basil directly over the pan and fold through gently — add it off the heat so it stays bright green and fragrant. Serve immediately from the pan into wide bowls, topped with nutritional yeast or vegan parmesan and an extra drizzle of olive oil. A few extra basil leaves on top make it look beautiful.

1. Caramelize the Onions: Heat 4 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp vegan butter in a large, wide, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add all the sliced onions and ½ tsp salt. Toss to coat in the oil and cook, stirring every 3–5 minutes, for 45–55 minutes until deeply golden, jammy, and reduced to about a quarter of their original volume. Don’t rush this — low and slow is the only way. If the onions start to stick or brown too fast, add a splash of water and stir. After about 30 minutes, add the sugar to help with caramelization. The finished onions should be a deep mahogany brown and smell sweet and nutty.
  2. Add Garlic and Chili: Push the onions to one side of the pan. Add the sliced garlic and chili flakes to the cleared space and cook for 1–2 minutes until golden and fragrant, then stir everything together.
  3. Deglaze with Balsamic and Wine: Add the balsamic vinegar and stir vigorously — it will sizzle and reduce almost immediately. Then pour in the white wine or broth and stir to lift all the caramelized bits from the pan. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the liquid has reduced by half and the mixture is thick and jammy. Season with the remaining ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper. Taste and adjust.
  4. Cook the Pasta: While the onions are in their final stage, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta according to package directions until 1 minute shy of al dente — it will finish cooking in the sauce. Before draining, scoop out at least 1 cup (240 ml) of pasta cooking water and set aside. Drain the pasta.
  5. Combine: Add the drained pasta directly to the pan with the caramelized onions over medium heat. Add ½ cup of pasta water and 3 tbsp nutritional yeast. Toss vigorously for 1–2 minutes until the pasta is coated and the sauce is glossy and clings to every strand. Add more pasta water a splash at a time if needed to loosen. The starchy water emulsifies with the olive oil and onion juices to create a silky, saucy coating.
  6. Finish and Serve: Remove from heat. Drizzle with finishing olive oil and toss again. Taste for salt, pepper, and balsamic. Divide into wide bowls and top with fresh thyme or parsley, toasted breadcrumbs for crunch, and a sprinkle of vegan parmesan if using. Serve immediately — this pasta waits for no one.

Name: Broccoli Salad (Vegan)

• 2 heads broccoli (about 600 g), cut into small florets, stems peeled and thinly sliced
  • ½ small red onion, very finely diced

  • ½ cup (60 g) roasted sunflower seeds or slivered almonds
  • ⅓ cup (50 g) shelled pumpkin seeds

  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) apple cider vinegar

  • 5 g (1 tsp) Dijon mustard
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • ½ tsp salt, or to taste

Equipment:
• Large mixing bowl
  • Small bowl (for dressing)
  • Whisk or fork
  • Sharp knife and cutting board
  • Vegetable peeler (for broccoli stems)
  • Pot and bowl of ice water (if blanching)

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the Broccoli: Cut the broccoli into small, bite-sized florets — no larger than 2 cm (about ¾ inch). Don’t discard the stems — peel off the tough outer skin with a vegetable peeler and thinly slice the inner core into coins or matchsticks. The stems are sweet, crunchy, and just as good as the florets. For the best raw broccoli texture, make sure the florets are small and evenly sized so every bite gets dressing and mix-ins.
  2. Blanch (Optional but Recommended): For a more tender, less bitter broccoli, blanch the florets: bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, add the broccoli for exactly 60 seconds, then drain and immediately plunge into a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking. Drain and pat completely dry. This step softens the raw edge, brightens the color, and makes the broccoli more pleasant to eat while keeping it crunchy. Skip this step if you prefer fully raw and crisp.
  3. Make the Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together the vegan mayonnaise, tahini, apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, garlic powder, lemon juice, salt, and black pepper until completely smooth. Taste — it should be creamy, tangy, slightly sweet, and nutty. Adjust vinegar for more acidity, maple syrup for sweetness, or salt to taste. The dressing should seem quite bold on its own — it will mellow once tossed with the broccoli.
  4. Combine: In a large bowl, combine the broccoli florets and stems, finely diced red onion, dried cranberries or raisins, and most of the seeds (reserve a handful for topping). Pour the dressing over and toss thoroughly to coat every piece. The broccoli should be well-dressed but not swimming in dressing.
  5. Rest and Marinate: Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving — ideally 1–2 hours. The broccoli softens slightly, the cranberries plump up, and the whole salad becomes more cohesive and flavorful as it sits. This is one of those salads that genuinely improves with time. 1. Chill the Coconut Cream: The night before (or at least 4 hours ahead), place the can of full-fat coconut cream in the fridge. This allows the thick cream to solidify and separate from the liquid — you only want the thick, solid part. Do not shake the can.
  2. Make the Coffee Dipping Mixture: Combine the cooled espresso or strong coffee with the coffee liqueur or rum (if using) in a wide, shallow bowl. The coffee must be completely cool — hot coffee will turn the ladyfingers to mush instantly. Set aside.
  3. Make the Cream Layer: Open the chilled coconut cream can carefully — do not shake. Scoop out only the thick, solidified cream into a large mixing bowl, leaving behind the liquid (save it for smoothies). Add the vegan cream cheese, powdered sugar, vanilla extract, and lemon juice. Beat with an electric hand mixer or stand mixer on medium-high speed for 2–3 minutes until completely smooth, fluffy, and well combined. Taste — it should be rich, lightly sweet, and have a pleasant tang from the cream cheese and lemon. If it seems too stiff, add 1–2 tbsp of the reserved coconut liquid to loosen. Refrigerate while you prep the ladyfingers.
  4. Dip the Ladyfingers: Working quickly, dip each ladyfinger into the coffee mixture for exactly 1–2 seconds per side — no longer. Vegan ladyfingers absorb liquid faster than traditional ones. You want them soaked through but still holding their shape — not falling apart. If they feel slightly firm in the center, that’s correct — they will continue to soften as the tiramisu chills.
  5. First Layer: Arrange the dipped ladyfingers in a single, tight layer in the base of a 20 × 30 cm (8 × 12 inch) baking dish or equivalent deep serving dish. Snap ladyfingers to fill any gaps — no gaps means every slice gets full coverage. Spread half the cream mixture evenly over the ladyfinger layer using an offset spatula, smoothing to the edges.
  6. Second Layer: Repeat with a second layer of dipped ladyfingers, followed by the remaining cream mixture, spreading it smooth and level. The top layer of cream should be thick, flat, and even — this is what you’ll dust cocoa onto.
  7. Chill: Cover the dish tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours — overnight is ideal and gives significantly better results. The cream sets, the ladyfingers fully absorb the coffee, and the flavors deepen and meld together into something that tastes genuinely complex.
  8. Finish and Serve: Just before serving, use a fine mesh sieve to dust the top generously and evenly with unsweetened cocoa powder — a thick, even coat, not a light dusting. If using, scatter the finely grated dark chocolate over the cocoa. Slice and serve directly from the dish with a spatula. Serve cold.

Ingredients:

  • 1 tsp taco seasoning (optional)

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Prep the Cashew Sour Cream: Blend 130 g (1 cup) soaked raw cashews, 120 ml (½ cup) water, 15 ml (1 tbsp) lemon juice, 5 ml (1 tsp) apple cider vinegar, and ¼ tsp salt until completely smooth. Set aside.
  2. Layer the Beans: Mix 425 g (1 can) vegetarian refried beans with 1 tsp taco seasoning if using. Spread evenly into an 8×8-inch dish or shallow serving platter.
  3. Layer the Guacamole: Mash 2 ripe avocados with 15 ml (1 tbsp) lime juice and salt to taste. Spread over the bean layer.
  4. Layer the Cashew Sour Cream: Spread the cashew sour cream gently over the guacamole layer.
  5. Layer the Salsa: Spoon 240 ml (1 cup) drained salsa or pico de gallo evenly over the cashew sour cream.
  6. Add Cheese and Lettuce: Sprinkle with 115 g (1 cup) shredded vegan cheddar. Add 50 g (1 cup) shredded romaine or iceberg lettuce if desired.
  7. Add Toppings: Finish with 75 g (½ cup) chopped tomatoes, 35 g (¼ cup) sliced black olives, 10 g (2 tbsp) chopped green onions, 15 g (⅓ cup) fresh parsley, and jalapeño slices if using.
  8. Chill and Serve: Refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving with tortilla chips.

Prep: Make sure the cashews for the sour cream layer are fully soaked and soft before blending — under-soaked cashews leave a gritty texture that a food processor can't fully smooth out.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Not draining the salsa — watery salsa will make the layers soggy. Always drain excess liquid first. Adding toppings too early — lettuce and tomatoes should go on right before serving to stay fresh and crisp.

Notes: Soak cashews for 4 hours or boil for 10 minutes for the smoothest cashew sour cream. Spread each layer all the way to the edges of the dish for a tidy, layered presentation.

Prep in Advance: Make the cashew sour cream and refried bean layer up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate separately. Assemble the day of serving.

Storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Best assembled the day of serving.

Swaps: Replace cashew sour cream with store-bought vegan sour cream for a shortcut. Swap refried beans for black beans or pinto beans.

Tips: Add toppings right before serving to keep lettuce crisp and tomatoes fresh. Use a clear glass dish to show off all the beautiful layers.
Why These Ingredients:
Refried beans — the hearty, protein-rich base layer that anchors all the toppings and adds fiber and substance to every bite.

Avocados — provide creamy healthy fats and form the guacamole layer; lime juice prevents browning and adds brightness.

Raw cashews — blended with water, lemon juice, and vinegar to create a thick, tangy dairy-free sour cream that mimics the real thing.

Apple cider vinegar — adds the characteristic tang to the cashew sour cream that makes it taste like actual sour cream.

Salsa (drained) — draining removes excess liquid so the layers stay firm and don't make the dip watery or soggy.

Vegan cheddar — adds a melty, savory layer and familiar cheese flavor without dairy.

Romaine or iceberg lettuce — adds freshness and a cool crunch that balances the rich, creamy layers below.

Black olives — provide a briny, salty contrast to the creamy guacamole and sour cream layers.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cut the pomegranates: Using a sharp knife on a cutting board, cut each pomegranate in half crosswise.
  2. Extract the arils: Hold each half cut side down over a large bowl. Firmly tap the back of the skin with a wooden spoon to release the arils. Alternatively, break apart sections by hand and pick out the arils.
  3. Juice the arils: Place the arils in a citrus juicer and press firmly to extract all the juice. Alternatively, place arils in a large jar and mash with a potato masher until fully crushed.
  4. Strain: Pour the juice through a fine-mesh strainer into a pitcher, pressing the pulp with the back of a spoon to extract every drop. Discard the solids.
  5. Taste and adjust: If too tart, stir in 30 ml (2 tbsp) agave or maple syrup. If too concentrated, add 120 ml (½ cup) cold water.
  6. Serve: Pour over ice into glasses. Garnish with fresh mint if desired. Serve immediately for best flavor and nutrients.

Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Blender Method: Blend the arils with 60 ml (¼ cup) water for 20 seconds, then strain through cheesecloth or a fine-mesh strainer.
Common Mistakes: Don’t over-mash or blend on high speed — excessive agitation makes the juice bitter from the white pith and membranes.
Frozen Arils: Works well; thaw completely before juicing.
No Juicer: Use a potato masher or the blender method — no special equipment needed.
Storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container or jar for up to 3–5 days. Shake or stir before serving. Freeze in ice cube trays for up to 3 months — great for smoothies.
Sweetener Swap: Use stevia, honey, or skip entirely. Fresh pomegranate juice is naturally sweet-tart and rarely needs sweetening.

Pomegranates are the star — their arils are packed with punicalagins and anthocyanins, two of the most potent antioxidants found in any fruit. Fresh-squeezed juice retains far more of these compounds than store-bought, which is often pasteurized and stored for months. They are also a rich source of potassium, folate, and Vitamin K.

Cold water (optional) simply dilutes the intensity without sacrificing flavor — fresh pomegranate juice is very concentrated and some people prefer a lighter, more refreshing drink.

Agave or maple syrup (optional) balances tartness naturally. Pomegranates vary in sweetness depending on variety and ripeness, so this is purely to taste and can be skipped entirely.

Fresh mint adds a cooling aromatic note that complements the deep, tangy flavor of the juice without overpowering it — and makes for a beautiful garnish.

1. Press the tofu: Wrap 200 g (7 oz) firm tofu in a clean kitchen towel and press firmly for 5 minutes to remove excess moisture. Crumble into very fine, minced-meat-like pieces.
  2. Make the topping: In a food processor, pulse the onion, tomato, red bell pepper, and garlic until very finely chopped — not pureed. Transfer to a mixing bowl. Add the crumbled tofu, 30 ml (2 tbsp) tomato paste, 15 ml (1 tbsp) red pepper paste, 15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp allspice, chili flakes if using, and the chopped parsley. Prep:
Press the tofu: Wrap 200 g (7 oz) firm tofu in a clean kitchen towel and press firmly for 5 minutes to remove excess moisture. Crumble into very fine, minced-meat-like pieces.

Finely chop the vegetables: Pulse the onion, tomato, red bell pepper, and garlic in a food processor until very finely chopped — not pureed. Alternatively chop very finely by hand.

Chop the parsley: Finely chop 20 g (⅓ cup) fresh flat-leaf parsley for the topping. Set aside extra for serving.

Slice the onion: Thinly slice 1 medium white or yellow onion for serving. Set aside.

Preheat oven to 220°C (430°F). If using a pizza stone or cast iron pan, place it in the oven now to heat up.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Don’t overload the tortilla — a thin, even layer of topping is key. Too thick and the center stays wet and the tortilla goes soggy.

Dough Option: Replace tortillas with homemade or store-bought pizza dough rolled very thin for a more traditional result. Bake at 230°C (450°F) for 5–8 minutes.

Extra Crispy: Place the baking sheet on the lowest rack or use a preheated pizza stone for a crispier base.

Prep Ahead: The tofu topping can be made up to 24 hours in advance and refrigerated. Spread and bake the tortillas fresh.

Serving: Always serve rolled up with sliced onion, fresh parsley, and lots of lemon — this is essential to the lahmacun experience.

Storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftover topping keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Assembled lahmacun can be refrigerated for 1 day and re-crisped in the oven at 200°C (400°F) for 5 minutes.

Tofu Swap: Replace tofu with finely chopped walnuts or lentils for a different texture. Walnuts give a slightly meaty, rich flavor.
Why These Ingredients:
Firm tofu — replaces the traditional lamb or beef mince. Pressing out excess moisture is essential so it crumbles finely and cooks dry rather than steaming, mimicking the texture of ground meat.

Onion, tomato, and red bell pepper — the aromatic vegetable base of the topping. Pulsing them finely in a food processor (rather than chopping roughly) creates the wet, spreadable paste that is the hallmark of authentic lahmacun.

Tomato paste — concentrates the tomato flavor and adds body and color to the topping, helping it caramelize in the oven.

Red pepper paste (biber salçası) — a staple in Turkish cooking that adds deep, slightly sweet heat and a rich brick-red color. Tomato paste can substitute but the flavor is milder.

Olive oil — binds the topping together and helps it caramelize beautifully in the oven without drying out.

Cumin, smoked paprika, and allspice — the spice trio that gives lahmacun its distinctive warm, earthy, slightly smoky flavor profile that is unmistakably Middle Eastern.

Fresh flat-leaf parsley — mixed into the topping and served fresh on top; brightens the rich spiced flavors and is a non-negotiable part of authentic lahmacun.

Flour tortillas — a quick shortcut for the traditional yeast dough base. They crisp up beautifully at high heat and give the same thin, slightly charred result in a fraction of the time.

Lemon and sumac (to serve) — the acidity is essential to lahmacun — always squeeze generously. Sumac adds a fruity tartness that echoes the traditional flavor.

Sliced onion (to serve) — traditionally rolled inside lahmacun for freshness and crunch. Not optional — it’s part of how the dish is meant to be eaten.

Prep:
Carrots: Peel, wash, and pat completely dry. Cut into 5 cm (2-inch) matchsticks about ½ cm (¼ inch) thick.

Chilies: Slit lengthwise. Leave seeds in for heat, remove for mild.

Ginger (optional): Peel and cut into thin matchsticks matching the carrot size.

Garlic (optional): Thinly slice.

Jar: Pour hot water into the mason jar, let sit 1–2 minutes, drain, and let cool completely before filling.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Don’t skip drying the carrots completely — moisture causes the pickle to go bad quickly. Don’t grind the spices to a powder — coarse crushing gives better texture and flavor.
Garlic & Ginger: Both optional but add great depth — ginger adds warmth and freshness, garlic adds savoriness. Add one, both, or neither.
Mustard Oil: Traditional and best for authentic flavor. Heat until smoking to mellow its sharpness, then cool before adding. If unavailable, use a neutral oil — milder but still delicious.
Prep Ahead: Make up to 3 days ahead — it actually improves significantly after 24–48 hours as the spices infuse.
Storage: Refrigerate in an airtight glass jar for up to 6–8 months. Always use a clean, dry spoon — never wet.
Sweeter Version: Add 1 tsp jaggery or brown sugar for a sweet-sour variation popular in Gujarat.
Vinegar Swap: Replace white vinegar with apple cider vinegar for a slightly fruitier tang.
Why These Ingredients:
Carrots are the hero — firm enough to hold up to the acid and spices without going soft, and sweet enough to balance the heat and tang. Use fresh, firm carrots — soft or older carrots will turn mushy after a day.

Mustard oil is the traditional choice and gives the pickle its characteristic pungency and depth. Heating it to smoking point removes the harsh raw flavor and brings out a nutty, rounded warmth. It’s irreplaceable for the most authentic result — neutral oil works but the flavor will be noticeably milder.

Mustard seeds form the flavor backbone of the pickle alongside the oil. Coarsely crushed rather than ground, they add bursts of sharp, nutty heat in each bite.

Fenugreek seeds (methi dana) add a slightly bitter, earthy note that is essential to classic Indian pickle flavor. Use sparingly — too much becomes unpleasantly bitter.

Fennel seeds add a subtle sweetness and anise-like fragrance that lifts the overall spice blend and balances the heat.

Turmeric adds warm color and mild earthiness, and has natural preservative properties that help extend the pickle’s shelf life.

Red chili powder provides the heat. Kashmiri chili powder gives a beautiful deep red color with mild heat — ideal for a visually striking, moderately spiced pickle. Cayenne gives more heat with less color.

Lemon juice provides bright, fresh acidity that wakes up all the spices. It works alongside vinegar but has a fresher, more complex flavor than vinegar alone.

White vinegar is the primary preservative — it lowers the pH enough to keep the pickle shelf-stable for months. It also sharpens and deepens the tang over time as the pickle rests.

1. Boil pasta water: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil.

Prep:
Soak the cashews — cover 60 g (½ cup) raw cashews with boiling water, remove from heat, and soak for 20 minutes until softened. Drain before blending. This is the most important prep step — under-soaked cashews produce a grainy sauce.

Mince the garlic and shallot — finely mince all 10 garlic cloves and 1 shallot so they cook evenly and quickly once the pan is hot.

Measure and set aside the vodka and tomatoes — the sauce moves fast once you start; having everything measured and ready prevents burning.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil so the pasta is ready to drop when the sauce is simmering.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Not soaking cashews long enough — under-soaked cashews produce a grainy sauce instead of a silky one. Always soak for the full 20 minutes in hot water, or soak overnight in cold water. Boiling the sauce — once the cashew cream is added, keep heat at a gentle simmer. A hard boil can cause the sauce to separate. Not reserving pasta water — the starch in pasta water is essential for loosening and emulsifying the sauce. Always reserve at least 240 ml (1 cup) before draining. Rushing the vodka cook-off — the vodka needs to simmer for at least 5 minutes to cook off the raw alcohol taste. Don’t skip or shorten this step. Using pre-minced jarred garlic — fresh garlic makes a significant difference here. Finely mince fresh cloves for the best flavor.

Notes: Cashew cream vs. dairy cream — blended cashews with vegetable broth create a sauce that is nearly indistinguishable from a heavy cream vodka sauce — silky, rich, and slightly sweet. San Marzano tomatoes — sweeter and less acidic than standard crushed tomatoes. Worth seeking out for this recipe. Look for DOP-certified cans. Vodka — use a smooth, neutral mid-range vodka. No need for anything premium.

Prep in Advance: The sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Reheat gently on the stovetop with a splash of pasta water to loosen. Cook the pasta fresh. Cashews can be soaked up to 24 hours ahead — drain, cover, and refrigerate until ready to blend.

Storage: Refrigerator — store sauce and pasta separately in airtight containers for up to 4 days. Storing them together causes the pasta to absorb the sauce. Freezer — the sauce freezes well for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat on the stovetop with a splash of water. Do not freeze cooked pasta.

Tips: Add pasta water gradually — a little at a time until the sauce reaches a silky, coating consistency. Finish the pasta in the sauce rather than pouring sauce over plated pasta — tossing in the pan helps the sauce cling to every piece. Top with extra vegan Parmesan and fresh basil right before serving for the best presentation.

Swaps: Gluten-free — use your favorite gluten-free penne. All other ingredients are naturally gluten-free. Nut-free — substitute raw sunflower seeds for the cashews, soaked for the same 20 minutes. Optional add-ins — vegan Italian sausage, crispy tofu, mushrooms, spinach, zucchini, or cherry tomatoes all work well stirred into the finished sauce. Oregano — if using fresh oregano, use 3× the amount (about 4 g / 1½ tbsp).
Why These Ingredients: Raw cashews are the vegan secret to a luscious, creamy sauce — they blend into a silky base that mimics heavy cream perfectly. San Marzano tomatoes bring sweetness and depth with less acidity than standard crushed tomatoes. Vodka acts as an emulsifier, helping the tomato and cream components meld together while amplifying the sauce's aroma (the alcohol fully cooks off). Shallot and 10 cloves of garlic create a bold, savory foundation. Tomato paste concentrates the umami and adds body. Fresh basil keeps the sauce bright and herbaceous, and vegan Parmesan rounds it all out with a salty, cheesy finish.

Name: How to Keep Onion Powder from Clumping
Features: 20-minutes-or-less; gluten-free; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free
Common Ingredients: onion
Ingredients:
• Onion powder — your jar (any size)
  • 1 g food-safe silica gel packet (FDA compliant) — for jars under 4 oz (113 g)
  • 2 g food-safe silica gel packet — for 4–8 oz (113–227 g) jars
  • 5 g food-safe silica gel packet — for larger containers
  • Airtight glass spice jar
  • Dry paper towel
  • Dry spoon or spice scoop
  • Rimmed baking sheet
  • Oven set to 120°C (250°F)
Equipment:
• Dry paper towel
  • Airtight glass spice jar
  • Dry spoon or spice scoop
  • Rimmed baking sheet (for recharging only)
  • Oven set to 120°C (250°F) (for recharging only)
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Use a food-safe silica packet only: Look for packets labeled "food safe" or "FDA compliant" — the type found in beef jerky, seaweed snacks, and vitamin bottles. Do not reuse packets from shoe boxes, electronics, or handbags.
  2. Make sure the jar and spice are completely dry: Wipe the inside of your jar with a dry paper towel. Never add a silica packet to a jar that has moisture or has been splashed near the stove.
  3. Drop one packet into the jar: Place one small silica packet directly into the jar. Use a 1 g packet for jars under 4 oz, a 2 g packet for 4–8 oz jars, and a 5 g packet for larger containers.
  4. Seal with an airtight lid: Close the jar tightly. The silica packet absorbs ambient moisture inside the sealed container — the tighter the seal, the better it works.
  5. Never scoop over the stove: Steam from pots and pans is the number one cause of spice clumping. Always bring the jar away from heat before opening, and use a completely dry spoon.
  6. Recharge the packet every 2–3 months: When the packet feels heavier or slightly firm, place it on a baking sheet at 120°C (250°F) for 30 minutes. Let cool completely before returning to the jar.

Check the packet size — use a 1 g packet for jars under 4 oz, 2 g for 4–8 oz jars, and 5 g for larger containers.

Common Mistakes: Adding moisture first — never add a packet to a wet or recently steamed jar; moisture overwhelms the packet instantly. Non-food-safe packets — shoe box and electronics desiccants may contain unsafe additives. Always confirm the packet is FDA compliant. Scooping over the stove — steam is the number one cause of clumping. Always step away before opening the jar. Undersized packet — when in doubt go one size up; too small means faster saturation. Notes: All powdered spices benefit — garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, and any blend with sugar all clump by the same mechanism. Indicator packets recommended — color-change packets (blue to pink, or orange to green) tell you exactly when to recharge. Reusable for years — a single food-safe packet can be recharged many times. Label the jar with the date you added the packet so you know when the next recharge is due.

Name: Chocolate Chip Cookie Minis (Vegan)

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat the oven: Preheat to 350°F (176°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Mix the dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together 90 g (¾ cup) all-purpose flour, 75 g (¾ cup) oat flour, 3 g (½ tsp) salt, and 2 g (½ tsp) baking powder until evenly combined.
  3. Mix the wet ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk together 113 g (½ cup) melted vegan butter, 120 ml (½ cup) maple syrup, 60 ml (¼ cup) corn syrup, and 5 ml (1 tsp) vanilla extract until smooth.
  4. Combine into a dough: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until a thick, sticky dough forms. Fold in 85 g (½ cup) finely chopped vegan chocolate chips until evenly distributed.

  7. Bake: Bake at 350°F (176°C) for 10 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the pieces look dry and crisp.
  8. Cool completely: Let cool on the baking sheet for 15–20 minutes — the pieces crisp up further as they cool. Once cool, break apart along the scored lines.

Common Mistakes: Cutting pieces too large — large squares stay chewy in the center instead of crisping all the way through. Keep pieces to 1–1.5 cm. Not rolling thin enough — a thick dough sheet won't crisp up into true cereal texture. Aim for 3 mm (⅛ inch). Pulling from the oven too early — the cereal continues to crisp as it cools, but it needs to be golden and dry-looking before coming out. Skipping the cooling time — the pieces are soft straight from the oven and firm up significantly as they cool. Don't break them apart while warm. Using whole chocolate chips — large chips create uneven, chunky pieces. Chop them finely so they distribute evenly through the thin dough.

Vegan butter brands vary — stick-style vegan butters tend to perform more like dairy butter than tub-style spreads; sticks are recommended for best texture.

Prep in Advance: The dough can be made up to 2 days ahead and stored wrapped in the refrigerator. Let it sit at room temperature for 10 minutes before rolling, as cold dough is harder to roll thin.

Storage: Room temperature — store in an airtight container for up to 1 week. If the cereal softens over time, re-crisp in a 300°F (150°C) oven for 5 minutes. Freezer — freeze in a sealed bag for up to 1 month. Thaw at room temperature; re-crisp in the oven if needed.

Oat flour — combined with all-purpose flour, oat flour adds a slightly nutty flavor and helps the dough crisp up into a true cereal-like texture rather than staying soft like a traditional cookie.

Vegan butter — stick-style vegan butter mimics the fat structure of dairy butter closely enough to create the same crisp, golden edges without any animal products.

Corn syrup — works alongside maple syrup to keep the dough pliable for rolling thin and helps the baked pieces achieve a glossy, crisp finish rather than a dry, crumbly one.

Finely chopped vegan chocolate chips — chopping (rather than using whole chips) lets the chocolate distribute evenly through the very thin dough, so every small cereal piece gets a bit of chocolate instead of a few pieces hogging it all.

Name: Watermelon Feta Cake (Vegan)
Features: gluten-free; raw; grain-free; soy-free; oil-free; refined-sugar-free; nut-free
Common Ingredients: cucumber; watermelon; mint; salt; feta
Ingredients:
• 1 large seedless watermelon
  • 200 g (7 oz) vegan feta cheese
  • 300 g (1) English cucumber
  • 20 fresh mint leaves
  • Flaky sea salt, to taste
Equipment:
• Sharp chef’s knife
  • Cutting board
  • Wire rack
  • Baking sheet (to catch drips during chilling)
  • Paper towels
  • Cake stand or large serving plate
  • Offset spatula or butter knife
  • Mandoline (optional, for even cucumber slices)
Nutrition:
Servings 8  Calories 150  Carbohydrates 24 g  Fat 5 g  Fiber 2 g  Protein 3 g
‍Monounsaturated 1.5 g  Polyunsaturated 0.5 g  Saturated 2.5 g  Trans 0 g
‍Vitamin A 310 mcg  Vitamin C 18 mg  Vitamin D 0 mcg
‍Calcium 55 mg  Iron 1 mg  Potassium 320 mg
‍Cholesterol 0 mg  Sodium 280 mg  Sugar 18 g
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cut the watermelon rounds: Stand the watermelon upright and slice off both ends to create flat bases. Cut crosswise into three even rounds, each 4–5 cm (1½–2 inches) thick. Trim the rind off each round to create clean circles. Pat each round very dry with paper towels — this is essential for the feta to stick.
  2. Chill the watermelon: Place the rounds on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Refrigerate uncovered for at least 30 minutes — ideally 1 hour to draw out excess surface moisture.
  3. Prep the cucumber: Thinly slice into rounds 2–3 mm thick. Pat dry with paper towels. Set aside.
  4. Assemble the first layer: Place the largest watermelon round on your cake stand or serving plate. Crumble half the vegan feta (100 g / 3.5 oz) evenly across the top. Arrange a single layer of cucumber slices over the feta, slightly overlapping.
  5. Add the second layer: Place the second watermelon round on top and press down very gently. Crumble the remaining 100 g (3.5 oz) vegan feta over the top. Add another layer of cucumber slices.
  6. Add the third layer and chill: Place the final watermelon round on top and press gently. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before decorating.
  7. Decorate and serve: Arrange cucumber slices decoratively across the top. Tuck 20 fresh mint leaves between and around the cucumber. Finish with a pinch of flaky sea salt. Slice with a sharp knife wiped clean between each cut and serve immediately.

Choose a round watermelon — the more cylindrical the watermelon, the more even your three rounds will be.

Chill the watermelon before cutting — a cold watermelon holds its shape better and releases less surface moisture during the resting step.

Clear fridge space — you’ll need room for a wire rack with three watermelon rounds, then later the full assembled cake on its stand.

Pat everything dry — watermelon, cucumber, and even the serving plate should be as dry as possible before assembly.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Not drying the watermelon thoroughly — skipping the paper towel step means the feta slides right off. Dry each round well before chilling and again just before assembling. Assembling too far in advance — watermelon releases water over time; assemble no more than 2 hours before serving. Cutting rounds too thin — rounds thinner than 4 cm will crack under the weight. Keep each layer at least 4 cm thick. Not chilling between steps — both resting steps are essential for clean slicing. Don’t skip them. Using a blunt knife — a dull knife drags and tears the watermelon flesh. Use the sharpest knife you own.

Notes: Best served the same day — the assembled cake is best within 2 hours of assembly. Round watermelons work best — more spherical watermelons produce more even, symmetrical rounds that stack neatly. Vegan feta brands vary — some are saltier or drier than others. Taste before crumbling and adjust flaky salt accordingly.

Prep in Advance: Watermelon rounds can be cut, dried, and chilled up to 1 day ahead on a wire rack in the fridge. Pat dry again just before assembling. Cucumber slices can be cut and stored in a sealed container up to 1 day ahead. Pat dry before using.

Storage: The assembled cake does not store well overnight. If you have leftovers, separate the layers and wrap each watermelon round individually. Store feta and cucumber separately and consume within 1 day.

Tips: Use a mandoline for cucumber slices — ultra-thin, even slices look far more polished as decoration. Add the mint just before serving — mint wilts quickly on a cold surface. A cake turntable makes arranging the cucumber and mint much easier.

Swaps: Dairy feta can replace vegan feta if not vegan — remove the (Vegan) label from the recipe name. Persian cucumbers work well in place of English cucumber — use 2–3 small ones. Basil or dill can replace or mix with the mint for a different flavor profile. Lemon zest scattered on top adds brightness alongside the mint.
Why These Ingredients:
Watermelon rounds — three thick cross-sections of a whole watermelon create the structural layers without any baking. Thickness (4–5 cm) and thorough drying are the two non-negotiables — watermelon is over 90% water, so surface moisture is what causes everything to slide.

Vegan feta — its salty, tangy flavor is the perfect contrast to sweet watermelon. Used crumbled rather than blended it adds texture to every layer and creates the signature savory-sweet balance this cake is built on.

Cucumber — adds cool crunch between the layers and doubles as elegant decoration on top. Thinly sliced rounds overlap neatly and stay crisp much longer than leafy greens.

Fresh mint — mint and watermelon is one of the most classic summer pairings. Used only as decoration so it stays vibrant and doesn’t wilt into the cake before serving.

Flaky sea salt — a final pinch over the top amplifies both the sweetness of the watermelon and the savoriness of the feta, tying the whole cake together.

1. Activate the Yeast: In a bowl, combine the warm water, sugar, and yeast. Let sit for 5-10 minutes, until foamy.
  2. Mix & Knead the Dough: In a large bowl, mix the flour and salt. Add the yeast mixture and 2 tablespoons of olive oil, and stir until a shaggy dough forms. Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic (or use a stand mixer with a dough hook).

  8. Bake: Bake for 20-25 minutes, until golden brown. Cool slightly before slicing.

Ingredients:

  • 1/2 tsp ajwain (carom seeds), optional
  • 3 g (1/2 tsp) salt

  • 72.5 g (1/2 cup) green peas

  • 2 g (1 tsp) grated ginger
  • 1 green chili, minced (optional)

  • 1/2 tsp ground coriander
  • 0.6 g (1/4 tsp) turmeric

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Make the Dough: Mix the flour, ajwain, and salt in a bowl. Rub in the oil until crumbly, then gradually add cold water to form a firm dough. Cover and rest for 20-30 minutes.
  2. Toast the Cumin: Meanwhile, heat a little oil in a pan and toast the cumin seeds until fragrant.
  3. Make the Filling: Add ginger and green chili, cooking for 30 seconds, then stir in the peas, mashed potatoes, garam masala, coriander, turmeric, and salt. Cook for 3-4 minutes and set aside to cool.
  4. Shape the Wrappers: Divide the dough into small balls, roll each into an oval, and cut in half to form two semi-circles.
  5. Fill & Seal: Shape each half into a cone, fill with the potato mixture, and seal the edges with a little water.
  6. Heat the Oil & Fry: Heat oil in a deep pan to 325°F (160°C). Fry the samosas in batches for 8-10 minutes, until golden and crisp.
  7. Drain & Serve: Drain on paper towels and serve hot with chutney.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Fry the Onion: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the sliced onion until deeply golden and crispy. Remove half for garnish and set aside.
  2. Bloom the Spices: Add the cumin seeds, cinnamon, cardamom, and bay leaves to the remaining onion and oil, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
  3. Add Vegetables & Aromatics: Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and mixed vegetables, cooking for 3-4 minutes.
  4. Season: Add the garam masala, turmeric, and salt, then stir in the vegan yogurt.
  5. Add the Rice: Add the drained rice and gently mix to combine with the vegetables and spices.
  6. Add the Liquid: Pour in the water or broth and bring to a boil.
  7. Simmer: Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook for 18-20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
  8. Rest & Fluff: Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
  9. Garnish & Serve: Garnish with the reserved crispy onions, cilantro, and mint before serving.

  3. Add Garlic & Ginger: Add the garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
  4. Build the Sauce: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, garam masala, smoked paprika, cumin, and turmeric. Simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

  6. Add Coconut Milk & Butter: Stir in the coconut milk, vegan butter, maple syrup, and salt. Simmer for 5 minutes.

  8. Garnish & Serve: Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with rice or naan.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Prep: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. Whisk the Dry Ingredients: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
  3. Cream the Butter & Sugar: In a large bowl, cream the vegan butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes.
  4. Add the Wet Ingredients: Beat in the plant milk, flax mixture, and vanilla extract until combined.
  5. Combine: Gradually mix in the dry ingredients until a soft dough forms.
  6. Scoop & Roll: Scoop the dough into 1 1/2 tablespoon balls, roll in extra sugar, and place on the prepared baking sheets, spacing about 2 inches apart.
  7. Flatten: Flatten each ball slightly with the bottom of a glass.
  8. Bake: Bake for 9-11 minutes, until the edges are just set but the centers are still soft.
  9. Cool: Let cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Soak the Noodles: Soak the rice noodles until pliable, then drain.
  2. Sear the Tofu: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok and pan-fry the tofu until golden. Remove and set aside.
  3. Sauté the Aromatics: Add the remaining oil, garlic, and Thai chilies, stir-frying for 30 seconds.
  4. Add the Bell Pepper: Add the bell pepper and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
  5. Add the Noodles & Sauce: Add the noodles, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and brown sugar, tossing to combine.
  6. Return the Tofu & Add Basil: Return the tofu to the wok and stir in the Thai basil until just wilted.
  7. Serve: Serve immediately.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Mix dry ingredients: In a bowl, whisk together the 90 g (3/4 cup) all-purpose flour, 8 g (2 tsp) baking powder, and 0.75 g (1/8 tsp) salt.
  2. Mix wet ingredients: In a separate bowl or measuring cup, whisk together the 120 ml (1/2 cup) dairy-free milk and 7.5 ml (1/2 tbsp) apple cider vinegar and let sit for 1 minute to slightly curdle (this mimics buttermilk for extra fluffiness). Whisk in the 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup, 15 g (1 tbsp) apple sauce, and 4 ml (1 tsp) vanilla extract.
  3. Combine: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and gently stir just until combined. A few small lumps are fine — do not overmix, or the pancake will turn out dense.
  4. Rest the batter: Let the batter sit for 5 minutes so the baking powder can activate, giving you a fluffier pancake.
  5. Cook: Heat a 10-inch nonstick griddle or skillet over medium heat. A light spray of oil is optional but not required. Pour the batter into the pan. Cook until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set, about 2-3 minutes, then flip and cook another 1-2 minutes until golden brown.
  6. Cool: Transfer to a cooling rack for 1-2 minutes so the pancake doesn't steam and go soggy underneath.
  7. Serve: Serve warm with extra maple syrup.

1. Sear the Tofu: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp on all sides. Remove and set aside.

Ingredients:
• 170 g (1 cup) cooked quinoa
  • 135 g (1 1/2 cups) rolled oats
  • 48 g (1/2 cup) almond flour
  • 2.3 g (1/2 tsp) baking soda
  • 1.3 g (1/2 tsp) ground cinnamon

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Prep: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

  3. Combine the Wet Ingredients: In a separate bowl, mix the mashed banana, maple syrup, nut butter, oil, and vanilla until smooth.
  4. Combine & Fold In Mix-Ins: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir to combine. Fold in the cooked quinoa, dried fruit, nuts, and chia seeds if using.
  5. Scoop & Flatten: Scoop 2-tablespoon mounds of dough onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart. Flatten each slightly with the back of a spoon — these cookies won't spread much on their own.
  6. Bake: Bake for 12-14 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden. Cool on the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

Name: No-Bake Peanut Butter Cups
Common Ingredients: peanut-butter; chocolate-chips; maple-syrup; salt; oat-flour; graham-crackers; coconut-oil
Ingredients:
• For the peanut butter filling:
  • 258 g (1 cup) natural peanut butter
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) maple syrup or melted coconut oil
  • 25 g (1/4 cup) graham cracker crumbs or oat flour
  • 1.5 g (1/4 tsp) salt
  • For the chocolate shell:
  • 255 g (1 1/2 cups) dairy-free chocolate chips
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) coconut oil
  • Flaky sea salt, for topping (optional)
Equipment:
• 12-cup muffin tin
  • Paper or silicone muffin liners
  • Microwave-safe bowl
  • Small spoon
Nutrition: Approximate per cup (12 cups): 260 calories, 6g protein, 18g fat, 22g carbohydrates, 2g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Line the Muffin Tin: Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper or silicone liners.
  2. Make the Filling: In a bowl, mix the peanut butter, maple syrup, graham cracker crumbs, and salt until it forms a thick, moldable dough.
  3. Melt the Chocolate: Melt the chocolate chips and coconut oil together in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring between each, until smooth.
  4. Coat the Bottoms: Spoon about 1 tsp of melted chocolate into the bottom of each liner and tilt to coat the bottom evenly. Freeze for 5-10 minutes, until set.
  5. Shape & Layer: Roll the peanut butter mixture into 12 balls and flatten each into a disc. Place one disc on top of the chocolate layer in each liner.
  6. Top with Chocolate: Spoon the remaining melted chocolate over the peanut butter layer, spreading to cover completely. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt if desired.
  7. Freeze & Serve: Freeze for at least 30 minutes, until fully set. Store in the freezer or fridge and let sit a few minutes at room temperature before eating.

Name: Tempeh Bacon
Common Ingredients: tempeh; maple-syrup; garlic-powder; smoked-paprika; black-pepper; apple-cider-vinegar; neutral-oil; liquid-smoke-02f08; soy-sauce-e7086; tamari-de23a
Ingredients:
• 226.8 g (8 oz) tempeh
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) soy sauce or tamari
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) maple syrup
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) apple cider vinegar
  • 1 tbsp liquid smoke
  • 2.3 g (1 tsp) smoked paprika
  • 1.5 g (1/2 tsp) garlic powder
  • 0.5 g (1/4 tsp) black pepper

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Steam the Tempeh: Bring a small pot of water to a boil and steam or simmer the tempeh strips for 5-10 minutes to remove bitterness. Drain and pat dry.
  2. Make the Marinade: In a shallow dish, whisk together the soy sauce, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, liquid smoke, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and pepper.
  3. Marinate: Add the steamed tempeh strips to the marinade, gently tossing to coat. Let marinate for at least 15 minutes, or up to overnight in the fridge.
  4. Sear: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the tempeh strips in a single layer, reserving the leftover marinade.
  5. Cook Until Crisp: Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until browned and crisp at the edges, brushing with extra marinade partway through.
  6. Drain & Serve: Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and serve warm.

Name: Turmeric Rice
Common Ingredients: garlic; cilantro; parsley; rice; cashews; vegan-butter; almonds; onion; salt; vegetable-broth; olive-oil; cumin; black-pepper; turmeric-95970
Ingredients:
• 277.5 g (1 1/2 cups) long-grain white rice
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil or vegan butter
  • 80 g (1/2 small) onion
  • 6 g (2 cloves) garlic
  • 3.4 g (1 1/2 tsp) ground turmeric
  • 1 g (1/2 tsp) ground cumin
  • 0.5 g (1/4 tsp) black pepper
  • 540 ml (2 1/4 cups) vegetable broth or water
  • 3 g (1/2 tsp) salt
  • 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro or parsley, for garnish
  • 2 tbsp toasted slivered almonds or cashews (optional)
Equipment:
• Medium saucepan with lid
  • Fine-mesh strainer
  • Fork, for fluffing
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (4 servings): 320 calories, 5g protein, 7g fat, 55g carbohydrates, 1g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Rinse the Rice: Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Drain well.
  2. Sauté the Onion: Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3-4 minutes, until softened.
  3. Bloom the Spices: Add the garlic, turmeric, cumin, and black pepper. Stir constantly for 30-60 seconds, until fragrant.
  4. Toast the Rice: Add the drained rice and stir to coat every grain in the oil and spices, toasting for 1-2 minutes.
  5. Simmer: Pour in the broth and salt, and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
  6. Rest & Fluff: Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, then top with cilantro and toasted nuts if using.

Name: Pineapple Upside-Down Cake

• For the topping:
  • 56.8 g (1/4 cup) vegan butter
  • 142 g (2/3 cup) packed brown sugar
  • 567 g (1 (20 oz) can) pineapple rings
  • 6-8 maraschino cherries
  • For the cake:
  • 180 g (1 1/2 cups) all-purpose flour
  • 7 g (1 1/2 tsp) baking powder
  • 1.5 g (1/4 tsp) salt
  • 113.5 g (1/2 cup) vegan butter
  • 150 g (3/4 cup) granulated sugar
  • 30 g (2) flax eggs
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 120 ml (1/2 cup) unsweetened plant milk
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) reserved pineapple juice
Equipment:
• 9-inch round cake pan
  • Two mixing bowls
  • Hand or stand mixer
  • Serving plate, for inverting
Nutrition: Approximate per slice (8 slices): 430 calories, 5g protein, 19g fat, 62g carbohydrates, 1g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Make the Caramel Base: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Melt the 1/4 cup vegan butter and pour it into a 9-inch round cake pan, tilting to coat the bottom evenly.
  2. Arrange the Fruit: Sprinkle the brown sugar evenly over the butter. Arrange the pineapple rings on top, filling gaps with cherries.

Name: Gochujang Tofu
Common Ingredients: garlic; green-onions; rice; tofu; maple-syrup; sesame-seeds-2; neutral-oil; brown-sugar; cornstarch-0db33; ginger-b4168; gochujang-9684a; sesame-oil-c6ff4; soy-sauce-e7086
Ingredients:
• 1 block (14 oz) extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed
  • 24 g (3 tbsp) cornstarch
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) neutral oil
  • 2 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste)
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) soy sauce
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) rice vinegar
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup or brown sugar
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) sesame oil
  • 6 g (2 cloves) garlic
  • 2 g (1 tsp) fresh ginger
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) water
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
  • 320 g (2) green onions
Equipment:
• Large non-stick skillet or wok
  • Small mixing bowl
  • Paper towels or tofu press
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (4 servings): 250 calories, 14g protein, 15g fat, 16g carbohydrates, 2g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Coat the Tofu: Toss the cubed tofu with the cornstarch until evenly coated on all sides.
  2. Sear the Tofu: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Remove and set aside.
  3. Make the Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup, sesame oil, and water to make the sauce.
  4. Sauté the Aromatics: Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the pan. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
  5. Simmer the Sauce: Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 1 minute, until it thickens slightly.
  6. Combine: Return the tofu to the pan and toss to coat evenly in the sauce, cooking for another 1-2 minutes.
  7. Garnish & Serve: Remove from heat, garnish with sesame seeds and green onions, and serve over rice.

Name: Peanut Butter Granola
Common Ingredients: chia-seeds; oats; peanut-butter; chocolate-chips; maple-syrup; walnuts; almonds; flaxseeds; salt; cinnamon; vanilla-extract; neutral-oil; coconut-oil
Ingredients:
• 270 g (3 cups) rolled oats
  • 1/2 cup chopped nuts (peanuts, almonds, or walnuts)
  • 42 g (1/4 cup) chia seeds or ground flaxseed
  • 1.3 g (1/2 tsp) ground cinnamon
  • 1.5 g (1/4 tsp) salt
  • 172 g (2/3 cup) peanut butter
  • 80 ml (1/3 cup) maple syrup
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) neutral oil or melted coconut oil
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 85 g (1/2 cup) dried fruit or chocolate chips
Equipment:
• Large baking sheet
  • Parchment paper
  • Large mixing bowl
  • Small saucepan or microwave-safe bowl
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (10 servings, about 1/2 cup each): 320 calories, 9g protein, 18g fat, 28g carbohydrates, 4g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Prep: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Combine the Dry Ingredients: In a large bowl, mix the oats, nuts, chia seeds, cinnamon, and salt.
  3. Warm the Wet Ingredients: In a small saucepan or microwave, warm the peanut butter, maple syrup, and oil together until smooth and pourable. Stir in the vanilla.
  4. Combine: Pour the wet mixture over the dry ingredients and stir until every bit of oats is coated.
  5. Spread on the Sheet: Spread the mixture in an even layer on the prepared baking sheet, pressing down firmly with a spatula for extra-clumpy granola.
  6. Bake: Bake for 20-25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until golden brown. For big clusters, don't stir and instead just rotate the pan.
  7. Cool & Break: Cool completely on the pan without disturbing it — this is what forms the clusters. Once cool, break into pieces and stir in dried fruit or chocolate chips if using.
