Name: Baked Vanilla Glazed Donuts
Common Ingredients: flax-egg; all-purpose-flour; plant-milk; vegan-butter; salt; sugar; vanilla-extract; nutmeg; powdered-sugar; baking-powder-3e21e
Ingredients:
• For the donuts:
  • 180 g (1 1/2 cups) all-purpose flour
  • 100 g (1/2 cup) granulated sugar
  • 7 g (1 1/2 tsp) baking powder
  • 1.5 g (1/4 tsp) salt
  • 1.2 g (1/2 tsp) ground nutmeg
  • 120 ml (1/2 cup) unsweetened plant milk
  • 30 g (2) flax eggs
  • 2 tbsp melted vegan butter
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • For the glaze:
  • 180 g (1 1/2 cups) powdered sugar
  • 2-3 tbsp plant milk
  • 2.2 g (1/2 tsp) vanilla extract
Equipment:
• Donut pan (6-cavity)
  • Two mixing bowls
  • Piping bag or zip-top bag with corner snipped, for filling the pan
  • Wire cooling rack
Nutrition: Approximate per donut (12 donuts): 160 calories, 2g protein, 3g fat, 30g carbohydrates, 0g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Prep: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a donut pan.
  2. Combine the Dry Ingredients: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg in a large bowl.
  3. Combine the Wet Ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk the plant milk, flax eggs, melted vegan butter, and vanilla until combined.
  4. Combine Wet & Dry: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until smooth — don't overmix.
  5. Fill the Donut Pan: Spoon or pipe the batter into the donut pan cavities, filling each about two-thirds full.
  6. Bake & Cool: Bake for 9-11 minutes, until the donuts spring back when touched and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
  7. Glaze: Whisk together the powdered sugar, plant milk, and vanilla for the glaze. Once the donuts are fully cool, dip the tops in the glaze and let set for a few minutes before serving.

Name: Homemade Oreos
Common Ingredients: all-purpose-flour; cocoa-powder; baking-soda; salt; vegan-butter; sugar; flax-egg; vanilla-extract; powdered-sugar; plant-milk
Ingredients:
• For the cookies:
  • 150 g (1 1/4 cups) all-purpose flour
  • 45 g (1/2 cup) unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 4.7 g (1 tsp) baking soda
  • 1.5 g (1/4 tsp) salt
  • 170.2 g (3/4 cup) vegan butter
  • 200 g (1 cup) granulated sugar
  • 15 g (1) flax egg
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • For the cream filling:
  • 113.5 g (1/2 cup) vegan butter

• Two baking sheets

Nutrition: Approximate per cookie sandwich (20 sandwiches): 225 calories, 2g protein, 12g fat, 28g carbohydrates, 1g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Prep: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. Combine the Dry Ingredients: Whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
  3. Cream the Butter & Sugar: In a large bowl, cream the vegan butter and sugar together until light and fluffy. Beat in the flax egg and vanilla.
  4. Combine the Dough: Gradually mix in the dry ingredients until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
  5. Roll & Flatten: Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and place them 2 inches apart on the baking sheets. Flatten each slightly with the bottom of a glass or your palm to about 1/4 inch thick.
  6. Bake: Bake for 9-10 minutes, until the cookies look set at the edges. Cool completely on the pan.
  7. Make the Filling: For the filling, beat the vegan butter until smooth, then gradually add the powdered sugar and vanilla, beating until fluffy. Add plant milk a teaspoon at a time until the filling is smooth and spreadable.
  8. Sandwich the Cookies: Pipe or spread about 1 tablespoon of filling onto the flat side of half the cookies, then sandwich with the remaining cookies.

Name: PB&J Thumbprint Cookies

Ingredients:
• 113.5 g (1/2 cup) vegan butter
  • 120 ml (1/2 cup) creamy peanut butter
  • 100 g (1/2 cup) granulated sugar
  • 53.2 g (1/4 cup) brown sugar
  • 15 g (1) flax egg
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • 180 g (1 1/2 cups) all-purpose flour

Name: No-Bake Vegan Cheesecake Cups
Prep Time: Prep 20 min (plus 1 hr soaking and 4 hr freezing)
Common Ingredients: graham-crackers; vegan-butter; coconut-oil; maple-syrup; raw-cashews; coconut-milk; lemon; vanilla-extract; salt; mixed-berries
Ingredients:
• For the crust:
  • 100 g (1 cup) graham cracker crumbs or crushed vegan cookies
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) melted vegan butter or coconut oil
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) maple syrup
  • For the filling:
  • 205.5 g (1 1/2 cups) raw cashews
  • 80 ml (1/3 cup) full-fat coconut milk
  • 80 ml (1/3 cup) maple syrup
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) lemon juice
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) melted coconut oil
  • 4.3 g (1 tsp) vanilla extract
  • Pinch of salt
  • Fresh berries or fruit compote, for topping (optional)
Equipment:
• 6-cup muffin tin
  • Paper or silicone muffin liners
  • High-speed blender or food processor
  • Offset spatula or spoon
Nutrition: Approximate per cup (6 cups): 420 calories, 6g protein, 28g fat, 32g carbohydrates, 2g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Line the Muffin Tin: Line a 6-cup muffin tin with paper or silicone liners.
  2. Make the Crust: Mix the graham cracker crumbs, melted vegan butter, and maple syrup in a bowl until it resembles wet sand.
  3. Press the Crust: Divide the mixture among the liners, pressing firmly into an even layer at the bottom of each with the back of a spoon.
  4. Blend the Filling: In a high-speed blender, combine the soaked cashews, coconut milk, maple syrup, lemon juice, coconut oil, vanilla, and salt. Blend until completely smooth and creamy, scraping down the sides as needed.
  5. Fill the Cups: Divide the filling evenly among the cups, on top of the crusts, smoothing the tops with a spoon or offset spatula.
  6. Freeze: Freeze for at least 4 hours, or until firm.
  7. Thaw & Serve: Let sit at room temperature for 10-15 minutes before serving. Top with fresh berries or fruit compote if desired.

Name: Roasted Green Beans
Common Ingredients: green-beans-2; olive-oil; garlic; salt; black-pepper; crushed-red-pepper; lemon; vegan-parmesan; almonds
Ingredients:
• 453.6 g (1 lb) fresh green beans
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil
  • 9 g (3 cloves) garlic
  • 3 g (1/2 tsp) salt
  • 0.5 g (1/4 tsp) black pepper
  • 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes (optional)
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) lemon juice

Equipment:
• Large baking sheet
  • Parchment paper
  • Kitchen towel, for drying the beans
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (4 servings): 90 calories, 2g protein, 7g fat, 7g carbohydrates, 3g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Prep: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Trim & Dry the Beans: Trim the green beans and pat them dry with a towel — excess moisture will steam them instead of letting them roast.
  3. Season: Toss the green beans on the baking sheet with olive oil, garlic, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Spread them into a single, even layer.
  4. Roast: Roast for 18-20 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until the beans are tender and lightly charred in spots.
  5. Add the Lemon: Remove from the oven and squeeze the lemon juice over the top while still hot.
  6. Top & Serve: Top with shaved parmesan or toasted almonds if desired, and serve immediately.

Name: Mushroom Bolognese
Common Ingredients: mushrooms; portobello; olive-oil; onion; carrots; celery; garlic; tomato-paste; red-wine; vegetable-broth; tomatoes; oregano; basil; salt; black-pepper; pasta; vegan-parmesan
Ingredients:
• 453.6 g (1 lb) cremini or baby bella mushrooms
  • 226.8 g (8 oz) portobello mushrooms
  • 45 ml (3 tbsp) olive oil
  • 160 g (1 small) onion
  • 61 g (1) carrot
  • 40 g (1) celery stalk
  • 12 g (4 cloves) garlic
  • 32 g (2 tbsp) tomato paste
  • 120 ml (1/2 cup) red wine or vegetable broth
  • 793.8 g (1 (28 oz) can) crushed tomatoes
  • 1 g (1 tsp) dried oregano
  • 0.7 g (1 tsp) dried basil
  • 3 g (1/2 tsp) salt
  • 0.5 g (1/4 tsp) black pepper
  • 340.2 g (12 oz) pasta of choice
  • Fresh basil and grated parmesan, for serving (optional)
Equipment:
• Food processor (optional, for chopping mushrooms)
  • Large pot
  • Large pot, for pasta
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (4 servings, sauce and pasta): 420 calories, 13g protein, 11g fat, 68g carbohydrates, 6g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Process the Mushrooms: Pulse the mushrooms in a food processor in batches until finely chopped, resembling ground meat (or chop finely by hand).
  2. Brown the Mushrooms: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the chopped mushrooms and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release their liquid and it evaporates, leaving them browned.
  3. Sauté the Vegetables: Push the mushrooms to one side, add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, and add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
  4. Add Garlic & Tomato Paste: Add the garlic and tomato paste, stirring everything together, and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
  5. Deglaze with Wine: Pour in the wine and let it simmer for 2-3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
  6. Simmer the Sauce: Add the crushed tomatoes, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
  7. Cook the Pasta: Meanwhile, cook the pasta according to package directions in salted water. Drain, reserving a splash of pasta water.
  8. Combine & Serve: Toss the pasta with the sauce, adding a splash of pasta water if needed to loosen. Serve topped with fresh basil and parmesan if desired.

Storage: Refrigerate the sauce in an airtight container for up to 5 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water if it's thickened too much.

Name: Almond Flour Crackers
Common Ingredients: almond-flour; salt; garlic-powder; olive-oil; flax-egg
Ingredients:
• 192 g (2 cups) almond flour
  • 3 g (1/2 tsp) salt
  • 1.5 g (1/2 tsp) garlic powder
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil
  • 15 g (1) flax egg
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) water
Equipment:
• Baking sheet
  • Parchment paper (two sheets, for rolling)
  • Rolling pin
  • Knife or pizza cutter, for scoring
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (6 servings, about 8 crackers each): 190 calories, 7g protein, 16g fat, 6g carbohydrates, 3g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Prep: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Combine the Dry Ingredients: In a bowl, mix the almond flour, salt, and garlic powder if using.
  3. Add the Wet Ingredients: Add the olive oil and flax egg, and stir until a dough forms. If the dough seems dry and crumbly, add the water a teaspoon at a time until it comes together.
  4. Roll Out the Dough: Place the dough between two sheets of parchment paper and roll it out as thin and evenly as possible, about 1/8 inch thick.
  5. Score the Dough: Remove the top sheet of parchment and use a knife or pizza cutter to score the dough into cracker-sized squares. Sprinkle with flaky salt.
  6. Transfer to the Baking Sheet: Transfer the parchment with the scored dough onto the baking sheet.
  7. Bake: Bake for 12-15 minutes, until golden brown at the edges. Watch closely near the end, as almond flour browns quickly.
  8. Cool & Break: Let cool completely on the pan — the crackers will crisp up further as they cool. Break along the scored lines.

Storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week. If they soften, re-crisp in a low oven for a few minutes.

Tip: Roll the dough as thin and even as possible — uneven thickness means some crackers will burn before others are done.

Swap: Add dried herbs like rosemary or everything bagel seasoning instead of garlic powder for a different flavor.

Name: Vegetable Soup

Ingredients:
• 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil
  • 160 g (1 medium) onion
  • 122 g (2) carrots
  • 80 g (2) celery stalks
  • 9 g (3 cloves) garlic
  • 411.1 g (1 (14.5 oz) can) diced tomatoes
  • 1440 ml (6 cups) vegetable broth
  • 358 g (2 cups) chopped potatoes or 1 can white beans
  • 110 g (1 cup) green beans
  • 124 g (1 cup) chopped zucchini or yellow squash
  • 165 g (1 cup) frozen corn or peas
  • 1 g (1 tsp) dried thyme
  • 1 g (1 tsp) dried oregano
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt
  • 1 g (1/2 tsp) black pepper
  • 134 g (2 cups) chopped kale or spinach
  • Fresh parsley, for garnish (optional)
Equipment:
• Large pot or Dutch oven
  • Cutting board and knife

Nutrition: Approximate per serving (6 servings): 140 calories, 4g protein, 5g fat, 21g carbohydrates, 5g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Sauté the Aromatics: Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery, and cook for 5-6 minutes, until softened.
  2. Add the Garlic: Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
  3. Add the Vegetables & Broth: Stir in the diced tomatoes, broth, potatoes (or white beans), green beans, zucchini, corn, thyme, oregano, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.

Name: Pumpkin Peanut Butter Dog Treats
Common Ingredients: whole-wheat-flour; oat-flour; pumpkin; peanut-butter; flax-egg; oats
Ingredients:
• 300 g (2 1/2 cups) whole wheat flour or oat flour
  • 122.5 g (1/2 cup) canned pure pumpkin puree
  • 129 g (1/2 cup) natural peanut butter
  • 30 g (2) flax eggs
  • 22.5 g (1/4 cup) rolled oats
Equipment:
• Baking sheet
  • Parchment paper
  • Rolling pin
  • Cookie cutters (optional)
  • Wire cooling rack
Nutrition: Approximate per treat (24 small treats): 85 calories, 4g protein, 3g fat, 11g carbohydrates, 1g fiber. Treats should make up no more than about 10% of a dog's daily calories — check with your vet for portion guidance based on your dog's size.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat & Prep: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Mix the Wet Ingredients: In a large bowl, mix the pumpkin puree, peanut butter, and flax eggs until smooth.
  3. Add the Dry Ingredients: Add the flour and oats, and stir until a stiff dough forms. Knead briefly with your hands if needed to bring it together.
  4. Roll Out the Dough: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and roll to about 1/4-inch thickness.
  5. Cut & Arrange: Cut into shapes with a cookie cutter, or simply cut into small squares with a knife. Place on the prepared baking sheet.
  6. Bake: Bake for 20-25 minutes, until firm and lightly golden. For extra-crunchy treats, turn off the oven and let them sit inside for another 30-60 minutes to dry out further.
  7. Cool: Cool completely on a wire rack before serving or storing.

Prep: Double-check that your peanut butter is 100% xylitol-free before using it — xylitol is toxic to dogs, and some "natural" or reduced-sugar peanut butters contain it. Use plain canned pumpkin puree, not pumpkin pie filling, which contains added sugar and spices.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week, or refrigerate for up to 3 weeks. Freeze for up to 3 months.

Tip: Letting the treats sit in the turned-off oven after baking dries them out further for a crunchier texture that keeps longer.

Swap: Swap peanut butter for plain pumpkin puree only if your dog has a peanut allergy, adding a bit more if the dough seems dry.

Important: Always confirm ingredients are safe for dogs, avoid xylitol entirely, and check with your vet if your dog has any health conditions before introducing new treats.
Why These Ingredients: Pumpkin puree is gentle on a dog's digestion and adds natural sweetness without added sugar. Peanut butter (xylitol-free) makes these treats irresistible to most dogs, while oats and whole wheat flour give the dough enough structure to hold its shape and bake up firm.

Name: Classic Potato Latkes
Common Ingredients: potatoes; onion; flax-egg; all-purpose-flour; matzo-meal; salt; black-pepper; neutral-oil; apple-sauce; vegan-sour-cream
Ingredients:
• 907.2 g (2 lbs) russet potatoes
  • 160 g (1 small) onion
  • 30 g (2) flax eggs
  • 30 g (1/4 cup) all-purpose flour or matzo meal
  • 6 g (1 tsp) salt
  • 0.5 g (1/4 tsp) black pepper
  • Neutral oil, for frying (about 1/2 cup)
  • Applesauce or vegan sour cream, for serving (optional)
Equipment:
• Box grater or food processor
  • Clean kitchen towel or cheesecloth
  • Large skillet
  • Slotted spatula
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (4 servings, about 3 latkes each): 300 calories, 6g protein, 12g fat, 47g carbohydrates, 4g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Grate & Drain: Grate the potatoes and onion using a box grater or food processor. Transfer to a clean kitchen towel or cheesecloth and squeeze out as much liquid as possible over a bowl.
  2. Reserve the Starch: Let the squeezed-out liquid sit for a minute, then pour off the water on top, keeping the white potato starch that settles at the bottom. Add this starch back to the grated potato mixture.
  3. Mix the Batter: Stir in the flax eggs, flour, salt, and pepper until well combined.
  4. Heat the Oil: Heat about 1/4 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
  5. Form & Fry: Scoop about 1/4 cup of the potato mixture per latke into the pan, flattening slightly with a spatula. Fry in batches, without crowding the pan.
  6. Cook Until Crisp: Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and crisp. Adjust the heat as needed to prevent burning.
  7. Drain & Serve: Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate or wire rack to drain. Serve hot with applesauce or vegan sour cream.

Name: Creamed Spinach
Common Ingredients: spinach; vegan-butter; onion; garlic; all-purpose-flour; oat-milk; coconut-cream; vegan-parmesan; nutmeg; salt; black-pepper
Ingredients:
• 907.2 g (2 lbs) fresh spinach
  • 3 tbsp vegan butter
  • 80 g (1/2 small) onion
  • 6 g (2 cloves) garlic
  • 16 g (2 tbsp) all-purpose flour
  • 240 ml (1 cup) unsweetened oat milk
  • 60 ml (1/4 cup) full-fat coconut cream
  • 1/4 cup grated vegan parmesan
  • 0.6 g (1/4 tsp) ground nutmeg
  • 3 g (1/2 tsp) salt
  • 0.5 g (1/4 tsp) black pepper
Equipment:
• Large pot
  • Whisk
  • Colander, for draining spinach
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (4 servings): 220 calories, 8g protein, 17g fat, 11g carbohydrates, 4g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Wilt the Spinach: If using fresh spinach, wilt it in batches in a large pot over medium heat with just the water clinging to the leaves, about 2-3 minutes per batch. Drain well, cool slightly, and squeeze out excess liquid, then roughly chop. If using frozen spinach, squeeze it very dry.
  2. Sauté the Onion: In the same pot, melt the vegan butter over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3-4 minutes, until softened.
  3. Add the Garlic: Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
  4. Make the Roux: Sprinkle the flour over the onion and garlic, stirring constantly, and cook for 1 minute to remove the raw flour taste.
  5. Build the Sauce: Gradually whisk in the oat milk and coconut cream, and cook, stirring frequently, for 3-4 minutes, until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
  6. Season: Stir in the vegan parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until melted through.
  7. Add the Spinach: Fold in the chopped spinach and cook for 2-3 minutes, until heated through and well coated in the sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.

Name: Vegan Pie Crust
Common Ingredients: all-purpose-flour; salt; sugar; vegan-butter; apple-cider-vinegar
Ingredients:
• 150 g (1 1/4 cups) all-purpose flour
  • 3 g (1/2 tsp) salt
  • 4.2 g (1 tsp) granulated sugar
  • 113.5 g (1/2 cup) vegan butter
  • 4-6 tbsp ice water
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) apple cider vinegar
Equipment:
• Large mixing bowl
  • Pastry cutter or fork
  • Plastic wrap
  • Rolling pin
  • 9-inch pie dish
Nutrition: Approximate per serving (8 servings, for one 9-inch crust): 150 calories, 2g protein, 9g fat, 15g carbohydrates, 1g fiber.
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Combine the Dry Ingredients: Whisk together the flour, salt, and sugar (if using) in a large bowl.
  2. Cut in the Butter: Add the cold cubed vegan butter and cut it into the flour using a pastry cutter or your fingers, until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter remaining.
  3. Add the Liquid: Mix the ice water and apple cider vinegar together. Drizzle 4 tablespoons over the flour mixture, tossing gently with a fork.
  4. Bring the Dough Together: Add more water, a tablespoon at a time, just until the dough comes together when pressed — it should not be sticky or wet.
  5. Chill the Dough: Turn the dough out, shape into a disc, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or up to 2 days.
  6. Roll Out: When ready to use, let the dough sit at room temperature for 5-10 minutes to soften slightly, then roll out on a lightly floured surface to about 1/8-inch thickness.
  7. Transfer to the Pie Dish: Transfer to a pie dish, trim and crimp the edges, and use as directed in your pie recipe.

Storage: Refrigerate unbaked dough, well wrapped, for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before rolling.

Tip: Handle the dough as little as possible — overworking it melts the butter and develops the gluten too much, leading to a tough crust instead of a flaky one.

Swap: Leave out the sugar entirely for savory pies like pot pie or quiche.

Name: Enchiladas

Ingredients:
• 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil
  • 160 g (1 small) onion
  • 119 g (1) bell pepper
  • 6 g (2 cloves) garlic
  • 850.5 g (2 cans (15 oz each)) black beans
  • 165 g (1 cup) corn kernels
  • 2 g (1 tsp) ground cumin
  • 2.5 g (1 tsp) chili powder
  • 3 g (1/2 tsp) salt
  • 12 corn or flour tortillas
  • 720 ml (3 cups) red or green enchilada sauce

  • Chopped cilantro, sliced jalapeno, vegan sour cream, or avocado, for serving (optional)

1. Preheat & Prep the Dish: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Spread about 1/2 cup of enchilada sauce in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish.
  2. Sauté the Vegetables: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper, and cook for 4-5 minutes, until softened.

  4. Warm the Tortillas: Warm the tortillas briefly (in the microwave or a dry skillet) so they roll without cracking.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Juice the lemons: Squeeze fresh lemons until you have 750 ml (3 cups) of juice, straining out seeds and pulp if desired.
  2. Fill the trays: Pour the juice into ice cube trays, filling each compartment about 3/4 full to leave room for expansion.
  3. Freeze: Freeze until solid, at least 4 hours or overnight.
  4. Transfer and store: Pop the frozen cubes out of the trays and transfer to a freezer-safe bag or airtight container, labeled with the date.
  5. Use as needed: Thaw a cube at room temperature for a few minutes, or drop directly into hot dishes, dressings, or drinks.

Prep:
Use fresh, ripe lemons — riper lemons yield more juice and better flavor than firm, underripe ones.

Strain out seeds first — removing seeds and pulp before freezing makes the cubes easier to use directly in recipes later.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Common Mistakes: Overfilling the trays — juice expands as it freezes, so leaving a little headroom prevents overflow and cracked trays.

Storage: Keeps in the freezer for up to 6 months. Once frozen solid, transfer out of the trays into a bag to free up the trays for reuse.

Swaps: Lime juice works exactly the same way, and orange juice can be frozen for cooking and baking too. Freeze lemon zest separately in small portions for a flavor boost without needing a fresh lemon on hand.

Tips: One standard ice cube is roughly 15-30 ml (1-2 tbsp) of juice, making it easy to swap in for a fresh lemon in recipes without any guesswork. Silicone trays make popping the frozen cubes out much easier than rigid plastic ones.
Why These Ingredients: Fresh lemon juice — the only ingredient needed. Freezing it in small portions means you always have exactly the amount you need on hand, without letting whole lemons go to waste.

Name: Homemade Fruit and Vegetable Wash

  3. Scrub: Gently scrub firmer produce like potatoes, apples, or cucumbers with a soft brush or your hands.

Name: Mediterranean Orzo Salad
Ingredients:
• 300 g (1 1/2 cups) orzo pasta
  • 200 g (1 1/3 cups) cherry tomatoes
  • 200 g (1) English cucumber
  • 55 g (1/2) red onion
  • 100 g (1/2 cup) kalamata olives
  • 100 g (1/2 cup) vegan feta
  • 30 g (1/2 cup) fresh parsley
  • 15 g (1/4 cup) fresh mint or basil
  • 60 ml (1/4 cup) olive oil
  • 30 ml (2 tbsp) lemon juice
  • 15 ml (1 tbsp) red wine vinegar
  • 3 g (1 clove) garlic

Equipment:
• Large pot

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Cook the orzo: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the orzo according to package directions until al dente, about 8-9 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking and cool completely.
  2. Make the dressing: Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
  3. Combine the salad: In a large bowl, combine the cooled orzo, tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, olives, and herbs.
  4. Dress and toss: Pour the dressing over the salad and toss well to coat.
  5. Add the feta: Gently fold in the vegan feta, taking care not to break it up too much.
  6. Chill and serve: Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors meld, or serve immediately at room temperature.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Press the tofu: Press the tofu for at least 15 minutes to remove excess moisture, then slice into very thin rounds or half-moons (about 3mm thick).
  2. Make the marinade: Whisk together the tomato paste, olive oil, soy sauce, maple syrup, vinegar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, fennel seeds, oregano, red pepper flakes, black pepper, and cayenne (if using) in a bowl.

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Salt and drain the zucchini: Slice zucchini lengthwise into thin strips. Lay on paper towels, sprinkle with salt, and let sit for 20-30 minutes to draw out moisture. Pat dry thoroughly.
  2. Make the tofu ricotta: In a bowl, mash the tofu with lemon juice, nutritional yeast, olive oil, garlic, basil, oregano, and salt until it resembles ricotta cheese.

Instruction Rich Text:

  3. Thicken (optional): For an extra-thick compote, stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer for 1-2 more minutes until glossy and thickened.

Name: Pumpkin Pie (Vegan)
Ingredients:
• 1 (9-inch) vegan pie crust, unbaked
  • 425 g (15 oz) canned pumpkin puree
  • 200 g (1 cup) full-fat coconut milk
  • 150 g (3/4 cup) brown sugar
  • 40 g (3 tbsp) cornstarch
  • 2 tsp pumpkin pie spice (or 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ginger, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 1/4 tsp cloves)
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 5 ml (1 tsp) vanilla extract
Equipment:
• 9-inch pie dish
  • Mixing bowl
  • Whisk
  • Pie weights or dried beans
Nutrition:

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat and prep the crust: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie dish, crimp the edges, and chill for 15 minutes.
  2. Blind bake: Line the crust with parchment paper and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake for 10 minutes, remove the weights and parchment, then bake for 5 more minutes. Let cool slightly.
  3. Make the filling: Whisk together the pumpkin puree, coconut milk, brown sugar, cornstarch, pumpkin pie spice, salt, and vanilla until completely smooth.
  4. Fill and bake: Reduce the oven to 350°F (175°C). Pour the filling into the crust and bake for 45-50 minutes, until the center is just set with a slight jiggle.
  5. Cool and chill: Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours before slicing.

Common Mistakes: Overbaking — the filling should still jiggle slightly in the center when it comes out of the oven; it firms up fully as it cools and chills.

Name: Pecan Pie (Vegan)

Instruction Rich Text:
1. Preheat and prep the crust: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Fit the pie crust into a 9-inch pie dish and crimp the edges.
  2. Toast the pecans: Spread the pecans on a baking sheet and toast for 6-8 minutes, until fragrant. Set aside to cool.

Name: Classic Marinara Sauce
Features: gluten-free; soy-free; nut-free; freezer-friendly; meal-prep-friendly; leftover-friendly
Ingredients:
• 3 tbsp olive oil
  • 4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
  • 28 oz canned crushed tomatoes
  • 1 tsp dried oregano
  • 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
  • 3/4 tsp salt, plus more to taste
  • 1 tsp sugar
  • 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, torn
  • 1/4 tsp black pepper
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Warm the garlic: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add 4 sliced garlic cloves and cook, stirring, until fragrant and just golden at the edges — about 1–2 minutes. Do not let it brown.
  2. Add the tomatoes: Pour in 28 oz canned crushed tomatoes. Stir in 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, 3/4 tsp salt, and 1 tsp sugar.
  3. Simmer: Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for about 25 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
  4. Finish: Remove from heat. Stir in 1/4 cup torn fresh basil and season with 1/4 tsp black pepper and extra salt to taste.
  5. Serve: Toss with hot pasta, use on pizza, or spoon over your favorite dish. Store leftovers in the fridge for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
Prep: Slice the garlic thinly and have it ready before you start — it cooks quickly and can go from golden to burnt in seconds once the pan is hot.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,:
Storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days, or freeze in portions for up to 3 months.

Swap: Whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand, work well in place of crushed tomatoes for a chunkier texture.

Tip: For a smoother sauce, blend with an immersion blender before adding the basil.
Why These Ingredients: A few ingredients do most of the work in this recipe. The olive oil brings fruity depth and helps carry the other flavors. The canned crushed tomatoes adds bright acidity and juicy body. The garlic builds a savory, aromatic base. The fresh basil adds a fresh, peppery herbal note.

Name: Pickled Daikon and Carrots
Ingredients:
• 1 medium daikon radish, julienned
  • 2 large carrots, julienned
  • 1 tsp fine sea salt
  • 1 cup water
  • 1 cup rice vinegar (or distilled white vinegar)
  • 1/4 cup granulated sugar
Instruction Rich Text:
1. Salt the Vegetables: Place the julienned daikon and carrots in a bowl, sprinkle with the 1 tsp fine sea salt, and toss well. Let sit for 10 minutes, then squeeze out any excess liquid.
  2. Make the Brine: In a separate bowl or jar, combine the 1 cup water, 1 cup rice vinegar, and 1/4 cup granulated sugar. Stir until the sugar fully dissolves.
  3. Pack the Jar: Pack the daikon and carrots into a clean jar, then pour the vinegar mixture over them until fully submerged.
  4. Rest: Let the jar sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before using, or refrigerate for a more mellow flavor.
  5. Store: Store in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.
Common Mistakes, Notes, Storage, Swaps,: Swap rice vinegar for apple cider vinegar for a slightly different tang. For a spicier version, add a few slices of fresh chili to the jar. These pickles are a classic topping for banh mi sandwiches, but they're just as good on rice bowls, tacos, or alongside grilled tofu.
